jobs.title: Assistant Professor
jobs.description:
Job Posting:
JR101910 Assistant Professor (Open)
Department:
Bachelor of Science in Nursing, PM
Position Type:
Regular
Open Date:
10-30-2026
Close Date:
11-20-2026
$100,000.00 Annually
Job Description:
The Assistant Professor is responsible for teaching in the
classroom, clinical/campus laboratory clinical sites and clinical
seminars; planning, implementing, and evaluating nursing curriculum
as a member of the nursing teaching team’ and providing academic
counseling and guidance to nursing students.
Responsibilities:
Teaching in the classroom, clinical/campus laboratory clinical
sites and clinical seminars; Planning, implementing and evaluating
nursing curriculum as a member of the nursing teaching team.
Coordinating with community health agencies utilized for
clinical experiences and maintaining effective relations with them;
Planning, supervising and evaluating learning experiences for
students in the clinical area; scheduling conferences with
individual students regarding progress.
Participating in all School of Nursing and nursing course team
planning meetings and selected subcommittee within School of
Nursing and College of Health Professions; Participating actively
in University, College, School and Community service and
Activities.
Maintaining own professional growth and remains current in
nursing practice; Assisting in preparation for nursing
accreditation visits.; Day, evening and weekend classes and
clinical as applicable.
Providing academic counseling and guidance to nursing students;
Holding at least four post office hours per week.
Minimum Qualifications:
EDUCATION
Minimally a Master of Science in Nursing degree
required.
Doctoral Degree in Nursing or a health-related field from an
accredited institution preferred.
EXPERIENCE
Demonstrated clinical experience in medical-surgical nursing
and currently at least one area of specialty in pediatric,
maternal-child, critical care, and psychiatric/mental health or
community clinical areas.
Recent classroom and clinical teaching experience in a
college-level nursing program.
Ability to meet challenges of adult students with diverse
background.
Holds current license as a Registered Nurse in the State of
Maryland other verifiable state.
Preference will be given to candidates who have experience and
an appreciation for and are committed to working in a global,
multicultural academic setting; Preference will be given to
candidates who have experience with the integration of technology
and alternative delivery systems of instruction in
teaching-learning process.
KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES
Must be able to independently manage multiple tasks and set
priorities.
Possess strong oral/written communication, presentation, and
interpersonal skills.
Ability to meet challenges of adult students with diverse
background.
Integration of technology and alternative delivery systems of
instruction in teaching-learning process.
Additional Job Information:
BENEFITS SUMMARY
Coppin State University offers a competitive benefits package to
include health insurance options (medical, dental, vision), life
and disability insurance, retirement plan contributions, as well as
paid leave and federal holidays for all regular employees. Please
see the link below to view the benefits that Coppin State
University has to offer.
https://www.coppin.edu/benefits
E-VERIFY STATEMENT
This agency participates in the E-Verify system for verification of
citizenship and employment authorization.
Coppin State University is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action
employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for
employment without regard to race, creed, color, ethnicity,
national origin, ancestry, religion, gender, sexual orientation,
gender identity, genetic information, marital status, pregnancy,
age, disability status or veteran status. View the EEOC Know Your Rights poster for more
information regarding your rights under the law.
If you experience difficulties utilizing the online application
system or you require reasonable accommodations during any part of
the pre-employment process, please contact Human Resources at
AskHR@coppin.edu. Please note that only inquiries regarding a
request for reasonable accommodation or system issues will be
responded to when contacting this e-mail account. Reasonable
accommodation will be considered on a case-by-case basis.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor (OTD)
jobs.description:
Description
The College of Health and Human Sciences at Southern Illinois
University Carbondale is seeking qualified applicants for one
Assistant Professor position within the entry-level Occupational
Therapy Doctorate (OTD) hybrid weekend program in the School of
Health Sciences beginning August 10, 2027. This is a continuing,
nine-month, tenure-track position. Depending on course
availability, summer appointments may be offered.
This position is represented by SIU Carbondale Faculty
Association/IEA-NEA. For more information regarding salary and
other details please
visit:https://laborrelations.siu.edu/labor-contracts.
Salary is competitive and commensurate with qualifications and
experience, while also considering internal equity.
Examples of Duties
Provide direct classroom/laboratory/clinical instruction and
student engagement as assigned. Teach via online and traditional
delivery methods. Provide indirect teaching, such as: student
selection, student advisement, recruitment, and retention for the
OTD program. Please note: the SIU OTD program is a hybrid, weekend
program that requires faculty to teach on campus on selected
weekends.
Conduct scholarly research and produce creative activities
consistent with School of Health Sciences expectations within the
occupational therapy arena.
Participate in professional practice, seminars, or workshops
necessary to maintain up-to-date skills in the occupational therapy
profession.
Maintain a teaching, research, and service assignment
consistent with the workload of a tenure-track faculty position
within the College of Health and Human Sciences.
Comply with the spirit and intent of the University, College,
and School Operating Papers.
Contribute to program curriculum development processes.
Evaluate student performance, maintain accurate records of
student progress, and submit final grade rosters in accordance with
program/school/college and university policy.
Participate in capstone committees and facilitate student
research participation.
Engage in other duties as determined by the Director of the
School of Health Sciences
Qualifications
Minimum Qualifications:
An earned doctoral degree in occupational therapy or a related
field (e.g., PhD, ScD, OTD, or other relevant professional
doctorate) is required by the position’s start date. Candidates
whose doctoral degree is in a field other than occupational therapy
must also hold a bachelor’s or master’s degree in occupational
therapy.
A minimum of 3 years of full-time academic appointment with
teaching responsibilities at the post-secondary education
level.
A minimum of one year of full-time occupational therapy
clinical practice experience.
Certified by the Board of Certification as an Occupational
Therapist and licensed or eligible for licensure as an Occupational
Therapist in the state of Illinois by the start date.
Applicants for the rank of Assistant Professor must demonstrate
a record of potential for scholarly productivity.
Preferred Qualifications:
History of established research agenda and scholarly
achievement in occupational therapy.
Involvement in scholarly research and creative activities
within the occupational therapy arena.
Demonstrates a working knowledge of educational theory and
methodology.
Demonstrates an understanding of the current ACOTE
Standards.
Excellent oral and written communication skills, organizational
and technology skills.
Knowledge of OT program development and accreditation
processes.
Required Documents: Please submit a letter of application,
CV/resume, professional licenses, unofficial transcripts, and three
references.
Contact: Valerie Boyer, valboyer@siu.edu
Supplemental Information
Southern Illinois University Carbondale is a Carnegie Doctoral
Research University. Promising new faculty in CHHS are offered
competitive startup packages, including graduate/undergraduate
assistant support, course releases, and summer salary designed to
jumpstart research scholarship.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Art and Visual Culture
jobs.description:
Job Details
Located in Lewiston, Maine, Bates is internationally recognized as
a leading liberal arts college. We are proud to offer a highly
personalized education that centers on deep and sustained
interactions among students, faculty, and community. We are
engaging the forces — intellectual trends, demographic changes, and
technology — that are transforming higher education and the world
into which our students graduate.
The Department
of Art and Visual Culture (AVC) at Bates College invites
applications for a full-time, tenure-track position as Assistant
Professor in Studio Art with expertise in Photography and one or
several areas of foundational studies, such as 2-D design, digital
media foundations, color, and 3-D spatial dynamics. The position
will begin in July 2027. We seek an outstanding practicing artist
with a strong commitment to undergraduate teaching and mentorship.
Candidates will demonstrate a strong understanding of photographic
history, theory, and contemporary critical discourse, as well as
technical fluency across traditional analog, digital, and hybrid
photographic practices. The ability to teach digital and
traditional darkroom photography, including black-and-white film
photography and darkroom printing, is required. Candidates must
also have the knowledge and experience necessary to oversee,
maintain, and manage digital and darkroom photographic studios,
including equipment, materials, chemical processes, and safety
protocols.
The Art and Visual Culture Department offers courses in studio
practice and in the study of the intersecting categories of art,
architecture, and visual and material culture, from the distant
past to the present. The major offers two tracks: one in history
and criticism; the other, in studio art. The position carries a
standard five-course annual teaching load. Responsibilities include
contributing to curriculum development efforts, teaching courses in
photography and interdisciplinary studio courses (including
foundations and senior thesis), teaching in the general education
curriculum, and advising students.
Bates College is a residential liberal arts college located in
Lewiston, Maine. Faculty scholarship and creative work at Bates are
robustly supported by start-up packages, a paid pre-tenure leave,
support for post-tenure sabbaticals, internal grants, professional
travel funding, and a well-staffed external
grants office .
Community-engaged learning —with community partnerships
facilitated by the
Harward Center for
Community Partnerships —and study abroad are both
broadly encouraged and institutionally supported. Pedagogical
development and innovation is further buttressed by our highly
engaged
Center
for Inclusive Teaching and Learning . Educational access and
racial justice are central to Bates’ history and mission and
our
faculty-led initiatives reflect this commitment .
An MFA degree is required.
Review of applications will begin on January 4th and continue until
the position is filled.
Successful candidates will demonstrate potential to develop
inclusive and evidence-based methods of teaching, maintain an
active program of scholarship or creative work, and participate in
the life and governance of the College as described in Article II
of the Bates College Faculty
Handbook .
The anticipated salary range for this position is $87,000 to
$91,000, commensurate with rank, experience, qualifications, and
other relevant factors.
Required application materials include:
● Cover letter
● Curriculum vitae
● Teaching statement
● Artist Statement
● Creative work sample: a PDF up to 20 images - time based media up
to 5 min. Include the following information
for each piece: Title, Medium, size, and year of creation.
● A PDF up to 5 pages including a range of images of student work.
Include context of class and prompt of the
assignments.
Letters of recommendation will be requested only for candidates
selected to move forward after the initial review. Employment is
contingent upon successful completion of a background check and
verification of degree.
We seek candidates who are committed to supporting the success of
all students. Applicants are encouraged to describe relevant
preparation, experience, or plans for creating an inclusive
learning environment.
Bates College is committed to equal opportunity and to providing an
educational and work environment free from discrimination. The
college prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color,
national or ethnic origin, religion, sex, sexual orientation,
gender identity or gender expression, age, disability, genetic
information, veteran status, and other legally protected statuses
in the recruitment and admission of its students, in the
administration of its education policies and programs, or in the
recruitment of its faculty and staff. Bates College adheres to all
applicable state and federal equal opportunity laws and
regulations. All college faculty, staff, students, contractors,
visitors, and volunteers are responsible for understanding and
complying with the Non-Discrimination Policy.
Inquiries concerning the college’s policies, compliance with
applicable laws, statutes, and regulations (such as Title VII,
Title IX, and ADA/Section 504), and complaints may be directed to
the Title IX Officer, Gwen Lexow at 207-786-6445 or
titleix@bates.edu.

jobs.title: Professional Assistant Professor - Department of Curriculum and Instruction, College of Education
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Title
Professional Assistant Professor - Department of Curriculum and
Instruction, College of Education
Agency
Tarleton State University
Department
Curriculum & Instruction
Proposed Minimum Salary
Commensurate
Job Location
Fort Worth, Texas
Job Type
Faculty
Job Description
Tarleton State University, a distinguished Doctoral National
Comprehensive University, invites applications for the position of
Professional Assistant Professor in the Department of
Curriculum and Instruction, College of Education. As part of a
vibrant academic community dedicated to excellence in teaching,
research, and service, this role offers the opportunity to
contribute meaningfully to a university that values innovation,
collaboration, and inclusive growth. Join us in advancing knowledge
and transforming lives—on campus and beyond. Tarleton State
University continues to grow its impact across Texas, with four
distinct campuses located in Stephenville, Fort Worth,
RELLIS-Bryan and Waco, along with a robust online
community that extends our reach even further.
At the heart of it all is Stephenville, where Tarleton State
offers a dynamic environment for faculty and staff. From a lively
live music scene and numerous local festivals to rich traditions
rooted in the surrounding community, Stephenville provides a
vibrant and welcoming atmosphere.
No matter where you're located—on campus or online—you are part of
a mission that transforms lives and makes a
difference across the state of Texas and beyond.
________________________________________________________________________
Important Immigration Information:
A Presidential proclamation issued on September 19, 2025, imposes a
$100,000 fee on new H-1B petitions filed after September 21, 2025.
Please be advised that Tarleton State University will NOT pay this
fee. Therefore, if you need immigration sponsorship for your
employment, we recommend that you consult with your private
immigration counsel at your own expense to ascertain whether your
current immigration status would make a potential offer of
employment from Tarleton State University subject to this
fee.
In addition, on January 27, 2026, Texas Governor Abbot issued a
moratorium on the filing of any new H-1B unless approved by the
Texas Workforce Commission. Accordingly, if you will now or in the
future require sponsorship for employment visa status this
moratorium may affect our ability to employ you should you be
selected as the final candidate.
________________________________________________________________________
This is a 9-month, non-tenure-track faculty position based on
Tarleton's Fort Worth, Texas campus, with additional instruction
delivered online. Summer appointment is dependent upon need and
funding availability. Work hours: Mon-Fri; 8 AM-5 PM or as work and
teaching requirements indicate. May be assigned to teach at various
campus locations or through approved instructional modalities, as
determined by the institution based on operational needs. Serves as
a Campus Security Authority (CSA).
The successful candidate will demonstrate excellence and innovation
in teaching while contributing to undergraduate and graduate
instruction in educator preparation. The position requires a strong
commitment to high-quality classroom and online instruction,
curriculum development, academic mentorship, and program-level
assessment.
This position is not eligible for Visa sponsorship.
Essential Duties and Responsibilities
100% Teaching and Service:
Plan, prepare, and deliver undergraduate and graduate courses
across face-to-face, hybrid, and online modalities, which may
include general education core curriculum.
Carry a full instructional load across departmental programs,
with sections potentially scheduled at multiple campus locations or
through approved instructional modalities.
Develop course syllabi, select instructional materials, and
design assessments aligned to Texas Educator Standards and program
certification requirements.
Assess student performance, provide timely feedback, and
evaluate student learning outcomes to inform teaching practices and
curriculum improvements.
Engage students in active learning, foster critical thinking,
and provide opportunities for discussion, collaboration, and
hands-on learning.
Provide academic support and guidance through office hours,
feedback on assignments, advising, and mentoring.
Adhere to university policies, academic integrity standards,
and accreditation and accountability requirements, including
SACSCOC and Texas Education Agency reporting expectations.
Incorporate innovative teaching methods, technologies, and
pedagogical approaches to enhance student learning and
engagement.
Contribute course-level assessment data to program review and
continuous improvement.
Collaborate with departmental faculty and university staff to
coordinate course offerings, share resources, and maintain
curricular consistency across sections and campuses.
Participate in ongoing professional development that
strengthens teaching effectiveness and maintains currency in Texas
certification requirements and evidence-based instructional
practice.
Minimum Requirements
Required Education and Experience:
Earned doctorate in Curriculum and Instruction, Education, or a
closely related field from an accredited university by the date of
appointment. ABD candidates may be considered with a documented
completion timeline.
A minimum of three years of successful PK-12 teaching
experience.
Valid or previously held teacher certification.
Excellent written and oral communication skills in
English.
Required Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities:
Knowledge and understanding of disciplinary subject matter at a
level adequate for graduate-level instruction.
Written and oral communication skills sufficient to conduct
effective teaching activities.
Ability to interact with students, staff, and faculty in a
professional, collegial, and collaborative manner.
Preferred Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
University-level teaching experience in educator
preparation.
Expertise in one or more of the following: literacy and reading
instruction, ESL and bilingual education, special education, and
science methods.
Experience with online and hybrid course design and learning
management systems.
Familiarity with Texas educator certification requirements and
TExES examination preparation.
Demonstrated effectiveness teaching across multiple modalities
and locations.
Evidence of sustained excellence in undergraduate and graduate
teaching.
***Compensation will be competitive and commensurate with
experience***
Application Procedure:
During the application process applicants have one opportunity to
enter the requested information, upload documents, and Submit the
application. Applicants will not be able to make changes or add
additional documents once the application materials have been
submitted via the "Submit" action.
Employment applications must include (required):
Completed online application
Cover Letter / Letter of Interest addressing
qualifications
Curriculum Vitae or Resume
At least 3 current professional references and their full
contact information
Unofficial transcripts
Applicants with degrees earned outside the United States must
submit transcripts translated into English, along with an official
credential evaluation from a recognized service.
Philosophy Statement related to Teaching
Applications received by Tarleton State University must have all
job application data entered. Failure to provide all job
application data could result in an invalid submission and a
rejected application. “See resume” is not an acceptable entry in
the job application. Incomplete applications will not be
considered.
Review of applications will begin immediately and continue until
the position is filled. Anticipated start date Spring
2027.
Official transcripts must be received directly from each
degree‐granting institution prior to a letter of appointment being
issued.
All positions are security-sensitive. Applicants are subject to a
criminal history investigation, and employment is contingent upon
the institution’s verification of credentials and/or other
information required by the institution’s procedures, including the
completion of the criminal history check.
Equal Opportunity/Veterans/Disability Employer.

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor of Global Production and Trade Governance
jobs.description:
Job Details
Posting Details
Position Details
Title
Assistant/Associate Professor of Global Production and Trade
Governance
Appointment Status
Tenure Track
Department
IU Bloomington International Studies
Location
Bloomington
Position Summary
The Department of International Studies at Indiana University’s
Hamilton Lugar School of Global and International Studies invites
applications for an Assistant/Associate Professor, tenure-track
faculty position in Global Production and Trade Governance
beginning August 1, 2027.
We seek a scholar whose research and teaching examine the
governance, law, and political economy of global production
systems. Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, global
value chains, international trade and investment politics, the
regulation of transnational production networks, foreign direct
investment, and the implications of global economic governance for
development and inequality.
The successful candidate will contribute to the department’s
growing strengths in international political economy and global
governance while supporting existing undergraduate and graduate
programs, including the International Financial Governance, Trade,
and Development degree and the finance and trade concentration
within the Master of International Affairs ( MIA ) program. The
position reflects rising student and institutional interest in
issues surrounding globalization, economic interdependence,
financial governance, and the evolving rules and institutions that
shape international economic relations.
We welcome applications from candidates employing diverse
disciplinary and methodological approaches. Candidates should
demonstrate a strong research agenda, evidence of or potential for
excellence in teaching, and a commitment to interdisciplinary
engagement within an international studies environment.
Responsibilities include maintaining an active research program,
teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in areas related to
global production and trade governance, mentoring students, and
contributing to departmental and university service.
Applicants seeking appointment at associate rank with tenure will
be required to undergo a review of appropriateness for hire with
tenure at Indiana University as a part of the recruitment process.
Applicants seeking appointment at assistant rank must have a
doctoral degree in hand by August 1, 2027.
Applicants should submit a letter of application, curriculum vitae,
research statement, teaching statement, a sample course syllabus,
writing sample, and contact information for three references.
Review of applications will begin following a priority deadline of
September 11, 2026, with all applications received by that date
being guaranteed full consideration. Review of applications will
continue until the position is filled.
Interested candidates should review the application requirements
and submit their materials via the PeopleAdmin applicant portal at:
https://indiana.peopleadmin.com/postings/33720
Basic Qualifications
Ph.D. in International Studies, Political Science, Political
Economy, Economics, Law, Geography, Sociology, or a related field
by the time of appointment; Record of scholarly achievement
commensurate with appointed rank; evidence of teaching excellence
or strong potential for effective teaching
Department Contact for Questions
Inquiries regarding the position, the Department of International
Studies, and the Hamilton Lugar School of Global and International
Studies may be directed to the chair of the search committee, Dr.
Sarah Bauerle Danzman at sbauerle@iu.edu . Questions
regarding technical aspects of the application process may be
directed to Mr. Zac Muller, Hamilton Lugar School Assistant
Director of Faculty Relations, at zmuller@iu.edu .
Additional Qualifications
For applicants seeking appointment with tenure:
Before a conditional offer of employment with tenure is finalized,
candidates will be asked to disclose any pending investigations or
previous findings of sexual or professional misconduct. They will
also be required to authorize an inquiry by Indiana University
Bloomington with all current and former employers along these
lines. The relevance of information disclosed or ascertained in the
context of this process to a candidate’s eligibility for hire will
be evaluated by Indiana University Bloomington on a case-by-case
basis. Applicants should be aware, however, that Indiana University
Bloomington takes the matters of sexual and professional misconduct
very seriously.
Salary and Rank
Special Instructions
Indiana University is an equal opportunity employer and
provider of ADA services, and prohibits discrimination in
hiring.
See Indiana University Notice of Non-Discrimination here
which includes contact information
For Best Consideration Date
09/11/2026
Expected Start Date
08/01/2027
Posting Number
IU-101601-2026

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Crime Studies (Corrections and Reentry)
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Description:
Contribute as both a teacher and scholar committed to understanding
the experiences of justice-involved individuals, correctional
institutions, and pathways to successful community reintegration as
an Assistant Professor of Crime Studies, specializing in
Corrections and Reentry . In this role, you will contribute to
undergraduate instruction and the online M.A. in Crime, Justice,
and Community while developing a productive scholarly agenda and
participating in university and professional service.
As a tenure-track Assistant Professor at the State University of
New York (SUNY) Oneonta, you will benefit from a 10-month
academic-year schedule that includes a two-month period of
non-obligation. SUNY Oneonta has a standard teaching load of 21
semester hours per academic year, but the department is currently
operating on a reduced teaching load of 18 semester hours per
academic year. This full-time position reports to the Chair of the
Department of Sociology, Human Services, and Crime Studies.
The Department of Sociology, Human Services, and Crime Studies
brings together interdisciplinary perspectives on social
institutions, inequality, community well-being, and justice. Our
programs connect sociological inquiry with the practical challenges
facing communities, human service organizations, and criminal
justice systems. The growing online M.A. in Crime, Justice, and
Community emphasizes prevention, social equity, restorative
approaches, and community-centered responses to crime.
To learn more about the University, please visit https://suny.oneonta.edu/ and https://suny.oneonta.edu/sociology-human-services-and-crime-studies
.
Duties May Include:
Teaching undergraduate and graduate courses in corrections,
prisoner reentry, rehabilitation, and related areas of crime and
justice.
Contributing to the online M.A. in Crime, Justice, and
Community, including asynchronous course delivery.
Maintaining an active scholarly research and publication
agenda.
Advising and mentoring undergraduate and graduate
students.
Supervising student research or applied projects as
appropriate.
Participating in curriculum development, assessment, department
governance, and university service.
Cultivating professional or community partnerships relevant to
corrections and reentry.
Salary: $64,890. SUNY Oneonta is a Public Service Loan
Forgiveness qualifying employer. Information on SUNY's
comprehensive benefits offerings can be found at https://www.suny.edu/benefits . Visa sponsorship is
not available for this position.
Requirements:
Required Qualifications:
Ph.D. in Criminology, Criminal Justice, Sociology, or a closely
related discipline by the start of employment (ABD considered;
official confirmation of degree conferral by issuing institution by
start of employment).
Scholarly specialization in corrections, incarceration,
prisoner reentry, or closely related topics, as evidenced by
graduate training, research, or professional scholarship.
Ability to teach college-level courses in crime and justice, as
demonstrated through teaching experience, training, or submitted
teaching materials.
Additional Qualifications:
College-level teaching experience in corrections, reentry, or
related subjects.
Record of scholarly publications or presentations in relevant
areas.
Experience with online asynchronous teaching.
Experience mentoring undergraduate or graduate students.
Experience conducting applied, community-engaged, or
policy-relevant research.
Preferred Qualifications:
Research or teaching expertise in community reintegration,
desistance, restorative justice, rehabilitation, or the social
inequalities associated with incarceration.
Experience working collaboratively with correctional agencies,
reentry providers, nonprofit organizations, or affected
communities.
Experience developing graduate curriculum or supervising
graduate research.
Potential to secure external research support.
Experience in teaching, mentoring, research, or service with
diverse and/or multicultural populations.
Additional Information:
SUNY Oneonta enrolls about 5,500 students who pursue bachelor's or
master's degrees or certificates in one of 70-plus academic
programs. Known as an exemplary residential campus that values
inclusion, service and sustainability, SUNY Oneonta is a nurturing
community where students grow intellectually, thrive socially, and
live purposefully.
The university is located in the City of Oneonta, nestled in the
northern foothills of the Catskill Mountains about a four-hour
drive from New York City, Boston, and Philadelphia. With a
population just shy of 14,000, Oneonta is one of the 20 Most
Picturesque Small Towns in America, according to Microsoft News.
The natural beauty of the region is breathtaking year-round. Each
season offers outdoor activities such as hiking, biking, boating,
swimming, and skiing. Employees give SUNY Oneonta high marks for
work/life balance, management, and culture. The university's
indeed.com rating is 4.4, with one recent review noting that the
people are what make SUNY Oneonta so special.
SUNY Oneonta values a diverse university community. Please visit
our website on diversity at: https://suny.oneonta.edu/diversity . Moreover, the
university is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer.
Women, persons of color, persons with disabilities, and protected
veterans are encouraged to apply. "At SUNY Oneonta, we believe
that diversity is an asset and a source of strength that energizes
our collective growth and innovation." - President Alberto
Cardelle.
Application Instructions:
To apply online go to: http://oneonta.interviewexchange.com/candapply.jsp?JOBID=206285
. Please upload a letter of interest addressing the position and
qualifications; curriculum vitae; statement of teaching philosophy
and interests; statement of research interests and agenda; and
unofficial graduate transcripts. Please provide contact information
for three references; instructions for submitting letters of
reference will be sent directly to the referees.
For other employment and regional opportunities, please visit our
website at: https://suny.oneonta.edu/about-oneonta/employment
.

jobs.title: Teaching Faculty I
jobs.description:
Job Details
Salary:
Current Employees: If you are currently employed at any of
the Universities of Wisconsin, log in to Workday to apply through
the internal application process.
Job Category:Academic Staff
Employment Type:Regular
Job Profile:Teaching Faculty I
Job Summary:
The Department of Counseling Psychology at The University of
Wisconsin-Madison invites applications for a Teaching Faculty I
position in the field of counseling psychology.
The desired candidate will have the ability to provide instruction
in across our undergraduate courses, including our undergraduate
cross-departmental B.S. major in Health Promotion and Health Equity
and have the potential to contribute to expansion of future
undergraduate course offerings. The candidate may also provide
instruction in our master’s program in counseling, and depending
upon qualifications and needs, our PhD program in counseling
psychology. The desired candidate will teach twelve credits per
semester for a 100% appointment and, depending upon the needs and
structure of the course, may supervise graduate student Teaching
Assistants. Teaching responsibilities of up to 3 credits may be
substituted with other administrative and service duties related to
department needs and depending upon candidate expertise.
Candidates will be expected to contribute to training emphasizing
scientist practitioner perspectives, possess competence to serve
individuals for mental health and wellness across treatment
settings, and to uphold APA and ACA professional and ethical
standards. Preferred candidates will be able to demonstrate service
in the field that has a specific focus in Counseling Psychology
and/or components that are specific to the profession of Counseling
Psychology.
Information about the Department of Counseling Psychology and
School of Education:
The Department of Counseling Psychology offers the MPCAC-accredited
master's degree (M.S.) in counseling and the APA-accredited
doctoral degree (Ph.D.) in counseling psychology. The department is
also a contributor (along with Rehabilitation Psychology and
Kinesiology) to the collaborative, cross-departmental undergraduate
major in Health Promotion and Health Equity.
The department’s master's and doctoral programs are intended to
provide a closely- integrated didactic experiential curriculum for
the preparation of health service psychologists and mental health
counselors. The doctoral degree consistent with the APA's
scientist-practitioner model of training, emphasizes the
integration of counseling and psychological theory and practice
with substantive development of research skills in the domains
encompassed by counseling psychology. The masters in science degree
is MPCAC accredited and emphasizes service delivery, and its
practica/internship components reflect that emphasis. The
curriculum stresses knowledge and development of skills in
individual and group counseling, consultation, research, ethics,
multiculturalism, and career counseling. The department’s mission
is to foster growth, healing, and inclusion in teaching, research,
and practice. Current department faculty have scholarly expertise
in the following areas: psychotherapy processes and outcomes,
educational and vocational development, community-engaged practices
and systems-level healthcare interventions, child development and
parent-child interactions, mindfulness and meditation-based
interventions, and health psychology.
The Department of Counseling Psychology’s Counseling Psychology
Training Clinic (CPTC) offers no fee and sliding scale
psychological services to UW-Madison students and Dane County
residents. The clinic offers individual, family, and group therapy
services and provides direct mental health support and outreach to
UW-Madison students through an innovative community support
partnership with University Health Services at UW-Madison.
The Department of Counseling Psychology is part of the UW-Madison
School of Education, which is regularly ranked as one of the top
Schools of Education in the nation. The School is proud of the
outstanding breadth of its programs, with departments in Education,
Health, and the Arts. The School views this broad range of programs
as a tremendous strength. The UW-Madison School of Education is
committed to the pursuit of excellence in teaching, learning,
research and service by supporting and maintaining inclusive
working and learning environments where all can flourish, and where
the unique contributions of students, faculty, and staff from a
broad range of perspectives, backgrounds, beliefs, and cultures are
valued.

Education:

Job Summary:
The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering seeks to hire
a faculty member with expertise in physical artificial
intelligence, advancing the foundations and technologies that
enable intelligent systems to sense, learn, and act reliably/safely
in the physical world. Desired areas include perception and
multimodal sensing, learning and modeling of physical dynamics, and
the foundations of learning, control, and decision-making for
robotics and autonomous systems.
Outstanding candidates at all levels (Assistant, Associate, Full
Professor rank) will be considered. The ECE Department at
UW-Madison has a long tradition of excellence in educating,
mentoring, and inspiring future leaders; conducting research that
is of vital importance to society; and serving Wisconsin, our
nation, and the world. Our 52 tenure-track/tenured faculty (more
than 35% of which are women) and 10 instructional faculty are
leaders in their fields, respected nationally and internationally
for their innovative research and teaching excellence.
Approximately 400 graduate students and over 1100 undergraduate
students are enrolled in our top-ranked degree programs.

jobs.title: Assistant or Associate Professor of Environmental Health Science - RISE EARTH
jobs.description:
Job Details
Salary:
Current Employees: If you are currently employed at any of
the Universities of Wisconsin, log in to Workday to apply through
the internal application process.
Job Category:Faculty
Employment Type:Regular
Job Profile:Assistant Professor
Job Summary:
The Nelson Institute for Environmental Studies and the Department
of Population Health Sciences at the University of
Wisconsin–Madison invite outstanding environmental health
scientists to apply for a joint appointment, tenure-track position
for an Assistant or Associate Professor in environmental health as
part of the Wisconsin RISE-EARTH (Environment:
Adaptation, Resilience, Technology, and Humanity) initiative. We
seek scholars who demonstrate high potential for developing an
extramurally funded epidemiology research program at UW-Madison.
While any candidates with advanced (PhD or MD and Master
combination) training in environmental health will be considered,
highly competitive candidates will have training and scholarship in
one or more of the following areas of epidemiology: air pollution
epidemiology, human health effects of contaminants in drinking
water, biomarker and/or other environmental exposure and risk
assessment, and measurement and analysis of lifetime environmental
exposures on human health (exposome).
This position is part of the Wisconsin Research, Innovation and
Scholarly Excellence (RISE) Initiative. Through accelerated and
strategic faculty hiring, research infrastructure enhancement,
interdisciplinary collaboration, and increased student and
educational opportunities, RISE addresses complex societal
challenges of importance to the state, nation and world. Building
on UW–Madison’s strengths, RISE expands the University’s successful
track record of connecting with communities and industry on
collaborative solutions.
Over the next three academic years, UW–Madison will substantially
increase current hiring levels, bringing 150 new RISE faculty to
campus. Candidates hired through RISE will join a community of
scholars working across disciplines, schools and colleges on
research, teaching and outreach endeavors. The community will
engage regularly in venues such as seminar series and colloquia to
share ongoing projects and identify opportunities to work together.
The University will support the community, facilitating access to
research infrastructure, and funding to support broad and rich
collaboration.
Further information regarding RISE can be found at: https://rise.wisc.edu/
.
Environmental public health involves interdisciplinary
collaboration researching determinants of disease along causal
pathways of exposure through to health outcomes. This hire,
therefore, will be joint between the Nelson Institute and the
Department of Population Health Sciences.
Research areas within environmental health may include, but not be
limited to human health effects of: exposure to contaminants in
air, water, soil, or food, climate change, noise, and environmental
health effects of emerging technologies. We welcome applications
from scholars employing observational or experiment studies,
longitudinal or cross-sectional designs, and/or mathematical
modeling of environmental health risk.
In addition to a joint appointment in the Nelson Institute for
Environmental Studies (75%) and the Department of Population Health
Sciences (25%), affiliations with other departments, centers, and
institutes across campus are possible. This faculty appointment
will be on an annual (12-month) pay basis. In addition, a generous
start-up package including flexible research funds will be
available for qualified candidates.
The Nelson Institute is a freestanding division of the university,
serving more than one thousand undergraduate and graduate students,
and home two dozen faculty from across the physical, biological,
and social sciences and the humanities. It also houses four
interdisciplinary research centers that serve as cross-campus
laboratories and incubators for solutions to the world’s most
critical environmental challenges. These include: the Center for
Climatic Research, the Center for Culture, History and Environment,
the Center for Sustainability and the Global Environment (SAGE)
that includes an environmental health focus, and the Center for
Ecology and the Environment. The Institute has many partnerships in
education, research and community service that promote a more
environmentally, economically and socially sustainable world. The
Institute offers an undergraduate major and certificates in
environmental studies, and sustainability. Graduate students pursue
MS and PhD degrees in environmental conservation, environmental
observation and informatics, environment and resources, or water
resources management; and certificates in energy analysis and
policy or culture, history, and environment. The institute also
stewards the Office of Sustainability Research and Education for
the UW-Madison campus.
Population Health Sciences is an interdisciplinary department with
the goal of understanding, preserving, and improving the health of
populations and individuals. The candidate selected for this role
will contribute to the advancement of this mission through
research, teaching, and service, and interact with a collaborative
community of scholars throughout SMPH and across campus. The ideal
candidate will have experience working within interdisciplinary
teams. The successful applicant will develop and lead an
extramurally funded research program in environmental epidemiology,
teach courses or equivalent research direction during the academic
year, and participate in administrative and committee work to
support the mission of the School of Medicine and Public Health and
the Nelson Institute. An essential part of these duties will be
working in a collegial relationship with other faculty
members.
Madison is the state's capitol city and is well known for offering
a small town feel in a medium sized city. It is a great place to
raise a family and offers an ideal combination of natural beauty,
stimulating cultural events, outstanding schools and outdoor
recreation.
Key Job Responsibilities:
10% Service:
Participate in faculty governance and service to the department,
school, university, and profession, as appropriate.
30% Teaching:
Teach 9 credits (or equivalent) annually of courses or credited
research direction in environmental health and PHS/Environmental
epidemiology.. Advise and mentor graduate students in the Nelson
Institute, PHS Population Health and Epidemiology programs and
other relevant degree programs at UW-Madison.
The successful applicant will participate in interdisciplinary and
collaborative efforts with other departments, schools and
colleges.
The successful applicant will participate in administrative and
committee work to support the clinical and scholarly missions of
the Nelson Institute and School of Medicine and Public Health. An
essential part of these duties will be working in a collegial
relationship with other faculty members. Especially desirable is an
ability to engage and interact with interdisciplinary communities
and an enthusiasm for team-building within and beyond the health
sciences to include physical systems sciences, social sciences and
the humanities.
The successful candidate, depending on their background, will teach
graduate and undergraduate students, medical students, residents,
and fellows.
60% Research:
Develop and maintain an independent program of research in
environmental epidemiology. Research programs may include but are
not limited to innovative study of air pollution epidemiology,
human health effects of contaminants in drinking water, biomarker
and other environmental exposure assessment, health risks from
climate change and energy policy, and exposome measurement and
analysis.
Department:
The Nelson Institute for Environmental Studies and the Department
of Population Health Sciences
Compensation:
Negotiable – 12-month / full-time (100%) / ongoing /
renewable
Actual pay will depend on experience and qualifications.
This position offers a comprehensive benefits package,
including generous sick leave, competitively priced
health/dental/vision/life insurance, tax-advantaged savings
accounts, and participation in the nationally recognized Wisconsin
Retirement System (WRS) pension fund. For a summary of benefits,
please see https://www.wisconsin.edu/ohrwd/benefits/download/fasl.pdf
.
Required Qualifications:
Candidates should demonstrate evidence of creativity and excellence
in teaching and scholarly research as well as the ability to make
valuable contributions to the department, college, and RISE
initiative. Application materials for this tenure-track position in
environment epidemiology should communicate capacity to conduct
cutting-edge research, teach/mentor undergraduates and graduate
students, and participate in department and university service. In
addition, the successful candidate will demonstrate fostering or
the ability to foster a teaching, learning, mentoring,
departmental, and research environment where all can thrive.
Hiring rank will be commensurate with years of relevant experience.
To be hired at the associate professor level, candidates must
possess experience and scholarly credentials that meet the tenure
standards of the UW-Madison Divisional Committee and of the Nelson
Institute.
All requirements must be met by the position start date.
Preferred Qualifications:
Education:
Terminal Degree (PhD, MD or DrPH) is required by the start date
of the position.
How to Apply:
Apply online at "Jobs at UW" (http://jobs.wisc.edu) under Job
Requisition JR10016349. Applications must be received through UW-
Madison's online application system. Applications submitted outside
of this system will not be considered. Click the "" button to start
the application process. Applicants should submit the following
items:
1. a letter of application,
2. curriculum vitae,
3. a research statement
You will be asked to provide the names and contact information of
three (3) references who are well-respected authorities in the
field. For those who advance in the process, references will be
contacted to provide letters of recommendation. Candidates will be
notified prior to contacting references.
To ensure consideration, complete applications must be received
by 11:59pm (CST) on December 7, 2026. Applications will be
accepted until position is filled. Please note that applicants will
be evaluated based upon submitted application materials and
therefore should speak to and include evidence of their
qualifications.
Please note that successful applicants are responsible for ensuring

Job Summary:
AI and Games in Education is an emerging, growing sub-discipline
that draws from a wide variety of hard and soft skills which are
relevant and applicable across educational research. A core
commitment of the Design, Informal, and Creative Education (DICE)
program in the Department of Curriculum and Instruction at
UW-Madison is that equity, education, making, and play are deeply
interrelated. By enabling more students to express themselves by
playing and making games, we can explore and improve our
understanding of teaching and learning outcomes and engage students
who are both consumers and producers of knowledge.

Job Details
Position Rank and Title: Assistant Professor, Electrical
Engineering

CSU Employee Benefits Summary for details about the CSU’s
excellent benefits package.
Target Start Date: August 17, 2027
Application Deadline: December 1, 2026
(Applications accepted until filled or closed)
Position Description
The Department of Electrical Engineering at San José State
University is pleased to announce a search for a tenure-track
Assistant Professor beginning in August 2027. We seek candidates
with expertise in Application-Specific Integrated Circuits (ASICs),
System-On-a-Chip (SOC), artificial intelligence/machine learning
(AI/ML), Radio Frequency (RF) hardware, and embedded systems. The
successful candidate will be required to teach undergraduate and
graduate electrical engineering courses and maintain an active
research program in these areas. The EE Department encourages and
celebrates multidisciplinary research that solves real-world
problems, including but not limited to food scarcity, assistive
technologies, healthcare, manufacturing, and transportation.
Located in the center of Silicon Valley, the Department of
Electrical Engineering at SJSU has established a firm goal of
providing a high-quality electrical engineering education to its
students at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. The
department offers classroom instruction by the best-qualified EE
faculty, hands-on experience in industry-sponsored,
state-of-the-art laboratories, and opportunities for industry
internships. The department has over 800 undergraduate students, 20
SAGE (accelerated master's in EE) students, and 190 graduate
students. Both the EE undergraduate and graduate programs help
students gain professional experience while taking classes. In
conjunction with their classes, many students work as Instructional
Student Assistants and Teaching Associates in the department, and
as EE interns at Silicon Valley firms. Our graduates enjoy
excellent career opportunities in a broad spectrum of theoretical
and practical areas such as device physics, micro and nano
electronics, analog electronics, integrated circuits,
communications, signal processing, network and network security,
mobile network, power electronics, energy systems, microprocessors
and computer systems, embedded systems, control, robotics,
autonomous systems, machine learning and deep learning, quantum
information and quantum computing. The Department of Electrical
Engineering website is at www.sjsu.edu/ee/ .
Department Resources & Infrastructure
Micro Processing Engineering Laboratory (MPEL) : Offers
hands-on facilities for oxidation/diffusion, contact and maskless
photolithography, IC testing, wet/dry etching, and a minor in
semiconductor fabrication. The facility has a strong tradition of
workforce development. ( MPEL
Website )
Advanced Characterization Equipment : Access to MCMC
SEM, Atomic Force Microscopy, X-Ray Diffraction, and 3-D Optical
Profilometry.
Specialized Laboratories :
Charles Babbage Synopsys Laboratory: Servers and Software
Cadence Design Systems Laboratory: Servers and Software
Teradyne: Memory ATE Laboratory
LitePoint Corporation: RF Antenna Pattern Test Chamber
E&M and microwave: VNA, ANSYS software
Cheadle RF Communications Laboratory : Spectrum Analyzer, Logic
Analyzer, Time Synthesizer, Vector Signal Generator, Network
Analyzer
● Consortia, Hubs & Academic Partnerships
Member of the California-Pacific-Northwest AI
Hardware Hub and the Edge Consortium
NNME
Pacific-Intermountain Regional Node
Collaborative facilities, including
Stanford SNF and Berkeley Marvell Nano
Lab
Extensive relationships with local community colleges
The Department has numerous corporate sponsors, and faculty have
access to research development support through the Division of
Research and Innovation and teaching and career development support
through the Center for Faculty Excellence and Teaching and
Innovation ( CFETI ).
The Department of Electrical Engineering at San José State
University values institutional excellence and is committed to
advancing equity through research, teaching, and service. We enroll
more than 40,000 students, many of whom are historically
underserved; approximately 45% of our undergraduates are
first-generation, and 38% are Pell Grant recipients. In addition,
we are both a Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI) and an Asian
American and Native American Pacific Islander-Serving Institution
(AANAPISI). SJSU aspires to create holistic learning environments
that facilitate both individual and collective transformation. We
seek teacher-scholars who cultivate inclusive, empowering spaces
for mutual learning, skill-building, and knowledge exchange for all
students. Our commitment to lifelong learning supports meaningful
connections among faculty, staff, students, alums, and the broader
communities we serve.
We invite all applicants to include a Statement of Institutional
Excellence (or incorporate it into your cover letter) to share how
your lived and professional experiences will contribute to the SJSU
community—particularly in relation to student success. A guide to
writing this statement can be found at
SJSU Institutional Excellence Statement Guidelines .
Required Qualifications
Applicants must have a Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering
or Electrical and Computer Engineering by the start of the
appointment.
Applicants must have a research background in Embedded Systems,
ASIC, and SOC design.
Applicants must have a strong commitment, demonstrate potential
for teaching excellence at both the undergraduate and graduate
levels, and engage in curriculum development.
Applicants should demonstrate awareness of and sensitivity to
the educational goals of a socially and economically diverse
student population, as might have been gained through
cross-cultural study, training, teaching, and other comparable
experience.
Preferred Qualifications
Postdoctoral experience in academia or industry
Experience mentoring undergraduate and/or graduate research
students.
Experience adapting teaching methods to a variety of learning
environments.
Involved in safety compliance across high-risk, multi-variable
industrial or academic environments
Key Responsibilities
Faculty member is expected to teach, supervise, and advise
students in both undergraduate and graduate programs, to provide
leadership in developing modern curriculum in Embedded Systems,
System on Chip, ASIC, with applications in Machine Learning, Deep
Learning, Robotics; to establish a research program related to
their field of interest; and to seek external partnership, funding,
and/or collaboration with Silicon Valley and beyond.
The candidate will participate in shared governance, usually
through departmental, college, and university committees and other
service assignments with a special emphasis on assessment.
Faculty shall organize all their classes within the Canvas
Learning Management System (LMS).
The candidate must demonstrate awareness of and experience with
the needs of a student population of great diversity – in age,
abilities, cultural background, ethnicity, religion, economic
background, primary language, sexual orientation, gender identity,
and academic preparation – through inclusive course materials,
teaching strategies, and advisement.
Other Duties
Note that all San José State University employees are considered
mandated reporters under the California Child Abuse and Neglect
Reporting Act and are required to comply with the requirements set
forth in CSU Executive Order 1083 as a condition of employment.
Pursuant to the Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy
and Campus Crime Statistics Act (Clery Act) and CSU systemwide
policy, some faculty duties may lead to designation as a Campus
Security Authority (CSA). CSAs are required to complete Clery Act
training and to immediately report Clery incidents to the
institution.
Faculty employees must complete CSU employee training as assigned
and required based on their role (e.g., Data Security, FERPA,
Preventing Discrimination and Harassment, Title IX, Health and
Safety). The President may recommend or require compliance with
safety measures that decrease the likelihood of COVID-19
transmission or illness and allows the core mission and activities
of the campus to continue.
Application Procedure
Click Apply Now to complete the SJSU Online Employment Application
and attach the following documents (3-page limit on each
document):
letter of interest (1-page limit)
curriculum vitae (3-page limit)
institutional excellence statement (dedicated statement or
addressed in letter of interest) (1-page limit)
statement of teaching interests/philosophy (1-page
limit)
research plans (2-page limit)
three references with contact information
Inquiries may be directed to the Department Chair, Professor David
W. Parent, David.Parent@sjsu.edu.
Pursuant to California Education Code 89521, applicants will be
required to disclose whether they have received a final
administrative decision or final judicial decision determining that
they have committed sexual harassment within the last 7 years only
after a determination is made that they meet the minimum
qualifications for the position, and before an offer of employment
is extended. Applicants who reach the final stages of the
application process must also sign a release form that authorizes
the release of information by the applicant’s current and/or former
employers to the CSU concerning any substantiated allegations of
misconduct.
Conditional Offer
The work for this faculty position may only be performed in the
State of California and requires establishing an on-campus
presence. Employment is contingent upon US residence and proof of
eligibility to work in the United States. Satisfactory completion
of background and reference checks (including criminal records and
prior employment) is required. SJSU will make a conditional offer
of employment, which may be rescinded if the background and
reference checks reveal disqualifying information, and/or it is
discovered that the candidate knowingly withheld or falsified
information. Failure to satisfactorily complete the background and
reference checks may affect the continued employment of a current
employee who was conditionally offered the position.
San José State University: Silicon Valley's Public
University
Located in the heart of Silicon Valley — one of the most innovative
regions in the world — San José State University
is the founding campus of the 23-campus California State University
(CSU) system and the first public university in the West.
Recognized as a leading transformative educational institution, San
José State is an essential partner in the technological, economic,
cultural, and social development of Silicon Valley, the Bay Area,
and California. SJSU is a top-200 school nationally for research
funding and ranks second in research productivity within the CSU
system. Cutting-edge research, world-class scholarship,

social justice allow SJSU to provide life-changing opportunities
and advance the public good locally and globally.
Equal Employment Statement
San José State University prohibits discrimination based on Age,

jobs.description:
The Department of Mechanical and Aerospace Engineering at North Carolina State University invites applications for multiple tenured or tenure track faculty positions at the rank of Assistant/Associate/Full Professor with particular interest in aerostructures, manufacturing, and engineering design disciplines.
Aerostructures:
Including but not limited to: 1) structures for space platforms; 2) fluid and/or thermal structure interactions, aerothermoelasticity, nonlinear structural dynamics and multiphysics phenomena as it relates to aerostructures; 3) physical reservoir computing and concepts relating to mechanically embodied intelligence for aerospace applications; and 4) advanced multifunctional structures for aerospace applications.
Advanced Manufacturing for aerospace, mechanical, and marine applications:
Including but not limited to: 1) modeling and simulations of manufacturing processes for innovation and scale up; 2) rapid and advanced manufacturing of hot structures and extreme-environment components, including space manufacturing; 3) multiphysics modeling, sensing, and process monitoring to inform manufacturing decisions; 4) AI/ML-enabled, intelligent, and autonomous manufacturing, including digital twins and advanced process control; and 5) quantum manufacturing paradigms, including quantum-enabled manufacturing and other transformative manufacturing technologies.
Complex System Design for aerospace, mechanical, and marine applications, exploring how advanced computational tools can change the way systems are conceived, optimized, and manufactured.
Including but not limited to: 1) Human-AI collaboration and co-teaming; 2) multidisciplinary optimization tools to synchronize design and digital manufacturing; 3) design decision-making under uncertainty; and 4) the strategic management of change to create resilient systems.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Tenure Track, AI and Business Strategy
jobs.description:
Job Description: The School of Global Business is seeking to fill a nine-month tenure track Assistant Professor position with a primary focus on AI in Business and Strategic Management.
The School of Global Business (SGB) is one of Arcadia University's specialty schools and colleges. Using a comprehensive curriculum and experiential learning environment, SGB is dedicated to developing socially responsible decision makers, critical thinkers, and effective communicators. SGB prepares students to become competent professionals informed by a global perspective by combining solid liberal arts studies with experiential learning, such as internships and corporate experiences.
SGB is accredited by the Accreditation Council for Business Schools and Programs (ACBSP). SGB offers Bachelor's Degrees in Business Administration, Accounting, Healthcare Administration, International Business and Culture, Marketing, and Sport Management. Students can pursue concentrations in Finance, Economics, and Management, as well as Minors in eight areas. SGB also offers a Master's Degree in Business Administration with specializations currently offered in Finance, Organizational Leadership, and Healthcare Finance.
SGB is expanding its academic portfolio to address the rapidly evolving role of artificial intelligence in business. The successful candidate will play a central leadership role in developing an undergraduate minor in AI and Business, with the eventual goal of establishing a full undergraduate major in AI and Business. Additionally, the candidate may be involved in the ongoing design and development of an MBA concentration in AI Strategy and Analytics.
Review of applications will begin immediately with a priority deadline of November 30. The position is expected to start in August, 2027.
Candidates must have permanent work authorization without the need for current or future employer sponsorship.
Location: Glenside
Responsibilities for this position include (but are not limited to):
Teach a six-course load per academic year across undergraduate and graduate offerings in multiple modalities (face-to-face, online, hybrid).
Teach capstone courses in Strategic Management at both the undergraduate and MBA levels, incorporating cutting-edge AI strategy and business application concepts.
Lead the curriculum development and implementation of a new undergraduate minor in AI and Business, laying the foundation for an eventual undergraduate major in AI and Business.
Apply proven experience and expertise in AI to innovate business education, integrating generative AI, predictive analytics, ethics, and corporate governance across SGB offerings.
Collaborate and support in the ongoing work to design and launch an MBA concentration in AI Strategy and Analytics.
Maintain an active scholarly agenda published in peer-reviewed journals, focusing on strategic management, business AI applications, or tech-driven business transformation.
Advise students, develop curriculum, participate in program assessment, and build relationships within the Philadelphia business community to create career and experiential learning opportunities for Arcadia students.
Provide service to the University and the community as a full-time faculty member of Arcadia University.
Required Qualifications:
Doctoral degree (Ph.D. or D.B.A.) in Business Strategy, Information Systems, Business Administration/Management (with a strategy specialization), or a closely related discipline with demonstrated expertise in AI applications in business.
Promising ABDs with relevant work-related experience who expect to have their degree completed by the start date will also be considered.
Proven teaching experience at the university level, with the capability to deliver capstone Strategic Management courses at both undergraduate and graduate levels.
Demonstrated expertise and applied experience integrating Artificial Intelligence into business strategy or curriculum.
Strong record or promising trajectory of scholarly publications in peer-reviewed journals.
Demonstrated experience teaching across multiple course delivery formats (face-to-face, online, hybrid).
Preferred Qualifications:
Demonstrated track record or strong interest in academic program development, particularly in creating new minors, majors, or graduate concentrations.
Practical experience with AI tools, business analytics, or generative AI frameworks applied to strategic decision-making and business management.
Strong commitment to AI ethics, data privacy, corporate governance, and responsible decision-making within a liberal arts educational framework.
Relevant industry, corporate strategy, management consulting, or tech sector experience.
Experience with experiential learning methodologies, including client-facing projects, business simulations, and live case studies.
Capacity for interdisciplinary collaboration with related departments such as Data Science, Computer Science, and Liberal Arts programs.

To apply, please upload the following documents with your application:
Cover Letter
Curriculum vitae
Recent student course evaluations
Statement of Teaching Philosophy (addressing experience with AI in business education)
Research Philosophy
Evidence of a commitment to Arcadia University's Mission and Lived Values through teaching or scholarly work
Name and contact information of three (3) professional references.
Review of applications will begin immediately with a priority deadline of November 16. The position is expected to start in August, 2027. Posting will be removed from the website once we've established a sufficient talent pool for consideration.

Due to the volume of applications received, communication will generally be limited to candidates selected for additional consideration. Application review will begin immediately.
