jobs.title: Open Rank Project/Program Manager
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Description
Based on the foundation of the Ted and Karyn Hume Center for
National Security and Technology, Virginia Tech launched the
Virginia Tech National Security Institute in September 2021. With a
presence in both Blacksburg and the Washington, D.C. metro area,
the Virginia Tech National Security Institute (VTNSI) performs
cutting-edge research and development for externally sponsored
national security programs and develops the next generation of
national security talent through student engagement in education
and research.
VTNSI is seeking several Project/Program Managers to support the
planning, financial management, coordination, and execution of
sponsored research projects and programs located in both the
Blacksburg, Virginia, and Arlington, Virginia locations. Candidates
may be considered for appointment as Project Manager I, Project
Manager II, Program Manager I, or Program Manager II, depending on
qualifications, demonstrated competencies, organizational needs,
and the scope of assigned responsibilities.
Positions are intended for administrative and professional (AP)
faculty classification requiring quantitative, mathematical,
analytical, and financial management skills. Responsibilities
increase in complexity, independence, accountability, leadership,
and sponsor engagement across the four levels. Appointment level
and location will be determined based on relevant knowledge,
skills, abilities, experience, position requirements, and available
opportunities. Positions are eligible for a hybrid work arrangement
requiring weekly in-office presence. Given the nature and
sensitivity of the institute’s funding portfolio, these positions
are restricted to U.S. Citizens.
Specific responsibilities include:
• Develop, maintain, monitor, and analyze project or program
budgets, expenditures, funding balances, forecasts, and resource
requirements; perform calculations, reconciliations, and
budget-to-actual comparisons.
• Coordinate project or program schedules, milestones,
deliverables, performance reporting, and risk management with
principal investigators, research teams, university offices,
sponsors, and partners.
• Prepare accurate financial and operational reports, maintain
project documentation, identify variances and risks, and support
applicable university policies and sponsor requirements.
• Support sponsor communications, proposal preparation, opportunity
identification, process improvement, and business development, as
appropriate to the assigned level.
• At Project Manager I and II levels, support or independently
manage assigned project activities. At Program Manager I and II
levels, additionally coordinate multiple related projects or
programs, balance resources, guide staff, and support broader
sponsor engagement and program development.
Required Qualifications
• Degree in Public Administration, Business Administration,
Project/Program Management, or a related discipline.
• Project Manager I: Bachelor’s degree in a related technical or
professional field with relevant experience, or an earned master’s
degree
• Project Manager II: Bachelor’s degree in a related field with at
least three years of relevant experience, or a related master’s
degree with relevant project management experience.
• Program Manager I: Bachelor’s degree in a related field with at
least five years of progressively responsible experience, or a
related master’s degree with at least three years of relevant
experience of small to moderate program portfolios.
• Program Manager II: Bachelor’s degree in a related field with at
least seven years of progressively responsible experience, or a
related master’s degree with at least five years of relevant
experience, including demonstrated leadership of moderate to
complex program portfolios.
Financial Management, Quantitative Analysis, and Spreadsheet
Skills
• All levels: Demonstrated proficiency with spreadsheet
applications, including formulas, calculations, financial tracking,
data organization, and analysis, along with strong mathematical,
quantitative, analytical, and problem-solving skills.
• Project Manager I: Demonstrated ability to perform financial
calculations, maintain budget spreadsheets, track and reconcile
expenditures, identify discrepancies, and prepare routine financial
reports for projects with straightforward funding
requirements.
• Project Manager II: Demonstrated ability to independently analyze
and manage financial data for higher-value projects with more
complex funding requirements, including budget reconciliations,
expenditure analysis, forecasting, variance identification, and
financial reporting.
• Program Manager I: Demonstrated ability to analyze and
consolidate financial information across multiple related projects,
monitor expenditures and funding balances, reconcile budgets,
identify financial risks, and prepare consolidated financial
reports to support program management decisions.
• Program Manager II: Demonstrated ability to oversee financial
analysis and reporting across complex programs or portfolios,
evaluate funding and resource requirements, resolve complex budget
issues, develop financial forecasts, and provide data-driven
recommendations to support program-level decision-making.
• Strong organizational skills, attention to detail, and ability to
manage multiple priorities and deadlines.
• Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to
collaborate with research teams, university stakeholders, sponsors,
and external partners.
• U.S. Citizen
• Ability to obtain and maintain a security clearance.
Preferred Qualifications
• Active security clearance
• Project management certification (e.g., PMP) or equivalent
project management training or experience.
• Experience supporting sponsored research, federally funded
projects, government contracting, or national security programs.
(Required at the Program Manager I and II levels)
• Experience coordinating with principal investigators, sponsors,
university departments, and external partners.
• For specialized assignments, experience with subcontract cost
monitoring, invoice review, financial reconciliation, funding
opportunity identification, proposal development, resource
planning, or business development. (Required at the Program Manager
I and II levels)
• Experience in an academic research environment, including working
with students.
• Required at Program Manager I and II levels, experience
coordinating multiple projects, managing program resources,
mentoring or leading staff, engaging sponsors, or overseeing
complex program portfolios.
Overtime Status
Exempt: Not eligible for overtime
Appointment Type
Restricted
Salary Information
$75,000–$150,000 annually, depending on position level,
qualifications, experience, and work location.
- Project Manager I starting at $75,000 in Blacksburg and $90,000
in Arlington
- Project Manager II starting at $85,000 in Blackburg and $95,000
in Arlington
- Program Manager I starting at $95,000 in Blacksburg and $100,000
in Arlington
- Program Manager II starting at $115,000 in Blacksburg and
$130,000 in Arlington
Hours per week
40
Review Date
11/16/2026
Additional Information
Due to the nature of our work, all applicants must be US citizens
and able to obtain and maintain a security clearance.
Work location may be in either the Blacksburg, VA or Arlington, VA
locations.
The successful candidate will be required to have a criminal
conviction check.

jobs.title: Faculty Position Clinical Research in Cardiovascular Science - Virginia Tech
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Description
Virginia Tech (VT) seeks to recruit an innovative
clinician-scientist to its Patient Research Center (PRC) at the
Fralin Biomedical Research Institute at VTC (FBRI - https://fbri.vtc.vt.edu/ ) for a
tenured or tenure-track faculty position at the associate or full
professor level. The PRC initiative has received substantial
funding support as part of the state’s Biomedical Research Diamond
(
https://cardinalnews.org/2026/02/20/friedlander-a-smart-investment-for-southwest-virginia/
) to launch this major new program.
The successful candidate will have an earned M.D. degree with
active medical license and preferably also have a Ph.D. as well as
appropriate postdoctoral residency-fellowship training. They should
have an active research program that is funded through federal
agencies and/or industry for patient-based clinical research, while
they may also have a more translational laboratory-based research
program as well. Applications from investigators using innovative
contemporary approaches to study human cardiovascular and/or
cardiometabolic function in health and disease with inclusion of
clinical research trials are welcomed. The faculty member will join
45 other faculty led teams at the FBRI, including 8 cardiovascular
research teams, 4 exercise medicine research teams and additional
groups working on dietary-metabolic health. The primary
responsibility for the position is to lead a strong extramurally
funded leading-edge clinical research program in cardiovascular
and/or cardiometabolic science with some time devoted to patient
care with our clinical partner, Carilion Clinic ( https://www.carilionclinic.org/heart
) and will include some research mentoring of graduate and medical
students as well as fellows.
The position will be located at the FBRI on Virginia Tech’s health
sciences and technology campus in Roanoke, Virginia, immediately
adjacent to the Virginia Tech Carilion School of Medicine, Carilion
Clinic and Carilion Roanoke Memorial Hospital. In addition to the
position at the research institute, the faculty member will also
have a tenured or tenure-track appointment in an appropriate VT
department from among multiple colleges, including the School of
Medicine.
The successful candidate will join a dynamic and growing community
of scholars including scientists, physicians and
physician-scientists focused on next generation approaches to
cardiovascular and cardiometabolic research directed at having
dramatic impacts on prevention, diagnoses, and treatment of
disorders that impact cardiometabolic function, including
arrhythmogenesis, heart failure, ischemia, obesity and diabetes.
Candidate whose research is complementary to that of FBRI faculty
in the research institute’s Center for Vascular and Heart Research
(
https://fbri.vtc.vt.edu/research/research-centers/center-for-heart.html
) and Center for Exercise Medicine Research (
https://fbri.vtc.vt.edu/research/research-centers/center-for-exercise-medicine-research.html
) and who are likely to add strengths in areas to contribute to
major collaborative program funding are encouraged to apply.
Research infrastructure at the FBRI currently includes over 300,000
square feet of lab, core facilities and office space ( http://fralinbiomed.info/buildingtour
). Facilities at the research institute include multiple human
subject research-dedicated 3.0T MRIs, high field MR guided PET for
animal cardiology research, and MR-guided focused ultrasound,
optically pumped magnetometers (OPM-MEG), multiple
cellular/molecular imaging facilities including transcriptomics and
genomics analysis in addition to two human whole room calorimeters,
DEXA, exercise facilities and metabolic kitchen as well as a next
generation molecular diagnostics laboratory.
Please submit your application to posting #538367 including full
curriculum vitae and statement of research accomplishments and
plans.
Required Qualifications
The successful candidate will have an earned M.D. degree with
active medical license and preferably also have a Ph.D. as well as
appropriate postdoctoral residency-fellowship training. They should
have an active research program that is funded through federal
agencies and/or industry for patient-based clinical research, while
they may also have a more translational laboratory-based research
program as well. Applications from investigators using innovative
contemporary approaches to study human cardiovascular and/or
cardiometabolic function in health and disease with inclusion of
clinical research trials are welcomed.

Exempt: Not eligible for overtime

Regular

40+

jobs.title: Tenure- Track Assistant Professor in Cardiovascular Science- Virginia Tech
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Description
Virginia Tech (VT) is recruiting a tenure-track faculty position in
cardiovascular sciences at the assistant professor level at the
Fralin Biomedical Research Institute at VTC (FBRI - https://fbri.vtc.vt.edu/ ), located
on its health sciences and technology campus ( https://hst.vt.edu/ ) in Roanoke,
Virginia.
Applicant eligibility requirements include: a Ph.D. and
postdoctoral research experience, with a record of accomplishment
of biomedical research innovation and productivity as demonstrated
through high quality publications in leading scientific journals
and a record of extramural funding.
The selected candidate will join a highly successful research group
of teams of innovative basic and translational researchers at the
FBRI’s Center for Vascular and Heart Research -
https://fbri.vtc.vt.edu/research/research-centers/center-for-heart.html
), who have considerable NIH and American Heart Association support
and are located in a state-of-the-art health sciences campus. The
faculty position at the research institute will include a tenure

cardiovascular research is open and may utilize a basic,
translational and/or clinical approach, using tools of molecular or
genetic science, cell biology, pharmacology, physiology/biophysics

growth include: i) cardio-oncology; ii) arrhythmogenesis; iii)
cardiac physiology and disease; iv) vascular physiology and
disease; v) pulmonary vascular disease; and vi) women’s cardiac
health.

support. Some teaching of graduate students is also expected along

undergraduate students.

Our all-hands-on deck culture requires leadership at all levels to ensure we achieve our mission, implement our goals, and invest in our future one student at a time. We are proud to offer a supportive environment that values well-being and continuous improvement. We believe in being bold, being kind, and being good teammates, making Ramapo not just a place to work, but a great place to belong.
Ramapo College offers outstanding benefits through the New Jersey State Benefits system, generous PTO, professional development opportunities, wellness programs, tuition discounts for employees and their dependents, and much more.

jobs.title: Senior Faculty in Medicinal Chemistry / Chemical Biology
jobs.description:
Senior Faculty in Medicinal Chemistry / Chemical Biology
University of Virginia
Charlottesville, Virginia
The Department of Chemistry in the College and Graduate School of Arts & Sciences, with the Paul and Diane Manning Institute of Biotechnology at the University of Virginia (UVA), invites applications and nominations for a senior tenured faculty appointment in Medicinal Chemistry or Chemical Biology in the Department of Chemistry. The successful candidate will also serve as Head of Medicinal Chemistry at the Manning Institute.
As a faculty member, the successful candidate will develop and lead an innovative, externally funded experimental research program that bridges synthetic chemistry with biologically relevant problems in areas such as probe development, chemical biology, and drug discovery. As Head of Medicinal Chemistry, the candidate will build medicinal chemistry capacity that supports translational drug discovery across the University. This role carries strategic responsibility beyond the candidate’s own laboratory, including shaping the Institute’s long-term scientific direction, leading faculty and staff recruitment efforts, guiding budget and resource allocation decisions, and setting strategic priorities across the Manning Institute’s portfolio of biotechnology programs and investments.
This appointment comes at a pivotal moment for the University as it advances one of the most ambitious life sciences initiatives in its history. Through the Manning Institute, UVA is making a significant institutional investment to accelerate drug discovery, translational science, and biotechnology innovation across the University and the Commonwealth of Virginia. As one of the inaugural senior hires in this effort, the successful candidate will connect Chemistry’s strengths in molecular discovery and synthesis with a growing university-wide ecosystem in translational science and human health.
The successful candidate will join a highly collaborative research environment that spans chemistry, biology, medicine, and data science, engaging colleagues across the Manning Institute, UVA Comprehensive Cancer Center, School of Medicine, and other relevant areas of the University. These connections will provide a strong foundation for building an ambitious research program that brings together fundamental chemistry, disease biology, and therapeutic discovery, with opportunities to extend promising discoveries toward broader translational impact. This senior faculty member will contribute to UVA’s undergraduate and graduate educational mission and play a key role in mentoring graduate students and postdoctoral scholars to help shape new educational and training opportunities that connect graduate education with the Manning Institute's biotechnology and translational research mission.
Candidates must hold a Ph.D. in Chemistry or a closely related field and demonstrate a record of, or strong potential for, excellence in experimental research. The successful candidate will operate effectively in a highly matrixed organization and bring expertise in research that bridges synthetic chemistry with biologically relevant problems, including areas such as small-molecule probe development, chemical biology, or drug discovery. The Department of Chemistry is particularly interested in candidates whose work integrates modern synthetic approaches with mechanistic insight into disease-relevant biology. Beyond scientific excellence, UVA seeks a collaborative and entrepreneurial scholar with experience advancing research towards translational application, commercialization, and other forms of real-world impact. Appointment rank is open and will be commensurate with the successful candidate’s qualifications and experience.
Screening of complete applications will begin immediately and continue until the completion of the search process. Applications should include a cover letter, curriculum vitae, research statement, teaching statement, and contact information for three references. Materials should be submitted via the Isaacson, Miller website: https://www.imsearch.com/open-searches/university-virginia/faculty-medicinal-chemistrychemical-biology
Micah Pierce, Partner

Marlyn Desire, Senior Search Coordinator
Isaacson, Miller

For more than 60 years, Kennesaw State University has been known

north of Atlanta and combines a suburban setting on two
metro-Atlanta campuses in Kennesaw and Marietta. As one of

University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State is a
Carnegie-designated doctoral research institution (R2) committed to
becoming a world-class academic institution positioned to broaden
its academic and research missions and expand its scope on a local,
regional, and national level.
Our university's vibrant culture, career opportunities, rich
benefits, and values of respect, integrity, collaboration,
inclusivity, and accountability make us an employer of choice. As
part of the University System of
Georgia, Kennesaw State exemplifies the power and promise of a
student-centered, research-driven university. In addition, Kennesaw
State supports the University of Georgia's core values of
accountability, excellence, integrity, and respect. We are
searching for talented people to join Kennesaw State University in

website.
Location
Our Kennesaw campus is located at 1000 Chastain Road NW, Kennesaw,

Research experience in applied or computational mathematics and

jobs.title: Part-time and Limited Term Faculty Positions in School of Communication and Media
jobs.description:
Part-time and Limited Term Faculty Positions in School of
Communication and Media
Job ID: 305226
Location: Kennesaw, Georgia
Full/Part Time: Part Time
Regular/Temporary: Regular
About Us
For more than 60 years, Kennesaw State University has been known
for its entrepreneurial spirit and sense of community. A leader in
innovative teaching and learning, Kennesaw State is located just
north of Atlanta and combines a suburban setting on two
metro-Atlanta campuses in Kennesaw and Marietta. As one of
Georgia's largest universities, Kennesaw State offers undergraduate
and graduate degrees to over 50,000 students. Our high-impact
research and Division I athletics also draw students from
throughout the region and across the globe. A member of the
University System of Georgia, Kennesaw State is a
Carnegie-designated doctoral research institution (R2) committed to
becoming a world-class academic institution positioned to broaden
its academic and research missions and expand its scope on a local,
regional, and national level.
Our university's vibrant culture, career opportunities, rich
benefits, and values of respect, integrity, collaboration,
inclusivity, and accountability make us an employer of choice. As
part of the University System of
Georgia, Kennesaw State exemplifies the power and promise of a
student-centered, research-driven university. In addition, Kennesaw
State supports the University of Georgia's core values of
accountability, excellence, integrity, and respect. We are
searching for talented people to join Kennesaw State University in
our vision. For more information, visit the Kennesaw State University
website.
Location
Our Kennesaw campus is located at 1000 Chastain Road NW, Kennesaw,
GA 30144. Our Marietta campus is located at 1100 South Marietta
Parkway, Marietta, GA 30060.
Department Information
The School of Communication & Media prepares ethical, mindful,
and effective communicators who combine human skills and technical
expertise to pursue fulfilling careers, lead in their communities,
tell impactful stories, and grow strong relationships. We blend
industry-relevant programs with forward-thinking scholarship to
build understanding of the power of communication to innovate,
connect, and create.
With more than 400 full-time faculty and 8,100 degree-seeking
students, the Norman J. Radow College of Humanities & Social
Sciences is dedicated to pioneering workforce readiness in the
humanities and social sciences. By staying true to our Liberal Arts
values and integrating practical knowledge and experiential
learning into our curriculum, we empower our students to become
responsible citizens ready for the demands of the modern workplace.
The home of three schools and eight departments, the College offers
more than 80 graduate and undergraduate programs of study in both
traditional and interdisciplinary fields. These programs enable
students to develop leadership, problem-solving, and critical
thinking skills, as well as a strong sense of civic
engagement.
The College is committed to the success of our students, faculty,
staff and communities. We seek candidates whose experience has
prepared them to fulfill that commitment and engage our students,
partners, and stakeholders effectively.
Job Summary
Kennesaw State University is now accepting applications for a pool
of open rank, part-time and limited term faculty positions in the
School of Communication and Media for the academic year 2026-2027.
These positions are on an as needed, semester-by-semester basis.
Rank is determined at the time of hiring and will be commensurate
with credentials. These positions are for work to be performed in
the state of Georgia.
Please be advised that Kennesaw State University does not provide
any type of visa sponsorship, including transfers, for limited term
or part-time faculty.
Responsibilities
Teaching undergraduate courses to support our lower-division
and upper-division courses in the broad fields of Journalism &
Emerging Media, Media & Entertainment, Organizational &
Professional Communication, and Public Relations
Common courses for part-time faculty include Human
Communication; Public Speaking; Writing for Public Communication;
Communication Law, Ethics, and Diversity; and Digital Media
Production
Part-time faculty may be asked to teach in various modalities
(face-to-face, hybrid, and online) and courses may be assigned at
the Kennesaw or Marietta campus.
Teaching assignments will be based on earned degrees and SACSCOC
Faculty Credentials Guidelines.
Required Qualifications
A minimum of a Master's degree, or the foreign equivalent, in
Communication, Journalism, Mass Communication, or a closely related
discipline is required at the time of hire.
OR
A minimum of a Master's degree, or the foreign equivalent, in a
non-related discipline with 18 graduate credit hours in the
teaching discipline is required at the time of hire.
Preferred Qualifications
Previous college-level teaching experience
Relevant professional experience
Experience teaching on-line or hybrid courses
Required Documents to Attach
CV
Cover Letter
Unofficial Transcripts (Official Transcripts and Official
International Course-by-Course Evaluations Due Upon Hire)
Names, phone numbers, and email addresses of at least 3
references

available. (Candidates who have not taught in a university setting
should submit a statement describing how they would leverage their
industry experience as part of their teaching philosophy.) (Upload
as additional documents).

Contact Information
For questions about this faculty opening, please contact Chris
McCollough, cmccol20@kennesaw.edu.
For technical support or assistance completing a job application,
please contact the Shared Services Center at (877) 251-2644 or
support@usg.edu.
For questions about a specific job posting at Kennesaw State
University, please contact the search chair listed under the
contact information section on each posting. For general questions
about faculty jobs please email facultyjobs@kennesaw.edu.
USG Core Values
The University System of Georgia is comprised of our 26
institutions of higher education and learning as well as the System
Office. Our USG Statement of Core Values are Integrity, Excellence,
Accountability, and Respect. These values serve as the foundation
for all that we do as an organization, and each USG community
member is responsible for demonstrating and upholding these
standards. More details on the USG Statement of Core Values and
Code of Conduct are available in USG Board Policy 8.2.18.1.2 and
can be found on-line at
https://www.usg.edu/policymanual/section8/C224/#p8.2.18_personnel_conduct.
Additionally, USG supports Freedom of Expression as stated in Board

Equal Employment Opportunity
Kennesaw State University is an Equal Employment Opportunity

Background Check
Per the University System of Georgia background check policy, all

All applicants are required to include professional references as

jobs.title: Faculty Position (Assistant or Associate Professor) in Large Animal Anesthesia - Academic Clinician
jobs.description:
Faculty Position (Assistant or Associate Professor) in Large
Animal Anesthesia – Academic Clinician Track
Location: Kennett Square, PA
Open Date: Oct 30, 2026
Deadline:
The Department of Clinical Studies-New Bolton Center at the
University of Pennsylvania School of Veterinary Medicine (Penn Vet)
invites applications for a faculty position at the Assistant or
Associate Professor level in large animal anesthesia, with a focus
on equine anesthesia. The position will be in the Associated
Faculty in the Academic Clinician (AC) track, which focuses on
clinical service and teaching. A typical division of effort for
faculty in the AC track at New Bolton Center is 90% time on
clinics, including clinical service and clinical teaching, and 10%
time off clinics for academic efforts. Didactic and laboratory
teaching and administrative or other service duties are included in
both on- and off-clinic time.
Applications are also being accepted for the position in our
Clinician-Educator track, which carries with it assigned time and
expectations for research or other scholarly productivity. Please
see position number ***** for further details on the position as
Clinician Educator. A total of two positions will be
filled.
This position offers the opportunity to join a team of passionate
clinical and didactic educators with a shared commitment to
excellence in patient care and a significant emphasis on teaching
in the clinical environment. The Section of Anesthesia is home to
four diplomates of the American or European Colleges of Veterinary
Anesthesia and Analgesia and to three anesthesia technicians. Five
residents in training for ACVAA/ECVAA board certification divide
their time between Penn Vet's Matthew J. Ryan Veterinary Hospital
for Companion Animals and the New Bolton Center Hospital, while an
additional clinical fellow is dedicated full-time to New Bolton
Center.
Clinical service and clinical teaching are at the heart of this
position. The New Bolton Center Hospital for Large Animals provides
an exceptional environment for both, with approximately 1,400
animals anesthetized each year for a wide variety of procedures.
Clinical responsibilities include primary anesthesia care, pain
management, supervision and mentorship of technicians and residents
in the anesthetic management of patients (the majority of which are
equine), as well as participation in the after-hours anesthesia
rotation. Clinical effort is based at the New Bolton Center
Hospital; however, faculty who are interested may also have
opportunities to participate in the clinical services at the Ryan
Veterinary Hospital as well as in delivery of anesthesia at zoos
and animal parks in the surrounding area.
The Department of Clinical Studies-New Bolton Center includes more
than 40 diplomates of American and European specialty colleges,
including 15 faculty who are double-boarded, providing
opportunities for interaction across a broad range of specialties.
The faculty share a strong commitment to collaborative,
compassionate patient care. The multidisciplinary environment
provides frequent opportunities for case discussion and exchange of
perspectives across specialties, including through morbidity and
mortality rounds, grand rounds, clinical ethics discussions, and
informal consultation on the clinical floor. Anesthesiologists are
valued contributors to these discussions and to patient care
throughout the hospital.
Teaching is integrated throughout the clinical program and provides
opportunities to work closely with veterinary students, interns,
residents, technicians, and colleagues. In addition to case-based
teaching on the clinical floor, faculty contribute to didactic and
laboratory instruction and other educational activities. The
position is particularly well-suited to an individual who enjoys
teaching in the context of clinical practice, values mentorship and
the exchange of ideas, and would welcome the opportunity to help
learners develop their knowledge, technical skills, clinical
reasoning, and confidence. Penn Vet students and house officers are
highly qualified, motivated, and eager to learn, and faculty share
a strong commitment to creating a supportive and engaging
educational experience.
Research is not a requirement of this position; however, faculty in
the AC track who have an interest in scholarly activity are welcome
to participate in collaborative projects, including clinical
research, study design, enrollment of clinical cases in research
trials, and manuscript preparation. New Bolton Center's active
research community provides opportunities for involvement at a
level that complements each faculty member's clinical and
educational interests.
The successful candidate has the potential to access the clinical,
teaching, and research units on the campus, including the
Veterinary School's 200-cow
Marshak Dairy and the 250-sow
Penn Swine Teaching & Research Center. The Advanced Imaging
and Translational Center, currently in the pre-construction phase,
will provide state-of-the-art imaging modalities such as 3T MRI,
multi-axis mobile-gantry CT, and intra-operative CT. Opportunities
exist for interaction and collaboration with other initiatives and
departments, including the
Center for Stewardship Agriculture and Food Security,
Pathobiology,
Wildlife Futures, and core laboratories.
Located in the heart of Chester County's horse country, Kennett
Square offers an appealing blend of rural beauty and small-town
charm. The area's rich equestrian tradition, farms, and vibrant
community create opportunities to pursue interests outside of work,
from riding and local competitions to exploring the scenic
countryside. A welcoming downtown with restaurants and shops, along
with convenient access to Philadelphia and Wilmington, makes
Kennett Square a rewarding place to live and build a career.
Qualifications
Requirements include a DVM/VMD or equivalent degree, and board
certification or eligibility in either the ACVAA or ECVAA. Salary
and rank will be commensurate with qualifications and
experience.
Application Instructions
Application review will begin immediately, and applications will be
considered until the positions are filled. Questions about the
position can be directed to Dr. Billy I. Smith, Search Committee
Chair, by email at bis@vet.upenn.edu.
To apply, visit https://apply.interfolio.com/196293
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
The University of Pennsylvania is an equal opportunity employer.
Candidates are considered for employment without regard to race,
color, sex, sexual orientation, religion, creed, national origin
(including shared ancestry or ethnic characteristics), citizenship
status, age, disability, veteran status or any class protected
under applicable federal, state, or local law.

in the clinical environment. The successful candidate will
contribute to the clinical, teaching, and research missions of the
Section of Anesthesia at New Bolton Center. The Section is home to
four diplomates of the American or European Colleges of Veterinary
Anesthesia and Analgesia, and to three anesthesia technicians. Five

their time between Penn Vet's Matthew J. Ryan Veterinary Hospital

Center.

growing research program, focused on cardiovascular and respiratory
physiology and pathophysiology, advanced pain management and
pharmacology. Candidates are encouraged to pursue scholarly
activities in areas relevant to their interests and expertise. A
rich collaborative environment provides opportunities for
interdisciplinary research within Penn Vet and the broader
University of Pennsylvania community, as well as with veterinary

jobs.description:
Assistant/Associate Professor (Open Rank) - Electrical &
Computer Engineering
Job Class Code:
FLSA:
Posting Number: FRGV2090
Location: Rio Grande Valley, Texas
Division/Organization: Provost - Academic Affairs
Appointment Period for Non-Tenure Position:
Tenure Status: Tenure Track
FTE: 1.0
Scope of Job:
The Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering (ECE) at the
University of Texas Rio Grande Valley (UTRGV) seeks applicants for
one (1) faculty position in the broad area of Electrical
Engineering. The department will consider all qualified candidates;
however, preference will be given to candidates who can enhance the
department's electrical and computer engineering capabilities in
the areas of 1) power and energy or 2) communication and/or
microelectronics. The successful candidate is expected to start in
Fall 2027.
The ECE department at UTRGV enrolls over 1000 undergraduate
students in the ABET-accredited BSEE and BSCE undergraduate
programs and 43 master's students in the MSE program. Successful
candidates are expected to show a strong commitment to teaching
excellence, mentoring students at the undergraduate and graduate
levels, and conducting research and publishing scholarly materials
at the two main campuses where the ECE department is located. UTRGV
is moving toward Carnegie Classification as an R1 university soon,
and we will evaluate candidates on their ability to support this
effort. The College of Engineering & Computer Science has an
interdisciplinary PhD program in Materials Science and Engineering
and several centers in which the successful candidate can
participate as appropriate: the Center for Advanced Manufacturing
Innovation and Cyber Systems (CAMICS), the Center for
Nanotechnology, the Center for Multidisciplinary Research
Excellence in Cyber-Physical Infrastructure Systems (MECIS), the
University Transportation Center for Railway Safety (UTCRS), and
the Industrial Training and Assessment Center. Please visit our
website at www.utrgv.edu/ece/.
The position is for a tenure-track assistant professor; however, an
exceptional candidate may be considered for credit toward time on
the tenure track or for appointment as associate professor.
About UTRGV: UTRGV serves the Rio
Grande Valley and beyond via an innovative and unique multicultural
education dedicated to student access and success. By championing
leading research, healthcare, and application of university
discoveries, we support sustainable development, community
engagement, and well-being. The University of Texas Rio Grande
Valley (UTRGV) is committed to building and sustaining a highly
qualified and talented faculty to pursue excellence in everything
that we do, including teaching, research, and service.
Drawing on our unique identity as the leading Hispanic-Serving
Institution in a bilingual and bicultural environment, UTRGV will
promote student access and success by building from strength in
education and creating a vibrant campus experience. By 2027, we
will accelerate transformation in the Rio Grande Valley and beyond
by driving meaningful advancements in research and creative works,
expanding access to high-quality and affordable healthcare, and
fostering authentic community engagement and integration.
UTRGV is a distributed campus, one university spanning four
counties and multiple locations. Our purpose is to be a university
for the entire Rio Grande Valley and beyond. Over 91% of the
students enrolled at UTRGV identify as Hispanic, making UTRGV one
of the top 3 universities with the highest percentage of Hispanic
students. For additional information, please visit UTRGV
website.
Minimum Qualifications:
Applicants must have earned a Ph.D. in Electrical and Computer
Engineering or a related field from an accredited university (at
least conferred before the start date of September 1, 2027).
Candidates at the Assistant Professor level will be considered
based on demonstrated potential to enhance the teaching and
research capabilities of the Electrical and Computer Engineering
Department. Applicants must have demonstrated evidence of potential
for independent research, skill in interdisciplinary research and
collaboration, along with the potential to develop an outstanding
research program and high-profile publications, as well as a
successful record of extramural funding.
Discipline Specific Required Qualifications:
Applicants must also have demonstrated ability (or a well-designed
plan) to develop and maintain a funded research program, and to
lead multidisciplinary collaborative projects, as well as the
ability to collaborate with faculty colleagues. The successful
candidate will demonstrate having (or potential to) achieve
excellence and balance in teaching, research, and service,
collaboration with faculty across disciplines, and the ability to
involve undergraduate students as well as graduate students in
research activities.
Preferred Qualification:
The highest consideration will be given to applicants who have
expertise in the areas of 1) power and energy or 2) communication
and/or microelectronics. Postdoctoral experience is
preferred.
Salary: Commensurate with Qualifications and
Experience
License or Certification Required?: No
Number of Vacancies: 2
Desired Start Date: 09/01/2027
EEO Statement:
It is the policy of The University of Texas Rio Grande Valley to
promote and ensure equal employment opportunities for all
individuals without regard to race, color, national origin, sex,
age, religion, disability, sexual orientation, gender identity or
expression, genetic information or protected veteran status. In
accordance with the requirements of Title VII of the Civil Rights
Act of 1964, the Title IX of the Education Amendments of 1972,
Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act of 1973, and the Americans
with Disabilities Act of 1990, as amended, our University is
committed to comply with all government requirements and ensures
non-discrimination in its education programs and activities,
including employment. We encourage women, minorities and
differently abled persons to apply for employment positions of
interest.
Open Date: 10/30/2026
Special Instructions to Applicants:
All applications must be submitted via the UTRGV application portal
at
https://careers.utrgv.edu. Complete
all sections on the application. If you are applying for the first
time, please complete all biographical information including
address, email and phone number. You may update this at any time by
selecting to edit your profile in the application. Incomplete
applications will not be considered.
Security sensitive: All UTRGV employees are required to have a
criminal background check (CBC). CBCs will be conducted for all
candidates invited for an on-campus interview.

UTRGV is a distributed institution. As such and as assigned, the
position may require presence at multiple locations throughout the
Rio Grande Valley. Work is performed primarily in a general office
environment. This position is security sensitive and thereby
subject to the provisions of the Texas Education Code §51.215. The
retirement plan for this position is Teacher Retirement System of
Texas (TRS), subject to the position being at least 20 hours per
week and at least 135 days in length. This position has the option
to elect the Optional Retirement Program (ORP) instead of TRS,
subject to the position being 40 hours per week and at least 135
days in length.

or internet-based of 61) on the Test of English as a Foreign
Language (TOEFL) or a satisfactory test score of 6.0 on the
International English Language Testing System (IELTS).
Incomplete applications will not be considered. All positions are
subject to budget approval.

Job Details
Faculty, Assistant or Associate Professor - Public
Policy
Salary: Depends on Qualifications
Job Type: FT Faculty

Closing: 11/29/2026 11:59 PM Mountain
Location: Main Campus - Orem

Position Announcement
The History and Political Science Department (HPS) at Utah Valley
University (UVU), housed in the College of Humanities and Social
Sciences (CHSS), invites applicants for a tenure-track Assistant or
Associate Professor position in Public Policy. The standard
teaching load for tenure-track faculty at UVU is four courses per
semester. The successful candidate will collaborate with faculty to
develop and establish curriculum, activities, processes, and
resources that support students' development of public policy
knowledge, skills, and values. The successful candidate will teach
lower-division courses as needed by the department and
upper-division courses in Public Policy or Public Administration,
with a preference for those candidates who can teach our Policy
Analysis course. The policy specialty is open, but expertise in
areas such as environmental, housing, energy, or transportation
policy is desired. The candidate may have the option to teach in
the online Master of Public Administration program within the
College of Health and Public Service (CHPS).
UVU offers extensive resources and workshops to expand and enhance
teaching abilities. The successful candidate is expected to use
pedagogical methods that emphasize student engagement, identify
measurable course objectives, and evaluate learning using methods
appropriate to the discipline. The successful candidate will have
opportunities to partner with various campus institutes (including,
but not limited to, the Gary R. Herbert Institute of Public
Policy). UVU values broad perspectives and seeks to provide a
respectful, safe atmosphere in our program.
HPS at UVU currently serves nearly 300 Political Science majors and
teaches thousands through required general education courses. Our
approach to education is student-centered and demands a high level
of faculty-student engagement, with substantial institutional
support for engaging students in faculty research. CHSS and the
institution support a strong work-life balance.
UVU, the state's largest public university, sits at the base of
Mount Timpanogos in the Wasatch Range amid a spectacular landscape
in Orem, Utah. Its main campus is just minutes from Provo Canyon
and Sundance Ski Resort, and a short drive from Salt Lake
City.
Summary of Responsibilities
Teach a standard tenure-track faculty load of four courses per
semester, including lower-division political science and public
policy courses as needed by the department. Teach upper-division
courses in Public Policy and/or Public Administration.
Develop and deliver instruction in Policy Analysis, if
qualified. Teach courses in specialized policy areas such as
environmental, housing, energy, transportation, or related public
policy fields.
Collaborate with department faculty to develop, enhance, and
assess Public Policy curriculum. Assist in establishing academic
programs, processes, activities, and resources that support student
learning and success in Public Policy.
Utilize effective, student-centered teaching practices that
promote engagement and learning. Teach in a variety of
instructional formats, including face-to-face, hybrid, online, and
large-enrollment courses.
Maintain expertise in current scholarship and emerging
developments within Public Policy, Public Administration, and
Political Science. Conduct scholarly research and disseminate
findings through presentations, publications, and other
professional activities.
Engage in ongoing professional development related to teaching,
research, leadership, and disciplinary expertise. Mentor
undergraduate students and incorporate them into research and
scholarly activities where appropriate.
Supervise and support student-driven research projects.
Participate in department, college, and university service
activities, including committee work and program development
initiatives.
Collaborate with colleagues across departments and colleges to
advance interdisciplinary teaching and learning opportunities.
Potentially teach graduate-level courses in the online Master of
Public Administration program within the College of Health and
Public Service.
Contribute to a positive academic environment that supports
students with various educational experiences, abilities, and
backgrounds. Effectively communicate complex public policy concepts
to students, colleagues, and external audiences through oral and
written communication.
Qualifications / Licenses / Certifications
Graduation from a regionally accredited university with an
earned doctoral degree in Political Science, Public Administration,
or Public Policy.
Ph.D. in Political Science or Public Policy or a related field
must be completed by the date of appointment.
Candidates must have a minimum of 2 years' experience in
teaching at the university level.
Evidence of college-level teaching (including the role of
TA)
Candidates who are ABD will be considered if they complete the
doctorate (dissertation defended and accepted by the graduating
institution) by June 30, 2027.
Preferred Qualifications:
Previous teaching experience at the college level in one or
more of the following areas:
Public Policy
Public Administration
Demonstrate the ability to teach a course on Policy
Analysis
Demonstrate the ability to teach in policy areas such as
environmental, housing, transportation, and energy policy
Frequent and consistent engagement in professional development
activities (including, but not limited to, teaching, research,
methods, and leadership).
Demonstrate the ability to mentor and conduct research with
undergraduate students.
Ability to teach online courses.
Required Application Materials:
Cover Letter
CV
Teaching Philosophy
Optional Application Materials:
Sample Syllabi
Teaching Evaluations
Research Statement
Knowledge / Skills / Abilities
Knowledge
Knowledge and skills in public policy, instructional theory,
methods strategies and techniques.
Knowledge of and demonstrated use of engaged teaching
techniques.
Knowledge of and openness to multiple approaches to teaching
political science.
Skills
Demonstrable teaching experience in an environment that
features a student body with different abilities and educational
backgrounds.
Skilled in effective oral and written communication, including
the ability to communicate to different audiences
Abilities
Ability to remain familiar with and contribute to advancing
current scholarship in political science and communicate scholarly
work through presentations and publications
Ability to include undergraduate researchers in scholarly
activities and supervise student-driven research.
Ability to effectively teach by implementing appropriate
pedagogy, clear presentation and preparation, and maintaining a
student-centered approach to education.
Ability and willingness to teach face-to-face, hybrid, online,
and large classes (60+)
EEO Statement:
UVU employment decisions are made on the basis of an applicant's
qualifications and ability to perform the job without regard to
race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation,
gender identity, gender expression, age (40 and over), disability,
veteran status, pregnancy, childbirth, or pregnancy-related
conditions, genetic information, or other bases protected by
applicable federal, state, or local law.

Assistant Professor Civil Engineering and Construction
Job ID: 305406
Location: Statesboro, Georgia
Full/Part Time: Full Time

About Us
Georgia Southern University is the state's largest and most
comprehensive center of higher learning south of Atlanta, and one
of the most dynamic public universities in the Southeast.
Founded in 1906, Georgia Southern has grown from a
single-purpose college into a Carnegie Doctoral/R2 institution with
149 degree programs at the bachelor's, master's and doctoral
levels, serving 31,600 students from all 50 states, Washington
D.C., Puerto Rico and more than 100 nations.
Four distinct campuses extend Georgia Southern's reach across
the region: a 900-acre quintessential college campus in Statesboro,
anchored by Georgian-style red-brick buildings set among oaks and
pines; the Armstrong Campus in Savannah, minutes from historic
downtown and a short drive from the beaches of Tybee Island; a
modern, purpose-built facility in Hinesville serving local and
military-affiliated students; and the East Georgia Campus in
Swainsboro, an outdoor oasis nestled on a 385-acre pine forest,
offering expanded pathways to higher education for students across
southeast Georgia.
Through ten colleges, the Allen E. Paulson College of
Engineering and Computing, the College of Arts and Humanities, the
College of Behavioral and Social Sciences, the College of
Education, the College of Science and Mathematics, the Jack N.
Averitt College of Graduate Studies, the Jiann-Ping Hsu College of
Public Health, the Parker College of Business, the Waters College
of Health Professions and University College, Georgia Southern
delivers academic programs backed by real-world experience,
research with regional and national impact, and a faculty committed
to helping every student go further than they thought possible.
Accredited by the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools
Commission on Colleges and holding specialized accreditation across
its professional programs, Georgia Southern prepares graduates who
are ready to lead, contribute and soar beyond, in Georgia, across
the nation and around the world.
For more information, visit GeorgiaSouthern.edu.
Location
Georgia Southern University, a public Carnegie Doctoral/R2 with
a Carnegie Community Engagement classification, offers
approximately 149 different degree programs serving nearly 31,600
students through 11 colleges on four campuses in Savannah,
Hinesville, Statesboro, Swainsboro and online instruction. Founded
in 1906, Georgia Southern is a leader in higher education in
southeast Georgia with expert faculty and a focus on public impact
research and engaging learning opportunities through knowledge and
know-how that prepare our students to soar beyond and take
ownership of their lives, careers and communities. Visit GeorgiaSouthern.edu.
Statesboro
Campus
1332 Southern Drive
Statesboro, GA 30458
Department Information
Within this
setting, the Department of Civil Engineering and Construction is
committed to preparing students for leadership roles in the
planning, design, and management of integrated infrastructure
systems that are critical to society. Our mission emphasizes
experiential learning, research, and community engagement that
address regional and global challenges in construction, civil
infrastructure, and the built environment. Looking ahead, the
Department is committed to expanding its research capacity in
resilient and sustainable infrastructure, advancing the integration
of digital technologies in design and construction, and preparing
the next generation of experts to meet the nation's growing
infrastructure and renewal needs.
The two faculty
hired through this search will play a pivotal role in shaping that
future. With campuses on Georgia's coast and in its rural interior,
and considering the rapid industrial and infrastructure growth
across Southeast Georgia, this university offers a living
laboratory for research that pairs AI and digital technologies with
structures, materials, water, and resilience. The university is
located in the heavily forested region of Southeast Georgia.
Involvement of the successful candidate in research involving
forestry and forest products, and sustainably harnessing its
economic potential will be considered positively in the hiring
process. The new faculty will strengthen interdisciplinary
collaboration, expand graduate education (including PhD-level
research), and help position Georgia Southern University as a
leader in solutions for America's new and aging infrastructure. The
new faculty is expected to develop a vibrant, funded research
portfolio, partly in collaboration with the research cluster on
sustainable communities.
Job Summary
Reporting to the
Department Chair, the positions require teaching undergraduate and
graduate courses, advising students, developing and sustaining an
externally funded research program, and providing service to the
department, college, university, and profession. The successful
candidates will teach in assigned areas, with courses not limited
to typical Civil and Construction Engineering ones. They may
include Graphics, Plane Surveying, Building Information Modeling,
Project Planning and Scheduling, and Construction Administration.
Faculty may develop new courses aligned with their expertise. The
successful candidates will also mentor undergraduate and graduate
students, support accreditation and assessment efforts, and
actively engage in professional societies. The positions are
tenure-track, 10-month academic year appointments.
Required Qualifications
Earned doctorate in Civil
Engineering, Construction Engineering, Construction Management,
Environmental Engineering, or a closely related field with at least
18 graduate semester hours in Civil Engineering, Construction
Engineering, Construction Management, or Environmental Engineering
by August 1, 2027.
Expertise in engineering and
artificial intelligence, with a proven record of multidisciplinary
work that improves infrastructure, strengthens community resilience
and safety, and advances sustainable resource management.
Evidence of research productivity in
one or more of the following areas, with particular interest in
candidates who apply AI and digital technologies across them:
Resilient and Sustainable
Infrastructure: sustainable communities, coastal sustainability and
resilience, clean water, and smart and resilient cities.
Intelligent Structures and Materials:
computational structural engineering, advanced and sustainable
construction materials (e.g., forestry and engineered wood
products), and AI and data-driven modeling of structural and
material performance.
Digital Construction and Automation:
civil and building information modeling (BIM), digital twins,
automation and robotics, and AI applications such as machine
learning, computer vision, and generative AI in construction
engineering and management.
Lean and Data-Driven Project
Delivery: lean principles and practices and AI-enabled planning,
scheduling, and project controls.
Geospatial Sensing and Analytics:
surveying and geomatics (geodesy, photogrammetry, LiDAR, remote
sensing, and GIS) and AI-driven geospatial analytics for
construction and infrastructure.
Credentials to teach undergraduate
and graduate courses in construction management and civil
engineering.
Demonstrated ability or potential to
secure external research funding.
Commitment to engaging with best
practice initiatives in instruction and pedagogy, mentoring, and
curriculum design and development.
Demonstrated strong and sustained
commitment to advancing a robust research and scholarship agenda,
including the production of peer-reviewed research and creative
works appropriate to the discipline.
Willingness to engage with
institutional student success initiatives.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience preparing or contributing
to research proposals for external funding (federal, state, or
industry).
Evidence of collaborative research
activity, particularly with faculty or interdisciplinary teams.
Exposure to or involvement with
undergraduate and graduate student mentoring or supervision (e.g.,
assisting with MS/PhD student projects, co-authoring papers).
Active funded research portfolio,
especially federal and industry funding
Active research at the intersection
of forestry and civil or environmental engineering, such as forest
hydrology, timber structures, or post-fire watershed response.
One or more years of postdoctoral
experience.
Professional engineering license is
desired but not required.
Proposed Salary
Commensurate with experience.
This is an
exempt position paid on a monthly basis.
Required Documents to Attach
A complete application consists of
the following:
Letter of application addressing the
candidate's qualifications and fit with the position(s) and naming
the position(s) of interest.
Curriculum vitae.
Research statement (2 pages max)
outlining current work and future plans, including potential for
external funding.
Teaching statement (1 page max)
describing instructional philosophy, experience, and interests in
courses aligned with Construction Management and Construction/Civil
Engineering.
Names, telephone numbers, and email
addresses of at least three (3) professional references.
Additionally, after submitting the
above documents, applicants may be asked to complete a brief
questionnaire summarizing their qualifications via a Google
form.
Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities
ABILITIES
Consistently exhibit engaging
customer service

constituencies served by the University

digital tools for instruction and research
KNOWLEDGE

procedures to meet Institutional goals and support the University's

SKILLS

communication (verbal and written), organizational, and human
relations skills

The Department of Psychology and Counseling at The University of
Texas at Tyler invites applications for an Assistant Professor of
Counseling to start in the Spring of 2027 or Fall of 2027. This is
a full-time tenure-track position with a nine-month academic year
appointment in the clinical mental health counseling (CMHC) program
in the Department of Psychology and Counseling within the School of
Health Professions at the University of Texas at Tyler.
Key Responsibilities
Pursue an active scholarly research agenda
Teach graduate courses in counseling
Supervise CMHC students in their internship and practicum
coursework
Advise counseling students
Provide service to the counseling profession at a local, state,
and/or national levels, and participate collaboratively in program,
department, college and university governance.

An earned a doctorate in counselor education (preference given
to applicants with a degree earned from a CACREP-accredited
program)
Professional experience and research expertise in counseling
and supervision in clinical settings
Evidence of university teaching and research activity
appropriate for an assistant professor candidate.
The ideal candidate will have demonstrated a strong
professional counselor identity, the ability to conduct a focused
and sustained program of research and scholarship, experience
teaching graduate students, and strong interpersonal skills.
Additionally, applicants should have a license or be license
eligible in Texas.

About The University of Texas at Tyler
The University of Texas at Tyler is part of the prestigious
University of Texas System that includes 14 institutions located
throughout the state. Founded in 1971, UT Tyler today enrolls
10,000 students and consists of six colleges.
Designated an R2 research institution by the Carnegie
Classification of Institutions of Higher Education, UT Tyler
supports our surrounding region through innovation intended to
uplift communities, spearhead sustainability initiatives, preserve
ecosystems and support entrepreneurship. UT Tyler has the highest
Carnegie classification in East Texas.
Our beautiful Tyler campus features more than 200 acres nestled
along a lake and surrounded by thick pine and oak forests,
providing a picturesque location for study and recreation. We also
offer instructional sites at The University of Texas Health Science
Center at Tyler and in Palestine, Longview, and Houston.
With more than 80 bachelor's, master's and doctoral degree programs
offered, UT Tyler provides a wealth of learning opportunities and
dynamic programs.

assist people with disabilities in living full lives, the School of

Position Announcement
The Department of Social and Behavioral Sciences in the College of
Humanities and Social Sciences at Utah Valley University invites
applications for tenure-track faculty positions in Social Work at
the assistant, associate, or full professor rank. Appointments will
begin in August 2027.
These positions provide an exciting opportunity to contribute to
the continued growth and development of UVU's Bachelor of Social
Work (BSW) and Master of Social Work (MSW) programs. Both programs
are fully accredited by the Council on Social Work Education
(CSWE).
UVU's social work programs provide effective instruction and
mentorship to students with varied educational backgrounds and life
experiences; maintain a respectful, professional, and
student-centered learning environment; use teaching practices and
course materials appropriate to the course learning outcomes and
applicable accreditation standards; and work professionally with
students, colleagues, and community partners.
The successful candidate will collaborate with social work faculty
in developing and establishing curriculum, activities, processes,
resources, and policies that support student development of social
work knowledge, skills, and values. The appointee's workload
expectations will be teaching (80%), research (10%), and
institutional service (10%). The position carries a teaching load
of 24 credit hours or equivalent per academic year, typically 12
credits per semester (4/4).
UVU offers extensive resources and professional-development
workshops to support and enhance teaching effectiveness. The
successful candidate will use pedagogical approaches that promote
student engagement, establish measurable course learning
objectives, and assess student learning through written
assignments, oral and/or skills-based assessments, examinations,
and other appropriate evaluation methods.
The successful candidate will collaborate professionally with
faculty and staff to support the well-being and continued
development of the social work programs, the Department of Social
and Behavioral Sciences, the College of Humanities and Social
Sciences, Utah Valley University, and its students and employees. A
commitment to collegiality, collaboration, and student success is
essential
The successful candidate is expected to uphold the professional
mission, purpose, and ethics of the social work profession and
comply with applicable university policies and legal
requirements.
Summary of Responsibilities
Teaching courses in the Social Work Discipline.
Plans, prepares, and follows an approved course of study with
measurable objectives and student outcomes for each course taught.
Prepares all instructional materials (to include course syllabi,
exams, readings, instructions, visual aids, and other materials) in
electronic and paper formats. Maintains and submits accurate and
current records concerning student accountability, attendance, and
performance. Maintains office hours and upholds a student-centered
approach to education.
University and community service.
Research and scholarly projects.
Qualifications / Licenses / Certifications
Doctoral degree in social work (PhD, DSW) or related
discipline, master's in social work from a CSWE-accredited program,
and two years of post-MSW social work practice experience.
Demonstrated commitment to social work education, including
preparation of students/supervisees for ethical, competent, and
effective professional practice.
Evidence of effective teaching, training, mentoring, or student
support in social work education or closely related settings.
Commitment to continuous improvement in teaching, including use
of student feedback, assessment data, and professional
development.
Demonstrated record of professional reliability, organization,
accountability, and timely completion of assigned
responsibilities.
Recent scholarly activity (within 5 years) or extensive
practice experience.
Please note: If the MSW was earned from an
international institution, the candidate is responsible for having
the degree evaluated and approved by CSWE. ABD candidates will be
considered; however, the doctoral degree must be conferred by the
time of appointment (August 2027).
If hired at the associate or full professor rank, the candidate
must have evidence of rank achievement, recent scholarly work and
continued agenda (publications, conference presentations, etc.),
achievement in teaching, and evidence of ongoing institutional
service.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience serving as the instructor of record in a social work
program.
Experience working effectively with under-resourced
populations.
Experience collaborating on program development, curriculum
revision, accreditation self-study, assessment, or strategic
planning.
Experience using technology in social work practice or
education.
Expertise in macro social work practice, addiction treatment,
and/or research instruction, particularly for MSW-program
teaching.
Leadership experience in a growing academic program, social
service agency, or related organization.
Required Application Materials:
A cover letter addressing the required and preferred
qualifications
A curriculum vitae
Transcripts for degrees: MSW, doctoral, etc.
Teaching statement/philosophy
Teaching evaluations for all courses where the applicant was
the instructor of record (if full-time faculty, the last 3 years
are sufficient)
Professional licensure or certification documentation, if
applicable
Contact information for three professional references
Knowledge / Skills / Abilities
Knowledge
Social work theory, practice, policy, and research across the
social work curriculum.
Professional social work ethics, values, and applicable
standards of practice.
Council on Social Work Education (CSWE) Education Policy and
Accreditation Standards.
Learning management systems (e.g., Canvas) and instructional
technology used in higher education.
Principles and methods of student learning assessment and
competency-based education.
Skills
Design, organize, and deliver effective in-person and online
course content.
Use engaged-learning pedagogies, instructional strategies, and
educational technology.
Apply course content to contemporary social work practice with
individuals, families, groups, organizations, and communities.
Facilitate respectful, productive learning conversations about
complex or challenging social work topics.
Develop and use assessment measures to evaluate student
learning outcomes and competencies.
Communicate effectively, orally and in writing, with students,
faculty, staff, agency administrators, and community partners.
Plan, prioritize, and manage multiple teaching, assessment,
accreditation, scholarship, service, and student-support
responsibilities.
Abilities
Work collaboratively and productively with faculty, staff,
students, community partners, and external stakeholders.
Participate constructively in collaborative decision-making,
shared governance, and program development.
Contribute positively to a collegial, student-centered, and
growing academic program.
Meet established deadlines and complete assigned
responsibilities reliably and professionally.
Exercise sound judgment, accountability, and follow-through in
teaching, service, and other faculty responsibilities.
Reflect on teaching practice and use feedback and assessment
results to improve instruction.
Adapt teaching and communication approaches to support students
with varied educational backgrounds and learning needs.
EEO Statement:
UVU employment decisions are made on the basis of an applicant's
qualifications and ability to perform the job without regard to
race, color, religion, national origin, sex, sexual orientation,
gender identity, gender expression, age (40 and over), disability,
veteran status, pregnancy, childbirth, or pregnancy-related
conditions, genetic information, or other bases protected by
applicable federal, state, or local law.
To apply, please visit https://www.schooljobs.com/careers/uvu/jobs/5529901/faculty-assistant-professor-msw-bsw-programs

Job Details
Assistant Professor, Entertainment and Hospitality
Management
Department of Management
College of Business and Economics
Assistant Professor
Fall 2027
The Department of Management at California State University,
Fullerton, invites applications for a tenure‐track Assistant
Professor position in Entertainment and Hospitality Management with
an appointment to begin Fall 2027.
Equal Opportunity and Excellence in Education and
Employment
This position is open and available to all
regardless of race, sex, color, ethnicity or national origin.
Consistent with California law and federal civil rights laws,
California State University, Fullerton (CSUF) provides equal
opportunity in education and employment without unlawful
discrimination or preferential treatment based on race, sex, color,
ethnicity, or national origin. Our commitment to equal opportunity
means ensuring that every student and employee has access to the
resources and support they need to thrive and succeed in a
university environment and in their communities. CSUF complies with
Title VI of the Civil Rights Act of 1964, Title IX of the Education
Amendments of 1972, the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA),
Section 504 of the Rehabilitation Act, the California Equity in
Higher Education Act, California's Proposition 209 (Art. I, Section
31 of the California Constitution), other applicable state and
federal anti-discrimination laws, and CSU's Nondiscrimination
Policy. We prohibit discriminatory preferential treatment,
segregation based on race or any other protected status, and all
forms of discrimination, harassment, and retaliation in all
university programs, policies, and practices.
In addition, California State University, Fullerton is a leading
public university known for its strong academic programs and
commitment to student success. As one of the largest campuses in
the CSU system, Cal State Fullerton fosters innovation,
collaboration, and professional growth. The university values
teaching, research, and service, creating an environment where
students, staff, and faculty can thrive. Cal State Fullerton is a
designated Hispanic-Serving Institution and an Asian American and
Native American Pacific Islander-Serving Institution. The
university also received the prestigious Seal of Excelencia in 2021
and 2024 from Excelencia in Education, the nation's leading
authority on Latinx student success. Cal State Fullerton is an
equal opportunity employer with a diverse student population of
over 45,000 and a faculty and staff population of 4,000. Cal State
Fullerton is firmly committed to helping students achieve academic
excellence, career success, and economic mobility. Joining Cal
State Fullerton means becoming part of a dynamic team dedicated to
making a meaningful impact. We continuously seek individuals from
various disciplines who share the university's mission and core
values. We welcome you to consider joining the Titan community.
CSUF is committed to retaining all faculty and has established
affinity groups you can join to support your success.
Position
CSUF faculty are teacher-scholars
who bring research and creative discovery into the classroom and
into individually mentored student experiences. They teach broadly
in their programs, advise and mentor students, and contribute
through service to the department, college, university, profession,
and community.
The successful candidate will teach introductory and advanced
courses in Entertainment and Hospitality Management and may
contribute to other Management courses as assigned. Courses may
include Entertainment Business, Entertainment Money Management,
Entertainment Operations, Hospitality and Tourism Management, Music
Business, Sport Management, and related subjects. The search is
broad. Candidates whose teaching, research, or professional
experience relates to entertainment, hospitality, tourism,
services, sport, media, music, events, or related management
settings may be considered. The successful candidate will maintain
an active program of peer-reviewed scholarship appropriate for
tenure; advise and mentor students; and participate in department,
college, university, and professional service. The candidate may
also contribute to the Center for Entertainment and Hospitality
Management and to industry, alumni, or community engagement.
Required Qualifications
A Ph.D. or equivalent terminal doctorate in management,
hospitality or tourism management, service management, sport
management, entertainment, media or music business, or another
closely related field from an accredited institution by the time of
appointment. ABD applicants may apply if all degree requirements
will be completed before the appointment begins.
Academic, research, teaching, and/or professional preparation
relevant to Entertainment and Hospitality Management.
Demonstrated commitment to and potential for excellence in
university teaching.
A record of, or clear potential for, peer-reviewed scholarly
accomplishments appropriate to the rank of Assistant
Professor.
Ability to balance responsibilities in teaching, scholarship,
and service.
Potential to use technology and evidence-based teaching
practices effectively.
Ability and commitment to communicate and work effectively with
students, staff, faculty, and external partners in a culturally and
professionally varied environment.
Demonstrated commitment to student success and inclusive
excellence.
Preferred Qualifications
Professional or industry experience in entertainment,
hospitality, tourism, sport, media, music, events, services, or a
related sector.
Experience developing productive relationships with industry,
professional associations, alumni, or community organizations.
Ability to contribute across more than one area of the
Entertainment and Hospitality Management curriculum.
Application
A complete online application
must be received by electronic submission to be considered. To
apply, please visit http://hr.fullerton.edu/workforce/careers.html,
choose full-time faculty, search for the position
561480, and provide the following required
materials:
Cover letter addressing the required and preferred
qualifications.
Curriculum vitae.
Graduate transcripts (unofficial copies are sufficient for
initial review).
Research statement describing current work, methodological
preparation, and the future scholarly agenda.
Teaching statement describing teaching preparation,
learning-centered practices, and approaches to supporting student
success.
Up to two representative scholarly publications, manuscripts,
or working papers combined into one PDF.
Candidate statement on commitment to inclusive excellence (no
more than 500 words):
Inclusive excellence
is a strategic framework that recognizes the importance of
diversity, equity, and inclusion in achieving organizational
success and high-quality learning and teaching. It's a way of
thinking and acting that integrates these values into all aspects
of an institution, from curriculum and pedagogy to recruitment and
hiring. Essentially, it means that excellence is not just about
achieving high standards, but also about ensuring that all members
of the community have the opportunity to thrive and contribute
(Williams et al., 2005).
With the Inclusive Excellence Statement, we aim to learn about
the applicant's perspective on their past and present contributions
to and future aspirations for promoting and engaging with a diverse
student population. This statement should showcase the candidate's
professional experience, intellectual commitments, and/or
willingness to teach and create an academic environment supportive
of all students, including but not limited to those of diverse
ages, abilities, cultures, ethnicities, gender identities,
languages, religions, and sexual orientations.
Cal State Fullerton
serves a student body that reflects the rich cultural, ethnic, and
socioeconomic mosaic of Southern California. Please provide
concrete examples of how you, as a faculty member, will support our
students in one or more of the following areas, which fall under
the areas of awareness and understanding, experience and
commitment, and future plans.
Your contributions (past, present, or future) to embedding
perspectives that are reflective of the student population into
your teaching and/or scholarship.
Your experience in service activities that are reflective of a
diverse student population.
Your experience and commitment to mentoring and providing
opportunities to a diverse student body inside and outside the
classroom environment.
Your experience integrating creative activities that are
inclusive of the identities of our student body and
communities.
A list of three professional references, including name, title,
email address, telephone number, and the candidate's professional
relationship to each reference:
Finalists must submit three letters of
recommendation. Please have these ready for the referents to
submit. On the References page of the online application, enter
information and email addresses for three referents who will
provide a confidential letter of reference for your application. At

inclusive of the identities of our student body and
