jobs.title: Assistant Professor in Transportation Engineering (Tenure Track)
jobs.institution: University of Washington, Department of Civil & Environmental Engineering
jobs.description:
The Department of Civil and Environmental Engineering (CEE) at the University of Washington invites applications for a faculty position at the rank of Assistant Professor (Tenure Track), with an anticipated start date of September, 2027. The location of this position is on the University of Washington campus in Seattle, Washington. We seek applicants who demonstrate commitment to excellence in research, teaching, and service in a diverse and inclusive academic community. The successful candidate will join our faculty on a full-time basis for a nine-month academic appointment, 3-year term, renewable, beginning September 16, 2027.
The base salary range for this position will be $11,500 - $13,500 per month, commensurate with experience and qualifications, or as mandated by a U.S. Department of Labor prevailing wage determination.
Positive factors for consideration include, but are not limited to, candidates with a promising record of research excellence in transportation; candidates working with emerging methods, tools, or technologies, such as artificial intelligence and machine learning, robotics and automation, new sensing and data sources, quantum applications, or directions we have not anticipated; and/or candidates who bring new areas of strength for the department. Applicants are encouraged to connect their work to one or more of the Grand Challenges identified in the Department's strategic plan.
All University of Washington faculty are expected to engage in teaching, research, and service. Our department offers a highly collegial and collaborative culture, with broad interdisciplinary research ties and opportunities. The UW has an active community of transportation researchers within CEE, the College of Engineering (CoE), and across the university. The candidate is expected to collaborate with colleagues within CEE, CoE, throughout the university, and externally; and to develop an externally funded research program. In teaching, the candidate will support and expand transportation course offerings at the undergraduate and graduate levels. In all aspects of this position, the candidate will be expected to contribute to a welcoming and inclusive environment in research, teaching, mentoring, and service.

jobs.title: Global Hispanophone Studies and Digital Humanitie at the rank of Assist. Professor–Assoc. Professor
jobs.institution: Department of Modern Languages and Literatures
jobs.description:
The Michele Bowman Underwood Department of Modern Languages and Literatures in the College of Arts and Sciences at the University of Miami invites applications for one faculty appointment in Spanish, in the field of Global Hispanophone Studies with additional expertise in Digital Humanities. The tenure-track/tenure-eligible appointment will be at the rank of Assistant Professor or Associate Professor and would begin August 15, 2027. We seek a dynamic scholar whose research and teaching focuses on Global Hispanophone Studies working on Spain with a comparative trans-Atlantic (including Latin America), African, Pacific, Asian, and/or transnational approach, including migration, economic and cultural flows from the Maghreb and sub-Saharan Africa into Spain, and from Latin America and Europe to Asia. Beyond expertise in Global Hispanophone Studies and Digital Humanities, areas of scholarly interest may include cultural analytics, critical media studies, and digital literacy. Building on the College’s strength in Digital Humanities and AI, this appointment advances global engagement, study abroad (UMadrid), experiential learning, interdisciplinary research, and innovative scholarship through digital projects and publications across the literary, visual, and cultural productions of the Global Hispanophone. It also prepares students to engage critically and ethically with emerging technologies and strengthens digital literacy.
We particularly encourage applications from candidates whose research explores the intersections of media, politics, the arts (including visual arts, film, literature, etc.), and digital culture in the Global Hispanophone. Applicants whose work bridges languages, regions, or disciplines – such as comparative/critical media studies, visual culture, or global DH – are especially welcome. The candidate will teach undergraduate and graduate courses in Spanish on the literary, visual, and cultural productions of the Global Hispanophone, as well as courses (in English and Spanish) in Digital Media Studies, Cultural Studies, or related interdisciplinary areas. Additional responsibilities include advising at all levels of the program, and service on departmental and university committees.
Qualifications:
Ph.D. in Spanish, Comparative Literature, Digital Humanities, Cultural Studies, Media Studies, or a closely related field by the time of appointment. ACTFL Superior level fluency in Spanish and English. Demonstrated excellence in teaching and an active, innovative research agenda. For Associate Professor: a record of leadership, program-building, or administrative experience will be desirable.
Interested applicants must apply online through the University’s Careers Website. Applicants should compile the following into a single PDF document and upload it under the CV/Resume link: cover letter, CV, teaching statement, and research statement. Please note that a writing sample and three reference letters to be sent directly to the department may be expected for selected candidates at a later stage. Applications received on or before December 4, 2026 will be given full consideration, though the search committee will continue to accept applications until the position is filled.
For further information about the position, please contact the department Chairperson, Dr. Lillian Manzor. General information about the department can be found at the department’s website.
The University of Miami is an Equal Opportunity Employer - Females/Minorities/Protected Veterans/Individuals with Disabilities are encouraged to apply. Applicants and employees are protected from discrimination based on certain categories protected by Federal law.
The University of Miami is a vibrant research institution located at the crossroads of the Americas. Its multilingual environment fosters innovative, interdisciplinary scholarship in the humanities. The Michele Bowman Underwood Department of Modern Languages and Literatures is home to active programs across ten languages and a multilingual, interdisciplinary PhD program in Literary, Cultural, and Linguistic Studies.

Job Details
Clinical Assistant Professor of Pharmacy Practice, Acute
Care
Job Description Summary, Duties and Responsibilities, Required
Qualifications and Preferred Qualifications
The search will remain open until the position is
filled. For full consideration, applications should be
submitted by January 15, 2027. Applications
received after this date may be reviewed at the discretion of the
search committee.
________________________________________________________________________________________________________
The University of Rhode Island is the state's
flagship land and sea-grant research institution, with a commitment
to urban initiatives. A student-centered research institution, URI
actively partners with other organizations globally and locally to
advance knowledge and to develop informed residents and leaders.
URI is committed to community engagement, excellence in education,
and solving the world's most important challenges. Situated on the
traditional land and territories of the Narragansett Nation and the
Niantic People along the Atlantic Ocean, URI strives to create a
diverse and inclusive environment for researchers, teachers,
learners, and community members.
The College of Pharmacy is on the main campus in
Washington County, Rhode Island. Washington County is Rhode
Island's southernmost region, covering 100 miles of coastline and
sandy beaches along the Atlantic Ocean. The College of Pharmacy is
a welcoming and inclusive community of scholars with a vision to
"Advance Health and Transform Communities." The College community
seeks to pursue lives of service and intellectual exploration to
solve scientific challenges and deliver progressive
interdisciplinary healthcare with compassion and intention.
The Department of Pharmacy Practice and Clinical
Research prepares outstanding and compassionate
pharmacists and health outcomes specialists who excel as
clinicians, scholars, and leaders. We aim to strengthen and
diversify the practice of pharmacy. We seek a Clinical Assistant
Professor of Pharmacy committed to expanding our community of
scholars who work together and inspire one another in teaching,
research, practice, and service.
We seek applicants who are committed to embodying the College's
values. We are a people-first
community that is inclusive, accessible, equitable, and diverse,
and that respects the rights and dignity of all individuals. We
support the physical and mental well-being of our community and
value the freedom to learn, teach, conduct research, and
disseminate knowledge in service of the public good. We promote
integrity and innovation through lifelong
learning, ethical practice, research, and leadership. We also value
excellence in service, ongoing reflection, and
shared accountability as we work to strengthen the URI community
and serve Rhode Island and the broader world.
The University of Rhode Island College of Pharmacy values and
respects all individuals. We are committed to recruiting and
retaining a values-driven workforce to enhance our student
environment and the health of all people in Rhode Island, the
United States, and the world. We strongly encourage applications
from candidates who demonstrate through their efforts in teaching,
research, and engagement that create environments to promote
belonging in education and support health accessibility to improve
outcomes.
POSITION SUMMARY:
The University of Rhode Island College of Pharmacy invites
applications for a full-time, calendar-year, non-tenure-track
Clinical Assistant Professor in Pharmacy Practice, specializing in
acute care pharmacy. This shared academic-clinical position
includes approximately 32 hours per week dedicated to College of
Pharmacy responsibilities and 8 hours per week embedded at the
clinical practice site as an integrated member of the pharmacy
team. This three-year appointment, housed in the Department of
Pharmacy Practice and Clinical Research, includes responsibilities
for clinical teaching, service, and scholarly activity.
Continuation beyond the initial term is expected based on
successful performance review. Salary is commensurate with
qualifications and experience and includes a comprehensive benefits
package. The selected candidate will be expected to develop an
exemplary clinical practice model, demonstrate excellence in both
didactic and experiential teaching, provide meaningful service to
the profession, the college, and the university, and contribute to
clinically relevant scholarship.
KEY DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
• Contribute to the Doctor of Pharmacy and graduate teaching
missions of the University by mentoring and teaching graduate,
professional degree, and undergraduate required and elective
courses for the College.
• Establish and maintain a high-quality experiential training site
at a partnering healthcare institution by developing an exemplary
clinical practice model focused on acute care pharmacy.
• This will involve close collaboration with the clinical site, the
Director of Experiential Education, and the Chair of the Department
of Pharmacy Practice and Clinical Research to support advanced
pharmacy practice experiences (APPE) and interprofessional
education.
• Teach in didactic and experiential components of the Doctor of
Pharmacy curriculum, including core and elective courses related to
acute care and pharmacotherapy.
• Engage in sustained scholarly activity, including peer-reviewed
publications and presentations at regional, national, or
international professional meetings.
• Work collaboratively with patients and their families,
pharmacists, nurses, residents, faculty, physicians, and other
health professionals.
• Actively contribute to curriculum development and assessment
aligned with accreditation standards and participate in service
through committee involvement at both the College and University
levels.
OTHER DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES:
Perform other duties as assigned.
ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS:
The incumbent is not substantially exposed to adverse environmental
conditions.
QUALIFICATIONS
REQUIRED:
1. Doctor of Pharmacy degree from an
ACPE-accredited college or university.
2. Licensed or eligible for pharmacist licensure in Rhode
Island.
3. Completion of PGY1 or PGY2 pharmacy residency training or
equivalent clinical experience, generally demonstrated by a minimum
of five years of acute care pharmacy practice.
4. Demonstrated clinical expertise in acute care pharmacy
practice.
5. Eligibility to obtain or achieve board certification in pharmacy
specialties (e.g. BCPS).
6. Demonstrated strong interpersonal, oral, and written
communication skills.
PREFERRED:
1. Evidence of effective didactic, experiential, or
interprofessional teaching.
2. Experience precepting student pharmacists and/or pharmacy
residents.
3. Evidence of scholarly productivity or the potential to establish
a sustained program of scholarship.
4. Ability to contribute to teaching across a broad range of acute
care and pharmacotherapy topics.
5. Experience collaborating within interprofessional healthcare
teams.
6. Demonstrated ability to foster an inclusive and accessible
learning and clinical environment that supports the success of
individuals from varied backgrounds.
______________________________________________________________________________________________________
URI is unwavering in its commitment to equal opportunity,
community, equity, and diversity. In furtherance of its mission to
serve and support all learners as the state's public flagship
university, URI continues to expand efforts to recruit and retain a
broadly representative workforce as well as to regularly evaluate
the effectiveness of those efforts. All employment
decisions, including hiring, are made without regard to protected
status. Qualified individuals with disabilities may request a
reasonable accommodation by contacting the URI benefits office at
401-874-2416. For TTY assistance, contact R.I. Relay Services at
711.

Department Summary
The College of Arts and Sciences (CAS) is the intellectual hub of
the University of Oregon, serving nearly two-thirds of all

CAS is a dynamic and interdisciplinary academic community. Our

and advancing the mission of both the College and the

This position is in an Academic Service Unit (ASU), which houses

jobs.title: Tenure Track Assistant Professor, Experience Design
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Title: Tenure Track Assistant Professor, Experience
Design
Req ID: R0006447
Time Type: Full time
Location: Waltham, MA
Description:
Job Description Summary
The Experience Design Department at Bentley University invites
applications for a tenure track Assistant Professor position in
Experience Design, to begin 7/1/2027.
Applications are welcome from candidates who will hold a Ph.D.
by the start date and are seeking appointment at the assistant
professor level, including early-career scholars and current
assistant professors whose research and teaching align strongly
with the department's strengths in experience design (XD), user
experience (UX), human-centered design, human-computer interaction
(HCI), human factors, information design, and emerging technologies
as they relate to human-centered design.
The successful candidate will contribute to undergraduate and
graduate teaching in XD and Human Factors in Information Design
(HFID), with highest priority placed on the ability or clear
potential to teach design-focused courses in interaction design,
prototyping, and studio-based experience design, and additional
value placed on the ability to teach practice oriented research
courses. Across both design and research courses, the department
values theoretical grounding in perception, cognition, behavioral
science, engineering psychology, and human factors, as well as
clear application to experience design practice.
Strong candidates will be able to bridge research and practice,
producing impactful scholarship while preparing students to address
contemporary experience design and human-centered technology
challenges in professional settings. We welcome qualified
candidates whose paths connect academic research, professional
practice, and industry experience.
Bentley is committed to the teacher-scholar model where
teaching, scholarship, service and community engagement are
expected and valued. We seek qualified faculty who represent
diverse backgrounds, interests and talents and share a commitment
to high ethical standards and a willingness to embrace challenge
and change.
About the Experience Design Department:
The Experience Design (XD) Department is a collaborative,
interdisciplinary academic home for faculty whose work connects
design, human factors, user experience, human-centered technology,
behavioral science, and business. The department prepares
undergraduate and graduate students to design products, services,
systems, interfaces, environments, and experiences that are useful,
usable, responsible, and valuable for people, organizations, and
society.
XD at Bentley spans nearly 30 years of undergraduate, master's,
and doctoral education through the XD undergraduate degree program,
the Master of Science in Human Factors in Information Design (M.S.
HFID) program, and the experience design track within Bentley's
Executive Ph.D. in Business program. This portfolio of programs
creates opportunities for faculty to teach across levels, mentor
student research and applied projects, and contribute to the
continued development of experience design within a business
university environment.
The department's work also aligns with Bentley's growing
emphasis on technology, innovation, and entrepreneurship, including
the reimagined Adamian Academic Center, User Experience Center, and
planned spaces such as the Futures Lab and Build Lab. These
initiatives create opportunities for high-visibility student
engagement, immersive learning, prototyping, emerging technologies,
and interdisciplinary collaboration.
XD faculty connect teaching, scholarship, professional practice,
and external engagement through applied courses, sponsored
projects, research collaborations, consulting engagements, and
partnerships with organizations across the private, public, and
nonprofit sectors. The majority of HFID students are preparing for
professional careers as practitioners in UX, experience design,
product and service design, human factors, and related fields.
Across programs, students often work with ambiguous, real-world
problems and translate design methods, research insights, and
stakeholder needs into actionable recommendations, prototypes,
design strategies, and evidence-based design decisions.
About Bentley and the Area:
Bentley University, located in suburban Boston, is an AACSB and
NECHE accredited institution that enrolls approximately 5,500
students at the undergraduate, graduate, and doctoral levels.
Bentley is ranked at or near the top in several categories by US
News & World Report, including Best Regional Universities North
and Most Innovative Schools, with Bloomberg ranking Bentley in the
top 20 undergraduate business programs. Bentley's high graduation
and retention rates and top-ranked Pulsifer Career Center reflect a
commitment to student success and inclusiveness. With a strong
faculty of teacher-scholars, Bentley strives to be a "Force for
Good" through the integration of business with the arts and
sciences, and a strong emphasis on ethics and social
responsibility. Providing a stimulating academic community for
faculty, staff, and students, Bentley supports its faculty as they
pursue cutting-edge research and bring their expertise and real
world understanding into the classroom.
Minimum Qualifications:
Candidates must demonstrate:
Applicants should have a Ph.D. in a field relevant to the theory
and practice of experience design, or be scheduled to complete
their Ph.D. by September 1, 2027.
Teaching potential or experience relevant to design-focused,
studio-based, and/or practice-oriented research courses in
experience design.
Scholarly, applied research, or practice-based research agenda
connected to experience design practice.
Service potential or experience appropriate to career stage.
Relevant fields may include HCI, human factors, psychology,
cognitive science, sociology, anthropology, computer science,
engineering, design, design research, or other related fields,
provided the candidate's work has a clear connection to the theory
and practice of experience design, UX, or human-centered
design.
For teaching and scholarship, evidence may include potential
for, or a record of, effective teaching, student mentoring,
scholarly publication, applied research, practice-based research,
or related work appropriate to career stage.
Preferred Qualifications:
We do not expect candidates to meet all preferred
qualifications. Strong candidates may demonstrate fit through
varying combinations of teaching, research, applied collaboration,
and professional engagement.
Teaching expertise or experience in one or more areas such as
visual design, prototyping, interaction design, applied design
studios, making, UX/HCI, human factors, design research, usability
and evaluation, design strategy, product design, service design,
systems design, service learning, sponsored projects, or community
engaged projects.
Research expertise in one or more areas such as applied HCI
research, design methods research, UX research, usability and human
factors studies, participatory or co-design, accessibility and
inclusive design, systems design, systemic design, transition
design, human-centered AI, responsible innovation, evidence-based
design, design pedagogy, or professional design scholarship.
Professional industry experience is valued but not required, and
we welcome candidates whose paths connect industry, applied
practice, and academic work.
Candidates may demonstrate practice relevance through applied
research collaborations, sponsored projects, consulting,
community-engaged design, practitioner partnerships, translational
research, evidence-based design work, or scholarship that informs
experience design practice, industry-relevant problem solving, and
real-world impact.
We are especially interested in candidates whose teaching,
scholarship, or applied projects could contribute to
high-visibility student engagement work involving prototyping,
making, emerging technologies, community-oriented collaborations,
and campus-based innovation spaces.
Ability or clear potential to contribute to the continued
growth, visibility, and impact of experience design within a
business university environment, including collaboration,
curriculum development, graduate mentoring, external partnership,
or program-building over time.
Special Instructions to Applicants:
For full consideration, candidates should submit all five
required application components by October 15, 2026; review of
applications will begin shortly thereafter and continue until the
position is filled:
An up-to-date curriculum vitae.
A Letter of Interest describing the candidate's fit with the
Experience Design Department, including relevant teaching areas,
research agenda, applied or industry experience where relevant, and
connections between the candidate's work and experience design
practice.
A Teaching Statement describing the candidate's approach to
teaching and mentoring.
A Research Statement describing the candidate's scholarly
trajectory and current and future research agenda.
Names and contact information for three academic or professional
references. References will not be contacted without prior
notice.
Candidates are expected to submit materials that accurately
represent their own experience, accomplishments, teaching approach,
and research agenda. If generative AI or other tools are used in
preparing application materials, candidates remain responsible for
the accuracy, integrity, and authenticity of the final
submission.
The Teaching Statement should address: (1) areas the candidate
is prepared to teach or develop, especially design-focused and
practice-oriented research courses; (2) evidence of teaching
potential or effectiveness, which may include independent teaching,
teaching assistant experience, curriculum development, applied
research mentoring, studio or project based learning,
industry-engaged teaching, or mentoring of professional or graduate
students; and (3) prior or planned approaches to inclusive,
accessible, and ethical design education.
The Research Statement should address: (1) key research
questions, methods, and contributions; (2) evidence of research
productivity, which may include scholarly publications, work under
review, conference papers, abstracts, posters, proceedings, design
or research artifacts, or other research outputs; and (3)
connections between the candidate's work and experience design, UX,
human-centered design, HCI, human factors, or related areas.
The search committee may request additional materials at a later
stage, such as selected publications, design or research artifacts,
teaching materials, a portfolio, or evidence of teaching
effectiveness.
For additional information about this position, please email
Jonathan Ericson, Associate Professor and Chair, Dept. of
Experience Design, Bentley University (jericson@bentley.edu).
Pay Transparency:
At Bentley we offer a "total rewards" package designed to
attract, motivate, retain, and reward our employees. This includes
competitive compensation, robust benefits, career development and
opportunities, generous paid time off, workplace flexibility and a
positive, engaging employee experience. In alignment with the
Massachusetts Pay Transparency Act and our commitment to equity and
transparency, we're sharing the salary grade range for this role.
The grade range is based on market data and the scope of
responsibilities. Final pay will depend on your experience,
education, and other relevant qualifications.
Salary Ranges (depending on rank, qualifications and
experience):
Assistant Professor: $137,819 - $168,446
If you have questions about the salary grade range or need
additional information, please contact us at
GA_HR_Employment@bentley.edu.
Bentley University requires references checks and may conduct
other pre-employment screening.
Bentley University requires references checks and may conduct
other pre-employment screening.
DIVERSITY STATEMENT
Bentley University strives to create a campus community that
welcomes the exchange of ideas, and fosters a culture that values
differences and views them as a strength in our community.
Bentley University is an Equal Opportunity Employer, building
strength through diversity. The University is committed to building
a community of talented students, faculty and staff who reflect the
diversity of global business. We strongly encourage applications
from persons from underrepresented groups, individuals with
disabilities, covered veterans and those with diverse experiences
and backgrounds.

ABOUT US
QUALIFICATIONS JOB DESCRIPTION
About us:
Harper College was established by referendum in 1965 and opened its
doors in September 1967. Named after Dr. William Rainey Harper, a
pioneer in the junior college movement in the United States and the
first president of the University of Chicago, the College carries
forward this legacy of innovation in education.
Today, Harper College stands as one of the nation’s premier
community colleges and one of the largest, serving approximately
29,000 students annually in Chicago’s northwest suburbs. Our
academic programs are designed to prepare students for rewarding
careers and seamless transfer to four-year universities. Harper
offers a wide range of associate degree and certification programs,
advanced career tracks, workforce training, professional
development opportunities, continuing education classes,
accelerated degree options for adults, and developmental education
programs.
At Harper College, we are committed to facilitating active learning
and fostering the knowledge, critical thinking, and life/work
skills necessary for participation in our global society. We
collaborate with our community partners to enrich the intellectual,
cultural, and economic fabric of our district. We believe that
excellence in education must thrive within an ethical environment
of integrity and respect. We recognize that the strength of our
society is rooted in diversity, and it is through synergy that we
achieve excellence. Our core values—Respect, Integrity,
Collaboration, and Excellence—guide everything we do.
Aspen Prize
· For the third consecutive time, Harper College is a semifinalist
for the Aspen Prize for Community College Excellence, the nation’s
most prestigious recognition for community colleges that are
attaining high and improving levels of student success, as well as
equitable outcomes for Black and Latine students and those from
lower-income backgrounds.
· Twenty colleges are vying for the Aspen Institute College
Excellence Program’s 2026 Prize. Harper was also one of the 25
semifinalists for the 2023 prize.
Hispanic Serving Institution (HSI)
· In 2023, Harper College was designated as a Hispanic Serving
Institution (HSI) by the U.S. Department of Education.
· This designation provides federal funding to enhance educational
programs and support services for Latine and underrepresented
students.
· Latine students make up about 30% of Harper's enrollment,
reflecting the College's pride in its HSI status.
Equity and Diversity Award
· Harper College received the 2023 Equity and Diversity Award from
the Illinois Community College Trustees Association (ICCTA).
· The award honors leadership in promoting diversity, inclusion,
and equity for underrepresented groups.
· Harper previously won this award in 2017
Schedule Information: The successful candidate is expected
to teach 30 contact hours each year in the Art and Design
Department. In addition to teaching 30 contact hours per academic
year, a full-time faculty member serves on departmental, divisional
and institutional committees; holds six office hours per week (some
of which must be on campus); and pursues professional development
opportunities related to discipline and pedagogy. Evening and
weekend instruction may be required. Instruction may take place in
face to face, online, blended and flex formats.
Weeks per fiscal year: Faculty are covered under a 9-month
contract period (August thru May) – We seek a full-time colleague
to begin August 17, 2027.
This position may include additional periodic studio maintenance
and oversight duties in the Summer from May through August.
Additional compensation may be awarded for this time period.
Benefits: Health, Dental, Life & Disability Insurance;
Sick and Holiday pay; Personal Business; Educational Assistance:
Tuition Waivers at Harper & Professional Expense
Position Description and Duties:
The Art and Design Department at Harper College is actively seeking
a student-centered, diverse pool of candidates to fill a full-time
faculty position specializing in the field of Drawing Foundations
with a secondary specialization in either painting, printmaking,
animation, or digital art. Successful candidates will assume
teaching responsibilities that encompass Drawing Foundations and
courses in one or more of the following areas: painting,
printmaking, digital art, or animation. Additional responsibilities
include maintenance and supervision of the 2D studios, including
managing the budget, material ordering and inventory of studio
materials, equipment and furniture maintenance, facility upkeep,
managing hazardous waste compliance, and training and managing
adjunct faculty. This position hires, trains, and supervises lab
technicians and works cooperatively with non-credit programming at
the college.
The Art and Design Department program provides theory and training
in the skills essential to equipping students to transfer to a
four-year institution. The Art Department is composed of six
full-time faculty who teach foundation courses, painting,
sculpture, ceramics, digital photography, printmaking, figure
drawing, art history, art appreciation, and film appreciation. Our
facilities include a painting/drawing studio, printmaking facility,
a Mac lab, ceramics studios with multiple kilns, and a sculpture
area with wood and metal studios.
We are looking for candidates who are committed to teaching art
within the community college environment, maintaining a safe and
thriving 2D Foundations program, and helping the department
innovate and develop new curriculum and pathways, including
emerging and digital practices.
The successful candidate will be able to teach a wide variety of
introductory courses to students of diverse backgrounds and varying
levels of college readiness using traditional and alternative
delivery methods. We encourage interested candidates to familiarize
themselves with our course offerings. This position teaches a
standard load of fifteen (15) contact hours per semester (30
contact hours per academic year) in a variety of course modalities
and term lengths. The candidate's course load may include
reassigned time for chair/coordinator duties. Classes may be
offered in day, evening, and/or online modalities, and the
candidate may also have the opportunity to teach in the Honors
Program, Social Justice Studies Program and "linked" courses
(through the college's Learning Communities Program).
Candidates who maintain a professional studio practice and active
exhibition record are preferred.
Educational Requirements:
Master of Fine Arts (MFA) degree in an appropriate art discipline
required.
Experience Requirements:
Post-secondary teaching experience required (minimum of 3
years).
Application Review Date: Applications are accepted until the
position is filled though priority will be given to applications
received on or before January 8, 2027.
Special Notes:
*You will not be able to complete the application without attaching
the following documents:
· Cover letter
· CV/Resume, focused on teaching with evidence of studio art
practice (Does not substitute for a completed application)
· Copies of undergraduate and graduate transcripts from regionally
accredited institutions
· Teaching Portfolio
· A one-page, single-spaced statement of your teaching philosophy.
In your teaching philosophy, please include how you approach
classroom management, how you assess students, and how you use
instructional technology. How do you ensure students are prepared
for transfer or to go through an academically focused art
program?
*Official transcripts required upon hire.
*Employment is contingent upon a Criminal Background Check
*Employment Sponsorship is not available
Harper College is an Equal Opportunity Employer. We strive to
create an inclusive learning and working environment where
individual differences and identities are respected, valued and
embraced. We encourage women, people from historically
underrepresented groups, individuals with disabilities and veterans
to apply.

jobs.description:
Job Details
Department: Health & Human
PerformanceSalary: Commensurate with experience
Description:
The Department of Health and Human Performance (HHP) at the
University of Houston is seeking a community health promotion and
applied kinesiology specialist with demonstrable academic skills
for a tenure-track Assistant Professor position. This position is a
9-month appointment with summer school teaching optional.
The successful candidate will join a high-performing, high-yield
specialty designed to deliberately fortify our implementation
science core—a primary catalyst for interdisciplinary collaboration
across distinct departmental nodes, including the Center for
Neuro-Behavioral Research (CNBR), the Laboratory of Integrated
Physiology (LIP), and Sports Administration.
Qualifications:
A Ph.D. in Kinesiology, Nutrition, Behavioral Science,
Prevention Science, or a related community health promotion field
is required. Applicants must demonstrate a strong research focus
intersecting with implementation science, specifically targeting
two high-priority sub-disciplines:
• Digital Health Interventions: Utilizing mHealth, wearable
technology, and digital tracking tools to promote behavioral change
and monitor physical activity in real-time.
• Community-Based Research: Designing, implementing, and evaluating
sustainable, community-led physical activity interventions in
underserved or marginalized urban spaces. Preference will be given
to individuals who have expertise in community-engaged research in
underserved urban areas, pediatric/adolescent health promotion, and
large-scale project management (e.g., NIH R01/U54
frameworks).
Applicants are required to:
- Demonstrate strong potential to maintain an active, externally
funded research program (NIH, etc.) that strengthens/broadens our
current research areas.
- Show a consistent record of disseminating scholarly work through
publications in high-impact journals and presentations at major
scientific meetings.
- Display a commitment to university-level teaching and mentoring
at the undergraduate, Master's, and Ph.D. levels.
Responsibilities:
The successful candidate is expected to maintain a vigorous
scholarly research program that will foster the acquisition of
external funding, generate high-quality research publications, and
scale HHP's research expenditures and institutional
footprint.
Additional multi-level teaching and instructional responsibilities
include:
• Undergraduate Level: Expanding high-demand coursework in applied
kinesiology, community health programming, and digital health
literacy.
• Master’s Level: Training students in program design,
implementation science framework evaluation, and advanced
health-tracking methodologies.
• Ph.D. Level: Providing specialized training in mHealth
intervention design, community collaborations, and grant proposal
writing, while serving as a primary advisor and mentor for doctoral
dissertations.
• Service: Performing service to the department, college,
university, and the profession (such as active involvement in
organizations like the Society of Behavioral Medicine).
Application Process:
Review of application materials will begin immediately and
continue until the position is filled. Applicants should submit the
following materials electronically:
1. A Cover Letter describing your (a) qualifications and interest
in the position, (b) evidence of scholarly impact, (c) history of
or potential for external funding, and (d) teaching and mentoring
philosophy.
2. A current Curriculum Vitae.
3. Three Letters of Recommendation.
4. Copies of all Academic Transcripts.
University Description:
The University of Houston is a Carnegie-designated Tier One
public research university recognized with a Phi Beta Kappa chapter
for excellence in undergraduate education. UH serves the globally
competitive Houston and Gulf Coast region by providing world-class
faculty, experiential learning and strategic industry partnerships.
Located in the nation's fourth-largest city and one of the most
vibrant regions in the country, UH enrolls nearly 49,000
students.
Applications should be submitted through the University of Houston
Careers website at https://www.uh.edu/human-resources/careers/.
The anticipated start date is Fall 2027.
Employees are expected to have a home address in the state of
Texas for the duration of their appointments.
Official transcripts are required for a faculty appointment and
will be requested upon selection of the final candidates.
All positions at the University of Houston-System are security
sensitive and will require a criminal history check. Individuals
conducting research in critical infrastructure areas (i.e.,
communication infrastructure systems, cybersecurity systems,
electric grid, hazardous waste treatment systems, and/or water
treatment facilities) are subject to regular review to ensure the
security and integrity of the research is maintained.
The University of Houston System and its universities are Equal
Opportunity Institutions. Everyone is encouraged to apply.

Posting Details
Position Details
Title
Open Rank, Tenured/Tenure-track Faculty Position in Environmental
Fate and Effects of Microplastics
Appointment Status
Tenure Track
Department
IU Bloomington Vice Provost For Faculty Affairs
Location
Bloomington
Position Summary
The O’Neill School of Public and Environmental Affairs at Indiana
University Bloomington ( IUB ) invites applications for a
tenured/tenure-track faculty position in environmental science
focused on the biological, physiological, and ecological
processes governing the fate, transformation, transport, and
effects of microplastics in the environment .
As a part of the Faculty 100
strategic hiring initiative , IUB seeks a scholar whose
research connects processes across earth systems and biological
scales—from microbial communities and organisms to terrestrial and
aquatic food webs and ecosystems. Research areas may include
microbial colonization, biotransformation, and biodegradation of
microplastics; biologically mediated transport and accumulation in
organisms and food webs; microplastic-facilitated transport of
pathogens or other biological agents; food-web transfer; and
organismal, community, food web, or ecosystem-level
consequences . We particularly welcome research that uses
microplastics to address broader fundamental questions in
environmental microbiology, ecology, biogeochemistry, contaminant
fate, or environmental health. The candidate will complement
O’Neill’s strengths in environmental chemistry, toxicology, risk
assessment, ecology, and sustainability science while creating new
opportunities for collaboration across Indiana University.
Qualifications: Applicants should hold a Ph.D. in
environmental science, environmental engineering, biology, or a
related discipline by the time of appointment. Candidates should
demonstrate a record of publications and professional achievements
commensurate with appointment at the assistant professor rank;
postdoctoral experience is preferred.
We anticipate hiring at the assistant professor rank but will also
consider exceptional candidates at senior ranks. The successful
applicant should conduct lab and/or field research that integrates
across scales to understand how biological interactions and
processes influence microplastic persistence, movement, and
ecological consequences for organism well-being.
Responsibilities: The successful candidate will establish
and maintain a rigorous, externally funded research program with
national and international recognition; teach undergraduate and
graduate courses; mentor students; contribute service to the
O’Neill School and Indiana University. Institutional support will
provide adequate startup funding and space to establish a
successful research program.
We strongly encourage applicants whose work demonstrates interest
in disciplinary and interdisciplinary collaboration. All O’Neill
faculty members are expected to engage with our diverse community
of students and colleagues. We are especially interested in
candidates with a record of effective teaching and mentoring of
students from varied backgrounds.
Application procedure : To ensure full consideration,
application materials must be received by December 14, 2026.
However, the search will continue until the position is filled.
Please submit the following materials via the online system:
cover letter
curriculum vitae
statement on research and teaching
copies of up to three publications
names of three references who could provide letters of
recommendation upon request.
Applications should be submitted via:
https://indiana.peopleadmin.com/postings/34712
For more information, please contact the search committee chair
Marta Venier ( mvenier@iu.edu ) or F100 search

Before a conditional offer of employment with tenure is finalized,
candidates will be asked to disclose any pending investigations or
previous findings of sexual or professional misconduct. Candidates
will also be required to authorize Indiana University Bloomington
to inquire with current and former employers regarding such
matters. The relevance of information disclosed or obtained during
this process to a candidate’s eligibility for hire will be
evaluated on a case-by-case basis. Indiana University Bloomington
takes matters of sexual and professional misconduct very
seriously.
Indiana University is an equal opportunity employer and
provider of ADA services and prohibits discrimination in
hiring.
See Indiana University Notice of Non-Discrimination here
which includes contact information.
About Indiana University Bloomington and the O’Neill School
:
Founded in 1820, Indiana
University-Bloomington ( IUB ) is the flagship campus of
Indiana University. Located in Bloomington, IN., IUB constantly
strives to embody its mission to create, disseminate, preserve, and
apply knowledge. It does so through its commitments to cutting-edge
research, scholarship, arts, and creative activity; inspired and
challenging undergraduate, graduate, professional, and lifelong
educational programs; meaningful experiences outside the classroom;
expansive global educational opportunities; first-rate library and
museum collections; and far-reaching economic development and
impact in the state and region.
IUB is a member of the prestigious Association of American
Universities ( AAU ) since 1909, is accredited by the Higher
Learning Commission and is a member of the North Central
Association. With over 47,000 undergraduate and graduate students,
the campus has 16 degree-granting colleges and schools offering
300+ undergraduate majors, 300+ Master’s degrees, and 150+ doctoral
and professional degree opportunities. Known for its Indiana
limestone facades and green spaces throughout, IUB is widely
considered one of the country’s most beautiful college
campuses.
The O’Neill School of
Public and Environmental Affairs offers abundant
opportunities for cross-disciplinary collaboration within the
school and across campus, including with the Departments of
Chemistry ,
Earth and Atmospheric
Sciences , Biology , and Geography ; the
School of
Public Health ; and the Luddy School of
Informatics, Computing, and Engineering . Faculty also have
exceptional access to world-class supercomputing resources ,
state-of-the-art analytical facilities—including the Center for Genomics and
Bioinformatics , Flow Cytometry Core
Facility , and Light
Microscopy Imaging Center —and distinctive field
opportunities through the Indiana
University Research and Teaching Preserve .
The O’Neill School is among the largest schools of public affairs
and environmental science in the United States, with more than
34,000 alumni worldwide. Indiana University Bloomington is a major
research university founded in 1820 and enrolls more than 38,000
undergraduate and 10,000 graduate and professional students.
Bloomington is a diverse community in the wooded hills of southern
Indiana, approximately one hour from Indianapolis and four hours
from Chicago, offering cultural and recreational opportunities,
comparatively affordable housing, and excellent schools.

Morgan State University ( MSU ), Maryland’s preeminent public urban
research university located in Baltimore, Maryland, is a
Carnegie-classified Doctoral Research Institution with High
Research Activity (R2). It is known for its excellence in teaching,
research, and services. In the last six years, this bustling HBCU
has increased its enrollment by more than 50%, from 7,600 to 12,400
students, and has tripled its research grant output from about $30
million per year to over $100 million per year in 2024-2025. MSU

for leadership in the following areas: Generative and foundational
AI models; AI-driven approaches to quantum computing and
cybersecurity integration; autonomous systems and robotics; AI in
health and environmental sustainability; AI ethics; AI in
education, and workforce development.

recognized record of excellence in research, external funding, and
graduate training. The Endowed Chair will play a pivotal role in
advancing cutting-edge AI research, fostering interdisciplinary
collaboration across schools and centers, strengthening
partnerships with industry and federal agencies, and expanding
academic excellence in artificial intelligence across research,
education, and innovation.

program.

applications.

Ph.D. in Computer Science, Artificial Intelligence, Data

program coordination, committee leadership, center administration,
or departmental administration.

skills.

Job Details
Job Description:
When talent is in demand, we supply opportunity. SUNY Oneonta seeks
a tenure-track Assistant Professor of Supply Chain
Management to join its AACSB-accredited Department of Business
beginning in Fall 2027 . The successful candidate will
contribute to undergraduate instruction, scholarly research,
student mentorship, departmental and university service, and
ongoing professional development.
The Department of Business, part of the School of Liberal Arts and
Business, is AACSB-accredited and known for its supportive,
collaborative environment, small class sizes, highly accessible
faculty, and technology-supported classrooms that foster meaningful
student engagement.
To learn more about the University and the department, please visit
https://suny.oneonta.edu/ and https://suny.oneonta.edu/business .

Teaching undergraduate courses such as:
Productions and Operations management
Supply chain management
Logistics management
Project management
Enterprise resource planning
Fundamentals of management
Other courses based on departmental and school needs
Conducting research leading to publications in refereed
journals.
Advising students.
Fulfilling departmental and university service.
Engaging in ongoing professional development.
Salary: $95,000 - $100,000 commensurate with experience.
SUNY Oneonta is a Public Service Loan Forgiveness qualifying
employer. Information on SUNY's comprehensive benefits offerings
can be found at https://www.suny.edu/benefits . Visa sponsorship is
not available for this position.
Requirements:
Required Qualifications:
Earned doctorate degree in Supply Chain Management (SCM) or in
Production/Operations Management (POM) with a specialization in
Supply Chain Management, or a closely related field with
demonstrated expertise in Supply Chain Management, from an
AACSB-accredited institution. ABD considered; official confirmation
of degree conferral by issuing institution by start of
employment.
All applicants must have the potential to meet the scholarly
academic Department's qualification criteria for AACSB
standards.
Preferred Qualifications:
A record of published refereed journal articles in Supply Chain
Management, Production/Operations Management, or a related
field.
Experience in teaching, mentoring, and/or research.
Experience or strong interest in teaching business programs
with foundations in sustainability and management.
A focus on Green Supply Chain.
Experience working with and or service diverse population
and/or multicultural populations.
Additional Information:
SUNY Oneonta enrolls about 5,500 students who pursue bachelor's or
master's degrees or certificates in one of 70-plus academic
programs. Known as an exemplary residential campus that values
inclusion, service and sustainability, SUNY Oneonta is a nurturing
community where students grow intellectually, thrive socially, and
live purposefully.
The university is located in the City of Oneonta, nestled in the
northern foothills of the Catskill Mountains about a four-hour
drive from New York City, Boston, and Philadelphia. With a
population just shy of 14,000, Oneonta is one of the 20 Most
Picturesque Small Towns in America (Microsoft News). The natural
beauty of the region is breathtaking year-round. Each season offers
outdoor activities such as hiking, biking, boating, swimming, and
skiing. Employees give SUNY Oneonta high marks for work/life
balance, management, and culture. The university's indeed.com
rating is 4.4, highlighting a sense of community, and supportive
colleagues.
SUNY Oneonta values a diverse university community. Please visit
our website on diversity at: https://suny.oneonta.edu/diversity . Moreover, the
university is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer.
Women, persons of color, persons with disabilities, and protected
veterans are encouraged to apply. "At SUNY Oneonta, we believe
that diversity is an asset and a source of strength that energizes
our collective growth and innovation." - President Alberto
Cardele.

To apply online go to: http://oneonta.interviewexchange.com/candapply.jsp?JOBID=206307
. Please upload a letter of interest, most recent curriculum vitae,
statement of teaching philosophy, teaching evaluations (if

recent research (if available). Contact information for three
references must be provided; instructions for submitting letters of

For other employment and regional opportunities, please visit our
website at https://suny.oneonta.edu/employment.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor of Management Information Systems and Business Analytics
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Summary
The Department of Management & Marketing at Purdue University Fort Wayne (http://www.pfw.edu) invites applications for a nine-month, tenure-track Assistant Professor of Management Information Systems (MIS) and Business Analytics (BA) faculty position that begins August 2027.
Responsibilities
The candidate is expected to teach undergraduate and/or MBA courses in MIS and Analytics - Healthcare Analytics, Supply Chain Analytics, Insurance Analytics or Advanced Business Analytics. A combination of online, hybrid, and face-to-face course delivery will be expected. Duties will include teaching, research, and service (e.g., participating on school and university level committees) per department and university guidelines.
Qualifications
Candidates should possess a Ph.D. or DBA in MIS, Computer Information Systems, or a relevant business discipline with expertise in the area of Business Analytics. ABDs in advanced stages will also be considered. ABDs in advanced stages will be considered if the degree is in hand by August 2027.
The Department
Doermer School of Business is accredited by AACSB International. The Department of Management & Marketing consists of sixteen full-time faculty members. We offer baccalaureate majors in Management and Marketing, as well as minors and certificates. We also contribute extensively to the delivery of the MBA program. Our online baccalaureate degree is ranked 32nd nationally and 2nd in Indiana in the US News & World Report’s Best Online Programs 2026.
The University
Purdue University Fort Wayne (PFW) is the largest university in northeast Indiana, offering 25 graduate and over 100 prestigious Purdue University undergraduate degrees and certificates. The 594-acre campus in Fort Wayne is home to over 7,000 degree seeking undergraduate and graduate students. Through PFW’s partnerships with area high schools, almost 3,000 high school students take dual-credit courses, simultaneously earning both high school and college credits. PFW is accredited by The Higher Learning Commission of the North Central Association of Colleges and Schools. Learn more about us at PFW.edu.
Our campus is located within Indiana’s second-largest city, Fort Wayne, which has a population of 270,000 and resides within a greater metropolitan area of approximately 430,000. The city enjoys a diverse, active, and well-supported arts community, is home to several minor league sports teams, and has miles of pathways and trails that highlight the city and the three rivers that flow through it. Fort Wayne has been named an “All-American City” four times and is consistently cited for the high quality of life, low cost of living, and warm hospitality. Fort Wayne has been named one of the best places to live; US News & World Report ranked it a Top 50 Best Places to Live in 2022-2023.
Application Process
Please submit a cover letter, curriculum vitae, evidence of teaching effectiveness, 1–2-page statement of teaching philosophy, and copies of transcripts to https://careers.purdue.edu/FW/job/Assistant-Professor-of-Management-Information-Systems-and-Business-Analytics/44883-en_US. Candidates invited for a campus visit will deliver both research and instructional presentations, each lasting 45-60 minutes. The screening will start immediately and run until the position is filled. This position is contingent on available funding and a satisfactory backgrounds record check. For questions, contact Dr. Xiaoguang Tian, Chair, Department of Management and Marketing, Purdue University Fort Wayne at mgmkfs@pfw.edu.
Purdue University Fort Wayne is an EO/EA employer.

jobs.title: Assistant Professor, Electrical Engineering - Semiconductor
jobs.description:
Job Details
Position Rank and Title: Assistant Professor, Electrical
Engineering
School/Department Name: Electrical Engineering
Compensation: Commensurate with qualifications, experience,
and rank as established by the
CSU Salary Schedule . Anticipated hiring academic year annual
salary range: $106,000 - $126,000
Faculty employee benefits are very competitive for the higher
education sector. See the
CSU Employee Benefits Summary for details about the CSU’s
excellent benefits package.
Target Start Date: August 17, 2027
Application Deadline: 1 December 2026 (Applications
accepted until filled or closed)
Position Description
The Department of Electrical Engineering at San José State
University is pleased to announce a search for a tenure-track
Assistant Professor beginning in August 2027. We seek candidates
with expertise in semiconductor fabrication and test. The
successful candidate will be required to teach undergraduate and
graduate electrical engineering courses and maintain an active
research program in these areas. The EE Department encourages and
celebrates multidisciplinary research that solves real-world
problems, including but not limited to food scarcity, assistive
technologies, healthcare, manufacturing, and transportation.
Located in the center of Silicon Valley, the Department of
Electrical Engineering at SJSU has established a firm goal of
providing a high-quality electrical engineering education to its
students at both the undergraduate and graduate levels. The
department offers classroom instruction by the best-qualified EE
faculty, hands-on experience in industry-sponsored,
state-of-the-art laboratories, and opportunities for industry
internships. The department has over 800 undergraduate students, 20
SAGE (accelerated master's in EE) students, and 190 graduate
students. Both the EE undergraduate and graduate programs help
students gain professional experience while taking classes. In
conjunction with their classes, many students work as Instructional
Student Assistants and Teaching Associates in the department, and
as EE interns at Silicon Valley firms. Our graduates enjoy
excellent career opportunities in a broad spectrum of theoretical
and practical areas such as device physics, micro and nano
electronics, analog electronics, integrated circuits,
communications, signal processing, network and network security,
mobile network, power electronics, energy systems, microprocessors
and computer systems, embedded systems, control, robotics,
autonomous systems, machine learning and deep learning, quantum
information and quantum computing. The Department of Electrical
Engineering website is at www.sjsu.edu/ee/ .
Department Resources & Infrastructure
Micro Processing Engineering Laboratory (MPEL) : Offers
hands-on facilities for oxidation/diffusion, contact and maskless
photolithography, IC testing, wet/dry etching, and a minor in
semiconductor fabrication. The facility has a strong tradition of
workforce development. ( MPEL
Website )
Advanced Characterization Equipment : Access to MCMC
SEM, Atomic Force Microscopy, X-Ray Diffraction, and 3-D Optical
Profilometry.
Specialized Laboratories :
Charles Babbage Synopsys Laboratory: Servers and Software
Cadence Design Systems Laboratory: Servers and Software
Teradyne: Memory ATE Laboratory
LitePoint Corporation: RF Antenna Pattern Test Chamber
E&M and microwave: VNA, ANSYS software
Cheadle RF Communications Laboratory : Spectrum Analyzer, Logic
Analyzer, Time Synthesizer, Vector Signal Generator, Network
Analyzer
● Consortia, Hubs & Academic Partnerships
Member of the California-Pacific-Northwest AI
Hardware Hub and the Edge Consortium
NNME
Pacific-Intermountain Regional Node
Collaborative facilities, including
Stanford SNF and Berkeley Marvell
Nano Lab
Extensive relationships with local community colleges
The Department has numerous corporate sponsors, and faculty have
access to research development support through the Division of
Research and Innovation and teaching and career development support
through the Center for Faculty Excellence and Teaching and
Innovation ( CFETI ).
The Department of Electrical Engineering at San José State
University values institutional excellence and is committed to
advancing equity through research, teaching, and service. We enroll
more than 40,000 students, many of whom are historically
underserved; approximately 45% of our undergraduates are
first-generation, and 38% are Pell Grant recipients. In addition,
we are both a Hispanic-Serving Institution (HSI) and an Asian
American and Native American Pacific Islander-Serving Institution
(AANAPISI). SJSU aspires to create holistic learning environments
that facilitate both individual and collective transformation. We
seek teacher-scholars who cultivate inclusive, empowering spaces
for mutual learning, skill-building, and knowledge exchange for all
students. Our commitment to lifelong learning supports meaningful
connections among faculty, staff, students, alums, and the broader
communities we serve.
We invite all applicants to include a Statement of Institutional
Excellence (or incorporate it into your cover letter) to share how
your lived and professional experiences will contribute to the SJSU
community—particularly in relation to student success. A guide to
writing this statement can be found at
SJSU Institutional Excellence Statement Guidelines .
Required Qualifications
Applicants must have a Ph.D. degree in Electrical Engineering
or Physics, by the start of the appointment.
Applicants must have a research background in semiconductor
process design, TCAD, device modeling, and/or advanced materials,
such as but not limited to ferro-electric devices, quantum dots,
graphene, and memristors.
Applicants must have a strong commitment, demonstrate potential
for teaching excellence at both the undergraduate and graduate
levels, and engage in curriculum development.
Applicants should demonstrate awareness of and sensitivity to
the educational goals of a socially and economically diverse
student population, as might have been gained through
cross-cultural study, training, teaching, and other comparable
experience.
Preferred Qualifications
Postdoctoral experience in academia or industry
Experience mentoring undergraduate and/or graduate research
students.
Experience adapting teaching methods to a variety of learning
environments.
Involved in safety compliance across high-risk, multi-variable
industrial or academic environments
Key Responsibilities
Faculty members are expected to teach, supervise, and advise
students in both undergraduate and graduate programs in a manner
that emphasizes experiential learning, to provide leadership in
developing modern curricula in Device physics, transistor
fabrication, solar cell fabrication, MEMS, to establish a research
program related to their field of interest, and to seek external
partnerships, funding, and/or collaboration with Silicon Valley and
beyond. To develop a hands-on workforce development program in
semiconductor fabrication that includes microcredentials.
The candidate will participate in shared governance, usually
through departmental, college, and university committees and other
service assignments with a special emphasis MPEL operations.
Faculty shall organize all their classes within the Canvas
Learning Management System (LMS).
The candidate must demonstrate awareness of and experience with
the needs of a student population of great diversity – in age,
abilities, cultural background, ethnicity, religion, economic
background, primary language, sexual orientation, gender identity,
and academic preparation – through inclusive course materials,
teaching strategies, and advisement.
Other Duties
Note that all San José State University employees are considered
mandated reporters under the California Child Abuse and Neglect
Reporting Act and are required to comply with the requirements set
forth in CSU Executive Order 1083 as a condition of employment.
Pursuant to the Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy
and Campus Crime Statistics Act (Clery Act) and CSU systemwide
policy, some faculty duties may lead to designation as a Campus
Security Authority (CSA). CSAs are required to complete Clery Act
training and to immediately report Clery incidents to the
institution.
Faculty employees must complete CSU employee training as assigned
and required based on their role (e.g., Data Security, FERPA,
Preventing Discrimination and Harassment, Title IX, Health and
Safety). The President may recommend or require compliance with
safety measures that decrease the likelihood of COVID-19
transmission or illness and allows the core mission and activities
of the campus to continue.
Application Procedure
Click Apply Now to complete the SJSU Online Employment Application
and attach the following documents (3-page limit on each
document):
letter of interest (1-page limit)
curriculum vitae (3-page limit)
institutional excellence statement (dedicated statement or
addressed in letter of interest) (1-page limit)
statement of teaching interests/philosophy (1-page
limit)
research plans (2-page limit)
three references with contact information
Inquiries may be directed to the Department Chair, Professor David
W. Parent, David.Parent@sjsu.edu.
Pursuant to California Education Code 89521, applicants will be
required to disclose whether they have received a final
administrative decision or final judicial decision determining that
they have committed sexual harassment within the last 7 years only
after a determination is made that they meet the minimum
qualifications for the position, and before an offer of employment
is extended. Applicants who reach the final stages of the
application process must also sign a release form that authorizes
the release of information by the applicant’s current and/or former
employers to the CSU concerning any substantiated allegations of
misconduct.
Conditional Offer
The work for this faculty position may only be performed in the
State of California and requires establishing an on-campus
presence. Employment is contingent upon US residence and proof of
eligibility to work in the United States. Satisfactory completion
of background and reference checks (including criminal records and
prior employment) is required. SJSU will make a conditional offer
of employment, which may be rescinded if the background and
reference checks reveal disqualifying information, and/or it is
discovered that the candidate knowingly withheld or falsified
information. Failure to satisfactorily complete the background and
reference checks may affect the continued employment of a current
employee who was conditionally offered the position.
San José State University: Silicon Valley's Public
University
Located in the heart of Silicon Valley — one of the most innovative
regions in the world — San José State University
is the founding campus of the 23-campus California State University
(CSU) system and the first public university in the West.
Recognized as a leading transformative educational institution, San
José State is an essential partner in the technological, economic,
cultural, and social development of Silicon Valley, the Bay Area,
and California. SJSU is a top-200 school nationally for research
funding and ranks second in research productivity within the CSU
system. Cutting-edge research, world-class scholarship,
student-centered learning, diverse communities, and commitment to
social justice allow SJSU to provide life-changing opportunities
and advance the public good locally and globally.
Equal Employment Statement
San José State University prohibits discrimination based on Age,
Ancestry, Caste, Color, Disability, Ethnicity, Gender, Gender
Expression, Gender Identity, Genetic Information, Marital Status,
Medical Condition, Military Status, Nationality, Race, Religion,
Religious Creed, Sex, Sexual Orientation, Sex Stereotype, and
Veteran Status. This policy applies to all San José State
University students, faculty, and staff as well as University
programs and activities. Reasonable accommodations are made for
applicants with disabilities who self-disclose.
Campus Security and Fire Safety Notification
Pursuant to the Jeanne Clery Disclosure of Campus Security Policy
and Campus Crime Statistics Act, the Annual Security Report (ASR)
is also now available for viewing at https://www.sjsu.edu/clery/docs/SJSU-Annual-Security-Report.pdf
. The ASR contains the current security and safety-related policy
statements, emergency preparedness and evacuation information,
crime prevention and Sexual Assault prevention information, and
information about drug and alcohol prevention programming. The ASR
also contains statistics of Clery crimes for San José State
University locations for the three most recent calendar years. A
paper copy of the ASR is available upon request by contacting the
Office of the Clery Director by phone at 408-924-1501 or by email
at clerycompliance@sjsu.edu.
Pursuant to the Higher Education Opportunity Act, the Annual Fire
Safety Report (AFSR) is available at
https://www.sjsu.edu/clery/docs/SJSU-Annual-Fire-Safety-Report.pdf
. The purpose of this report is to disclose statistics for fires
that occurred within SJSU on-campus housing facilities for the
three most recent calendar years, and to distribute fire safety
policies and procedures intended to promote safety on Campus. A
paper copy of the AFSR is available upon request by contacting the
Housing Office by phone at 408-795-5600 or by email at
uhs-frontdesk@sjsu.edu.

jobs.description:
The Animation & Game Design Program in the Harry W. Bass Jr. School of Arts, Humanities, and Technology at The University of Texas at Dallas invites applications for a tenure-system Assistant Professor specializing in one of the following: Virtual Reality, (VR), and/or Augmented Reality (AR). Professional experience in VR/AR studios, motion capture, real-time rendering, or volumetric capture workflows is preferred along with experience with Unreal Engine, Unity, real-time VFX, or virtual cinematography pipelines. This is a full-time, 9-month, tenure-track appointment.
We seek a creative scholar whose research, professional practice, and teaching advance emerging immersive media fields. The successful candidate will contribute to curricular growth in VR/AR, real-time interactive media, and immersive storytelling, with opportunities to collaborate across campus in areas such as computer science, simulation, visualization, digital humanities, and interdisciplinary arts.
The appointment commences for the fall 2027 semester.

Job Details
Position Summary
The Hugh Hodgson School of Music at the University of Georgia ( UGA
) seeks a dynamic senior faculty member to contribute to teaching
and creative activities as professor of trumpet. Primary duties
include applied instruction to undergraduate and graduate trumpet
majors; contribute to teaching courses in brass literature and
brass pedagogy; coaching of chamber music, and/or other areas
aligned with candidate’s advanced expertise; active participation
in area activities and recruitment; and performing in the faculty
brass quintet.
Responsibilities
Serve as an artist-teacher of trumpet
Teach applied trumpet lessons to students from undergraduate
through doctoral levels
Participate in student recruitment in and out of state
Contribute to courses on brass literature and brass
pedagogy
Coach chamber music
Perform in the faculty brass quintet
Mentor undergraduate and graduate students
Contribute to a dynamic and holistic music program
Maintain a productive career as a research/creative scholar and
performer
The position will be considered for tenure and graduate faculty
status upon appointment. A candidate of especially high
international reputation may be considered for the William F. and
Pamela P. Prokasy Professorship in the Arts, which has been
associated over decades with trumpet faculty of exceptional
renown.
Special Instructions to Applicants
Applications will be reviewed beginning December 3, 2026 and until
the position is filled. Applicants should include a curriculum

program. The cover letter should highlight information related to
their teaching philosophy and specific examples of how their
teaching, service, and research/creative activity will support the
success of students from a variety of interests and
backgrounds.
Additionally, application materials should include the following:
links to at least 3 stylistically diverse, unedited live recordings
from performances in the past two years; unofficial transcripts for
highest degree earned; names and contact information for a minimum
of three references. Candidates may also be asked to provide links
to teaching samples at a later juncture.
Questions about the application process can be directed to Susan
McClure (Susan.McClure@uga.edu); questions about the position can
be directed to Dr. Brandon Craswell (craswell@uga.edu), chair of
the search committee.
