jobs.title: HR Faculty Transaction Lead - KSAS (Human Resources)
jobs.description:
Job Details
Johns Hopkins, founded in 1876, is America's first research
university and home to nine world-class academic divisions working
together as one university.
This role will manage and oversee all faculty-related HR
transactions for a defined division. We are seeking a HR
Faculty Transaction Lead - KSAS who will oversee designated
Faculty Transaction Specialists and serve as a subject matter
expert, providing guidance on complex HR issues, ensuring
compliance with university policies, and streamlining processes to
enhance service delivery. This role requires strong analytical
skills, a deep understanding of applicable HR policies,
demonstrated expertise on specialized matters related to the
faculty population, and the ability to manage high-volume
transactions efficiently.
Job Scope/Complexity
Works with high-volume, detail-sensitive processes requiring
accuracy, consistency, and expert knowledge of applicable
faculty-related policy and operations. Success is measured by
customer satisfaction, transaction accuracy, policy adherence, and
effectiveness of process improvements in a high-demand
environment.
Specific Duties & Responsibilities
Transaction Oversight
Oversee teams that process faculty-related HR transactions,
including job changes, compensation adjustments, leaves, time and
attendance, and terminations for faculty personnel.
Ensure accuracy and compliance with university policies and
procedures.
Audit data entry and updates in HR systems with a high degree
of accuracy and attention to detail.
Policy and Compliance
Interpret and apply university and department policies related
to faculty HR transactions.
Ensure transactions comply with federal and state labor laws,
university guidelines, and faculty appointment policies and
guidelines.
Serve as the escalation point for complex faculty-related HR
issues and transactions.
Advising and Support
Act as a resource for faculty and faculty-related personnel on
HR-related matters.
Provide guidance to departments and HR business partners on
faculty-related HR processes and best practices.
Resolve transactional issues and work with Help Desk
Specialists, who provide frontline support and serve as the initial
point of contact for customer inquiries and other stakeholders to
ensure consistent service delivery.
Process Improvement
Identify opportunities to improve efficiency and accuracy of
faculty-related HR transactions.
Develop and implement best practices for handling high-volume
and complex HR transactions.
Collaborate with HR systems teams to update/enhance
functionality and user experience.
Training and Documentation
Develop and deliver training on applicable HR policies and
transactional processes.
Create and maintain documentation, including standard operating
procedures (SOPs) and process guides.
Ensure knowledge transfer and consistency across the faculty HR
support team.
Data Reporting and Governance
Generate reports and analyze data to monitor transaction
volumes, processing times, and accuracy rates.
Identify trends and recommend adjustments to improve service
delivery.
Provide regular updates to leadership on applicable HR
performance and operational challenges.
Support and consult with schools on faculty-related HR data and
system transactions related to faculty positions.
Provides guidance on complex issues related to employment,
ensuring compliance with university policies and ensuring data
accuracy, reliability, and quality in order to streamline processes
to enhance service delivery.
Enforce data governance policies related to faculty HR records,
ensuring compliance with institutional, state, and federal
regulations.
Technology
Oversee the use of HR systems (e.g., Workday) to manage and
track HR transactions and service requests.
Partner with IT and HRIS teams to implement system updates and
improvements.
Teach and train Faculty Transaction Specialists on the use of
reporting and dashboards.
In addition to the duties listed above
Establish and monitor SLAs and KPIs. Develop routine reporting,
and present performance metrics to leadership monthly to drive
accountability and support strategic objectives.
Lead continuous process improvement initiatives to streamline
operations and enhance the employee and faculty experience.
Manage faculty recruitment and appointment activities, ensuring
effective talent acquisition and adherence to institutional
requirements.
Utilize workforce data and analytics to identify trends, inform
strategic decisions, and support organizational planning.
Partner with Faculty Affairs, Department Administrators, KSAS
Finance, Administrative Operations, and Dean’s Office leaders to
provide recommendations on complex faculty HR transactions,
ensuring alignment with Krieger School Academic Council bylaws and
procedures, JHU policies, and applicable federal and state
requirements. Transactions may include, but are not limited to,
leaves, promotions, named professorships, and letters of
intent.
Minimum Qualifications
Bachelor’s Degree in Human Resources, Business Administration,
or related field.
Five years of experience in an HR support role, with at least 2
years of supervisory experience.
Strong knowledge of HR processes, benefits, payroll, and
employee relations.
Excellent communication skills, both written and verbal.
Strong attention to detail, with the ability to manage multiple
tasks and priorities in a fast-paced environment.
Ability to maintain confidentiality and handle sensitive
information with professionalism.
Additional education may substitute for required experience,
and additional related experience may substitute for required
education beyond a high school diploma/graduation equivalent, to
the extent permitted by the JHU equivalency formula.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience with HR software such as Workday, ADP, or
ServiceNow.
Fluency in Workday reporting and ability to teach others the
use of dashboards and reports.
Knowledge of data protection and confidentiality
regulations.
Previous experience working in a global HR support
function.
Experience with automation tools or coding languages for data
analysis and reporting.
Technical Qualifications and Specialized
Certifications
Proficiency in MS Office Suite (Excel, Word, PowerPoint) and
experience with HRIS or ticketing systems.
SHRM-CP or other HR certification (preferred but not
required).
Technical Skills and Expected Level of Proficiency
Faculty HR Management - Intermediate
Auditing - Intermediate
Continuous Improvement - Advanced
Confidentiality and Discretion - Intermediate
Customer Support and Service Management -Advanced
Data Management and Analysis - Intermediate
Internal Controls (HR) - Advanced
Interpersonal Skills - Intermediate
Payroll Practices - Intermediate
Process Improvement - Intermediate
Staff Training and Development - Intermediate
Wage and Hour Laws - Intermediate
Workflow Management -Advanced
The core technical skills listed are most essential;
additional technical skills may be required based on specific
division or department needs.

The School of Communication & The Arts invites applications for
various Part-Time Faculty positions for the 2026-2027 academic
year. Opportunities to teach multiple/additional courses may become
available. Successful candidates will teach, develop course
materials, assist students as needed, and assess student
work.
Minimum Qualifications:
Masters or Bachelors degree in an appropriate field, and/or
Industry/professional experience.
Preferred Qualifications:
Previous University level teaching experience.
Essential Functions:
Opportunities are available to teach in one or more areas across
several disciplines over time.
Subject matter includes:
Event Planning – taught Tuesday/Thursday 5:00pm – 6:15pm
(time slot may be negotiable) during Spring 2027
Semester
History of Costume - taught Tuesday/Thursday 5:00pm – 6:15pm
(time slot may be negotiable) during Spring 2027
Semester
Teaching opportunities include undergraduate courses that may be
available in both on-ground and online environments. Availability
to teach during daytime hours is desired.
Required Application Documents:
Resume, Cover Letter, & Contact Information of 3 Professional
References
About the Department/School:
The Fashion Program at Marist successfully prepares its students to
enter the world of fashion and pursue careers in merchandising,
planning, product development, retailing, operations, fashion
promotion, event production, and a gamut of other employment
opportunities. Students gain the skills, knowledge and internship
experiences within an encouraging academic environment to help them
flourish in the fashion industry.
The Fashion Program is housed in the School of Communication and
the Arts, which prepares students for careers in communication,
media, fashion & art practices, building valuable skills that
complement a foundation in a liberal arts education. With
nationally ranked programs and Centers of Excellence in Sports
Communication and Social Media, we foster an inclusive and engaged
community of industry experts and research faculty dedicated to
student success. We aim to inspire students to become empathetic
and ethically responsible professionals with an understanding of
the values of community engagement, sustainability, and social
responsibility. Marist’s location in the Hudson Valley offers a
traditional University experience that is only a train ride away
from the rich cultural and professional opportunities New York City
has to offer, while our global campus in Florence, Italy gives
students the opportunity to expand their world.
About Marist University:
Founded in 1929, Marist is a comprehensive, independent four-year
institution whose signature educational approach blends the liberal
arts with pre-professional studies and emphasizes experiential
learning to enrich classroom instruction. With campuses in
Poughkeepsie, N.Y., and Florence, Italy, plus over 70 programs
offering a variety of international study, Marist is a portal to
the world and is devoted to nurturing a welcoming, inclusive
community. Through six schools offering almost 50 majors, Marist
cultivates the intellectual growth and well-being of its more than
6,000 undergraduate and graduate students and encourages them to
color outside traditional academic lines as they pursue coursework
and personal experiences that provide valuable occupational
expertise and reflect their individual passions. Marist has been
acclaimed a top institution in the nation by U.S. News & World
Report, the Wall Street Journal/College Pulse, Princeton Review,
and others. To learn more, please visit https://www.marist.edu/about

jobs.title: Assistant Professor and Lab Manager, EMS Programs
jobs.description:
Compensation
$62,882.00 Annual
Job Description Summary
The application deadline for this position is 11:59pm EST on
November 29, 2026.
The Emergency Medical Services A.S. Program prepares students for
promotions and advancement within the EMS industry. Students who
are a state of the Florida certified as EMT and Paramedic, and
graduated from a Florida accredited EMS Training Program, have
already fulfilled the core requirements and can earn an A.S. degree
in as little as one or two semesters. With an A.S. degree in
Emergency Medical Services, it is possible to move beyond providing
care in the field and seek a position in management with a public
safety agency or healthcare provider.
Under general supervision, the Assistant Professor and Lab Manager
for Emergency Medical Services (EMS) Programs, will develop,
prepare, and teach a variety of EMS courses, while also managing
the EMS skills lab. Instructional activities will encompass more
than 50 percent of total duty time. The Assistant Professor must
have the flexibility to teach courses during the day, evening, or
online, as well as taught using other distance learning
formats.
Job Description
Responsibilities and Duties Include:
Plans, organizes, and delivers instruction to didactic,
laboratory and/or classroom settings to promote student success
within a community college setting.
Supports and promotes the college and departmental missions
centered on excellence in teaching and learning through quality
instruction, curriculum enhancement, and timely service.
Collaborates with the Associate Director, Chair, faculty, and
peers to evaluate, revise, and develop curriculum that cultivates
the mastery of course content.
Assists in the direction and supervision of EMS programs and
personnel, including adjunct faculty and EMS clinical
coordination.
Demonstrates technological literacy and innovation in the
delivery of instruction.
Provides leadership, positive role modeling, and strong working
relationships with students, public safety agencies, the EMS
Advisory Committee, SF faculty and staff, and members of the
community.
Works collaboratively as part of a cohesive academic team.
Assists with the implementation of college policies,
objectives, and functions in accordance with the SF philosophy,
mission, strategic initiatives, and procedures.
Participates in departmental meetings and collegewide
committees as needed.
Provides students with frequent, timely assessment and clear
feedback regarding academic performance.
Appropriately documents student progress and maintains records
including attendance, grading, and student learning outcomes.
Develops methods that fairly and accurately assess students’
progress in achieving the stated learning outcomes/objectives.
Collaborates with the EMS Programs Director to implement
requirements established by organizations such as CoAEMSP, the
Florida Department of Health, and partner organizations to maintain
accreditation of IPS programs and facilities.
Collects data and prepares, transmits, and maintains various
reports and records.
Collaborates with peer faculty to design and develop
simulation-based training with equipment to include a variety of
human patient simulators and ensure that assessments are performed
accurately.
Maintains simulation equipment to ensure operational
readiness.
Ensures that simulators and other equipment are properly
understood and utilized by faculty.
Collaborates with EMS Programs faculty to ensure continuity
between instruction in the classroom and skills lab along with
practices in clinical experiences.
Collaborates and provides support to SF staff and partner
organizations in the administration of American Heart Association
training center policies and operations.
Promotes a professional, supportive, innovative, safe, and
non-discriminatory environment for students, faculty, and staff to
ensure that all decisions and other actions are in the best
interests of the College.
Provides good stewardship of SF equipment, supplies, and
property to ensure that training and education resources are
provided and maintained in a prudent manner.
Maintains appropriate office hours proportionate to the
instructional assignment.
Keeps a record of operating procedures and may share position
specific knowledge, including use of collegewide ERP and related
system processes, by providing guidance on standard operations and
established departmental procedures as needed.
Provides service to the college through participation in
events, committees, and other college activities.
Complies with all published College Rules, procedures,
guidelines, and laws/regulations governing public employees,
including but not limited to those related to document retention
and destruction, FERPA, and confidentiality.
Strictly honors the privacy, security, and confidentiality of
records and other sensitive information according to appropriate
state, federal, and college regulations, policies, and
procedures.
Provides service excellence through courteous, informed,
accessible, and professional engagement.
Performs other duties as assigned.
QUALIFICATIONS
Required: Must meet requirements specified in FAC 64J-
1.0201, "EMS Instructor Qualifications." Accordingly, as of this
writing, the appointee must: Be certified as a Florida paramedic in
good standing with the Florida Department of Health. Have a minimum
of an associate's degree from an institution whose accreditation is
recognized by the United States Department of Education. Lead
instructor: Successfully complete the levels A and B instructor
coursework listed in Table I and Table II of FAC 64J-1.0201.
Additional Requirements: A criminal background check will be
conducted. Out-of-state applicants must obtain paramedic
certification from the National Registry of Emergency Medical
Technicians and licensure as a Florida paramedic in good standing
with the Florida Department of Health prior to their first day of
employment. Instructor certification in all of the following areas
is necessary within six months of employment: Basic Life Support,
Advanced Cardiac Life Support, Pediatric Advanced Life Support, and
either International Trauma Life Support or Prehospital Trauma Life
Support. Must be able to lift at least 20 pounds without
assistance. Applicants must have a valid Florida Class E Operator
(driver’s) license and be authorized to drive for the
college.
Preferred: A Bachelor’s degree in a relevant discipline with
experience working in a community college and/or university
setting. Teaching experience and the ability to incorporate
appropriate instructional technologies into coursework.
General Knowledge, Skills, and Abilities
Ability to work successfully in a multi-cultural
environment.
Adaptability to Change – able to be flexible and supportive,
able to positively and proactively assimilate change in rapid
growth environment.
Analytical Aptitude & Problem Solving - able to analyze
information, problems, situations, practices and/or procedures,
collect and interpret data, reason logically, establish facts,
identify and define existing and potential issues, recognize the
interrelationships among elements, draw valid conclusions, develop
recommendations, as well as alternative courses of action, select
appropriate course, follow up, and evaluate.
Communication – able to effectively communicate in a
professional, diplomatic, empathetic, and tactful manner using
preferred method and level as applicable to the job.
Critical Thinking & Judgement - able to make well-reasoned,
sensible, and timely decisions based on careful, objective review
and informed analysis of available information, considerations, and
other factors.
Customer Service – ability to respond promptly and courteously
to all questions from students and faculty, demonstrating patience
and persistence when helping students with little or no computer
skills.
Ethics – able to demonstrate integrity, professionalism,
civility, and a high degree of ethics in all job-related
actions.
Organization & Time Management – able to plan, schedule,
and organize tasks related to the job to achieve goals within or
ahead of established time frames.
Problem Solving – proven skills in identifying issues,
determining their cause, developing creative solutions, and
following through with implementing resolutions.
Relationship Management – able to personally provide high level
of interactive service to others, building relationships and
addressing identified needs.
Results Orientation – proven ability to set and exceed
established targets.
Systems & Software - proficient level of knowledge of
Microsoft Office and/or relevant position software programs.
Detail Oriented - Proven accuracy and attention to detail.
Multi-task - Ability to expeditiously organize, coordinate,
manage, prioritize, and perform multiple tasks simultaneously to
swiftly assess a situation, determine a logical course of action,
and apply the appropriate response.
If you are a retiree of the Florida Retirement System (FRS),
please check with the FRS on how your current benefits will be
affected if you are re-employed with the State of Florida. Your
current retirement benefits may be canceled, suspended or deemed
ineligible depending upon the date of your
retirement.

Inquiries regarding non-discrimination policies or concerns about

jobs.title: Business Analytics/Operations and Engineering Management Faculty (Open Rank)
jobs.description:
Business Analytics/Operations and Engineering Management Faculty
(Open Rank)
JOB DESCRIPTION SUMMARY
Florida Polytechnic University invites applications for a
tenure-equivalent faculty position in operations and engineering
management at the rank of Instructor, Assistant Professor,
Associate Professor, or Professor, beginning August 2027. We seek
candidates who can contribute to teaching and, as appropriate to
rank, research in one or more areas such as supply chain
management, logistics, engineering management, project management,
or quality management and process improvement, with an emphasis on
quantitative, analytical, and data-driven approaches.
Our B.S. in Business Analytics and M.S. in Engineering Management
emphasize quantitative, analytical, and computational approaches to
organizational and technical challenges. This position will
strengthen that focus by helping students apply these methods to
improve operations, manage projects and resources, and support
data-driven decision-making.
JOB DESCRIPTION
Responsibilities
Teach courses in one or more of the position’s areas of
specialization to support the B.S. in Business Analytics and online
M.S. in Engineering Management programs, and develop additional
courses aligned with departmental needs and the candidate’s
expertise.
Maintain a program of scholarship that leads to publication in
the discipline (Assistant Professor and above). Instructors
demonstrate a scholarly, intentional approach to pedagogy and
curriculum instead.
Contribute to department and University service.
Areas of interest
Areas of interest include, but are not limited to, supply chain
analytics, logistics, operations management, digital twin,
engineering management, project management, and quality management
and process improvement, including Six Sigma and statistical
quality control. Candidates should bring expertise in one or more
of these areas; expertise across all areas is not expected, and
related specializations that complement the department’s STEM and
analytics focus will also be considered.
Minimum qualifications
Instructor: An earned master’s degree or higher in operations
management, supply chain management, logistics, industrial
engineering, engineering management, operations research,
management science, project management, or a closely related field.
Candidates with a graduate degree in business administration or
another related discipline and relevant academic preparation or
professional expertise in one or more of the position’s teaching
areas will also be considered.
Assistant Professor: An earned doctorate in operations
management, supply chain management, industrial engineering,
engineering management, operations research, or a closely related
field, completed before the start date.
Associate Professor: An earned doctorate in one of the fields
specified for Assistant Professor, plus six years at the rank of
Assistant Professor or equivalent.
Professor: An earned doctorate in one of the fields
specified for Assistant Professor, plus six years at the rank of
Associate Professor or equivalent.
All ranks: Evidence of effective college-level teaching
and excellent oral and written communication skills.
Preferred qualifications
Industry experience in one or more areas such as supply chain
management, logistics, operations management, engineering
management, project management, or quality management and process
improvement.
Relevant professional certifications in project management,
supply chain management, Six Sigma, or quality management.
Evidence of effective and innovative teaching, including the
integration of analytical tools, industry applications, or
project-based learning.
Experience designing and teaching engaging, interactive online
courses, with familiarity with quality standards and review
frameworks developed by Quality Matters (QM) or the Online Learning
Consortium (OLC).
Demonstrated commitment to student advising and mentorship,
including support for students’ academic and professional
development.
Experience collaborating across disciplines or mentoring
interdisciplinary student projects, capstone experiences, or
undergraduate research.
Experience developing industry partnerships or contributing to
applied projects, professional training, or externally funded
initiatives.
Contributions to scholarship, professional practice, or service
commensurate with rank and instructional responsibilities.
Key dates
Start date: August 2027
Full consideration: applications received by January 11, 2027.
Review continues until the position is filled.
About the department:
The Department of Data Science and Business Analytics at Florida
Polytechnic University offers B.S. degrees in Data Science and
Business Analytics and M.S. degrees in Data Science and Engineering
Management. Its STEM-focused programs combine rigorous quantitative
and computational training with applied learning through
industry-connected internships and capstone projects.

Upload each document below as a PDF in the Resume/CV field before

and the application will be dismissed as incomplete.

applying for and explaining how your experience fits the role and
Florida Poly's mission

contact information

Professor, Associate Professor, and Professor applicants

outside the United States require an equivalency evaluation from a

application
Compensation : Commensurate with experience and rank.
Visa Sponsorship: Per Florida State University System
directives, all H1B visa sponsorship is on hold until further

in the U.S. at the time of hire and maintain status throughout

Foreign Influence Compliance Notice
Florida Polytechnic University complies with applicable Florida
laws and Florida Board of Governors requirements concerning foreign
influence, including Board of Governors Regulation 9.012,
Foreign Influence, and applicable provisions of Florida
Statutes.
Certain positions, including research, research-related support,

and University policy. Applicants for covered positions may be

supporting documentation regarding their educational and employment
history, publications, research funding, affiliations, and other

Any employment offer or appointment for a position subject to these
requirements is contingent upon satisfactory completion of all

ABOUT FLORIDA POLY:
Florida Polytechnic University opened for classes in 2014-15 and is

jobs.title: Faculty Position in Computational Chemistry / AI-Driven Drug Discovery (Open Rank)
jobs.description:
Faculty Position in Computational Chemistry / AI-Driven Drug Discovery (Open Rank)
University of Virginia
Charlottesville, Virginia
The Department of Chemistry in the College and Graduate School of Arts & Sciences, in collaboration with the Paul and Diane Manning Institute of Biotechnology at the University of Virginia (UVA), invites applications and nominations for a tenured faculty appointment in Computational Chemistry with a focus on molecular design and drug discovery. Depending on experience and interest, the successful candidate will have the opportunity to head a collaborative cohort helping to shape future concepts in AI Drug Discovery at the Manning Institute.
As a faculty member, the successful candidate will develop and lead an innovative, externally funded research program that advances computational methods for the discovery and design of functional molecules, in areas such as AI-driven drug discovery, generative modeling, molecular modeling, virtual screening, and predictive ADME/toxicity modeling. This faculty member will contribute to UVA Chemistry’s undergraduate and graduate educational mission and play a key role in mentoring graduate students and postdoctoral scholars to help shape new educational and training opportunities that connect graduate education with the Manning Institute's biotechnology and translational research mission. The department is particularly interested in researchers whose computational work is closely integrated with experimental validation and translational applications. As part of the Manning Institute, the candidate will build AI and computational drug discovery capacity that supports translational programs across the University. The leadership role potentially carries strategic responsibility beyond the candidate’s own laboratory, including shaping the Institute’s long-term scientific direction and may include leading faculty and staff recruitment efforts, guiding budget and resource allocation decisions, and setting strategic priorities across the Manning Institute’s portfolio of biotechnology programs and investments.
Candidates must hold a Ph.D. in Chemistry, Computational Science, or a closely related field and demonstrate a strong record of scholarship. The successful candidate will bring expertise in developing computational methods for the discovery and design of functional molecules. Beyond scientific excellence, UVA seeks a collaborative and entrepreneurial scholar who thrives in building partnerships across institutional boundaries and who is excited by the opportunity to help develop a growing research enterprise. Appointment rank is open and will be commensurate with the successful candidate’s qualifications and experience. Candidates with a record of research leadership comparable to that expected of a tenured faculty appointment, including experiences gained in industry or other non-academic research settings, are encouraged to apply.
Screening of complete applications will begin immediately and continue until the completion of the search process. Applications should include a cover letter, curriculum vitae, research statement, teaching statement, and contact information for three references. Materials should be submitted via the Isaacson, Miller website: https://www.imsearch.com/open-searches/university-virginia/faculty-computational-chemistryai-driven-drug-discovery
Micah Pierce, Partner
Damla Williams, Senior Associate
Marlyn Desire, Senior Search Coordinator
Isaacson, Miller
The University of Virginia is an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer and welcomes applications from women, minorities, veterans, and persons with disabilities.

jobs.description:
Job Details
NYU Abu Dhabi is pioneering a new model of higher education
for a global world, dedicated to excellence in teaching and
research and to advancing cooperation and progress on humanity?s
shared challenges. Drawing on the strengths of the NYU global
network, it offers an outstanding liberal arts and sciences
education to students from the United Arab Emirates, the United
States, and around the world, with a distinctive focus on
intercultural understanding and leadership. It supports innovative
research and graduate education programs that push forward the
frontiers of knowledge and respond in powerful and
interdisciplinary ways to vital global and local
challenges.
Description
The Division of Social Science at New York University Abu Dhabi
(NYUAD) is inviting applications for a tenure-track position in
Economics and Data Science. The successful candidate’s tenure home
would be in the Economics program and will hold an affiliation in
the new MSc in Interdisciplinary Data Science and AI (MIDSAI). The
position carries a teaching load of three courses per year, one of
which will be for MIDSAI.
As NYUAD is a research university, we seek applicants with an
active research agenda in economics and AI. The ideal candidate
will be a leader in applying data science and AI tools to questions
in economics, or conducting empirical research on the economic
implications of AI. This specialization is broadly construed and
might include research related to big data collection, machine
learning, natural language processing, image or video analysis,
network inference, computational finance, online platforms and
algorithmic behavior, and more. We are especially interested in
scholars who work effectively in multidisciplinary teams and
environments. All candidates should demonstrate important
contributions to their area of research.
About NYU Abu Dhabi
https://nyuad.nyu.edu/en/
NYU
Abu Dhabi is the first comprehensive liberal arts and research
campus in the Middle East to be operated abroad by a major American
research university. Times Higher Education ranks NYU among the top
30 universities in the world, making NYU Abu Dhabi the
highest-ranked university in the UAE and MENA region. NYU Abu Dhabi
has integrated a highly selective undergraduate curriculum across
the disciplines with a world center for advanced research and
scholarship. The university enables its students in the sciences,
engineering, social sciences, humanities, and arts to succeed in an
increasingly interdependent world and advance cooperation and
progress on humanity’s shared challenges. NYU Abu Dhabi’s
high-achieving students have come from over 120 countries and speak
over 100 languages. Together, NYU's campuses in New York, Abu
Dhabi, and Shanghai form the backbone of a unique global
university, giving faculty and students opportunities to experience
varied learning environments and immersion in other cultures at one
or more of the numerous study-abroad sites NYU maintains on six
continents.
NYUAD is committed to upholding a culture of non-discrimination,

jobs.description:
Description Title: Assistant Professor
Position Number: 0082272
Hiring Unit: College of Education, Center on Disability Studies (CDS)
Location: Manoa
Date Posted: Nov 2, 2026
Closing Date: Continuous - application review begins December 15, 2026
Salary Information: Commensurate with qualifications and experience
Monthly Type: 9 Month
Tenure Track: Tenure Track
Full Time/Part Time: Full Time
Temporary/Permanent: Permanent
Other Conditions: General funds, contingent upon position clearance. Appointment to begin August 2027 or soon thereafter. Selectee is required to complete the COE New Faculty Orientation in the first year, successfully pass a criminal background check, fulfill all mandatory training and compliance requirements and maintain an on-campus presence.
This position is a 9-month tenure track position. This position may be appointed by the Dean to an 11-month, one-year appointment as the Associate Director of CDS; renewable based on satisfactory performance and department needs. The Associate Director will work closely with the Director to provide strategic, administrative, academic, and programmatic leadership for the Center’s federally designated Hawai?i University Center for Excellence in Developmental Disabilities (HI-UCEDD). The Associate Director will be expected to develop an independent program of research and scholarship, pursue competitive federal funding, contribute to the COE’s teaching mission, and help expand CDS’ clinical and community service capacity. Should the candidate no longer serve as the Associate Director, the position will revert to a 9-month appointment in an academic department where workload is determined by the department chair.
Duties and Responsibilities
Teach undergraduate and graduate courses in face-to-face, online and/or hybrid formats, as determined by departmental needs.
Mentor students, trainees, faculty, and emerging leaders in disability research, education and professional practice.
Hold regular in-person office hours to support student learning and engagement.
Attend in-person departmental and college meetings.
Participate in accreditation processes, including documentation and report preparation.
Maintain an active program of research/scholarly activity and publications in area of specialization.
Pursue and secure competitive federal funding, including research, training, service, and demonstration grants.
Partner with the CDS Director in advancing the Center’s strategic vision, priorities, and statewide impact.
Help develop and expand clinical and clinical-adjacent services for individuals with disabilities and their families, including building partnerships, infrastructure, staffing, and sustainable models of culturally responsive and sustaining service delivery.
Attend CDS Council meetings, Pacific Rim International Conference on Disability planning meetings, and other Center programmatic meetings as needed.
Perform service to the department, college, university and community.
Performs other duties as assigned.
Minimum Qualifications
A doctoral degree in a relevant field such as psychology, special education, education, social work, disability studies, or closely related field from a college or university of recognized standing. ABD candidates will be considered if the degree is conferred by date of hire.
1 year of experience working directly with individuals with disabilities and/or developmental disabilities and their families in a clinical, educational, community, research, or related service setting.
An emerging or established program of research and scholarship related to developmental disabilities, health, special education, or a related field.
Knowledge of disability-related services and service-delivery systems and the ability to contribute to the development and expansion of culturally responsive clinical and/or community-based services.
Demonstrated interdisciplinary and collaborative leadership experience.
Desirable Qualifications
Demonstrated ability to develop and/or secure competitive federal grants or other extramural awards.
Demonstrated ability to develop or lead clinical or community-based services.
Expertise in implementation science and/or community-engaged research.
Expertise in training and workforce development.
To Apply: Click on the “Apply” button on the top right corner of the screen to complete an application and attach required documents to the online application. The applicants should submit the following documents:
Cover letter indicating how you satisfy the minimum and desirable qualifications
Curriculum vitae
Names and contact information (including e-mail address) of at least 5 professional references
Official transcripts (copies are acceptable with application; official transcripts are required upon hire)
Summaries of student evaluations of higher education courses taught previously
1-3 reprints of selected scholarly publications.
Late, incomplete, or unreadable application materials will not be considered. Please REDACT references to social security numbers and birth date on submitted documents. All items become the property of the University of Hawaii and will not be returned.
NOTE: If you have not applied for a position before using NEOGOV, you will need to create an account. The maximum file size to upload/attach is 10 MB. If the attachment is larger than 10 MB, please split the file and upload it as a supplemental attachment.
Inquiries: Meghan Miller at meghan.miller@hawaii.edu or 808-956-0891, or Lisa Eng at lctam@hawaii.edu or 808-956-5850.
EEO, Clery Act, ADA
The University of Hawai'i is an Equal Opportunity Institution and is committed to a policy of nondiscrimination in employment, including on the basis of veteran and disability status. For more information, visit: https://www.hawaii.edu/offices/eeo/policies/

Accommodation Request: The University of Hawai'i complies with the provisions of the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). jobs.title: Associate Professor, Endowed Chair in Community Practice
jobs.description:
Job Details
Johns Hopkins, founded in 1876, is America's first research
university and home to nine world-class academic divisions working
together as one university.
Salary : $123,002 - $179,905
Johns Hopkins University: School of Education
Description
The Johns Hopkins University School of Education seeks candidates
for a tenure-eligible Associate Professor in Community
Practice , with an emphasis in Early Childhood Education
(through grade 3). The position is intended to advance the
translation of scientific, evidence-based methods into practice for
teachers and community practitioners, with the goal of improving
the quality of education for all students. The successful candidate
will bring an established research program and a demonstrated
record of leadership to this work, along with a sustained scholarly
commitment to early childhood as a foundational period of human
development. This position offers the opportunity to shape graduate
education and lead partnerships that connect research to real-world
practice in early learning, underserved, and urban communities
across diverse local, national, and global contexts. Qualified
candidates will be considered for eligibility for a new endowed
chair, called the William and Sylvia Cohen Associate Professor in
Community Practice.
Responsibilities:
CURRICULUM AND TEACHING
Evaluate, develop, and deliver curricula for JHU School of
Education degree programs that translate advances in learning,
technology, and instruction science into practice accessible to
pre- and in-service teachers and community practitioners.
Mentor master's and doctoral degree candidates to deepen their
understanding of early childhood as the critical period shaping a
child's physical, intellectual, emotional, and social development,
as well as language acquisition, and provide senior guidance on
dissertation research in this area.
Engage in service to the department, school, and profession
appropriate to rank.
Research and Evidence Building
Strengthen the evidence base on what makes educational programs
and initiatives effective, with particular attention to early
learners and underserved and urban populations.
Collaborate with, and where appropriate lead, experts in
teaching and learning, brain and language development, and child
development across Johns Hopkins University with a specific
interest in early childhood development.
Collaborate with faculty across units and centers on
interdisciplinary research and grant activity.
Hold a secondary affiliation with one or more of the School of
Education’s five Research Centers
: https://education.jhu.edu/faculty-research/centers-institutes/
Community and Partnership Engagement
Build and sustain partnerships with schools and communities
that bridge the gap between cutting-edge research and everyday
practice, working toward improved educational outcomes for
students.
Work directly with community stakeholders to design and
implement practical programs and technologies that support student
performance and long-term outcomes and help secure the funding and
institutional support these partnerships require.
Qualifications
REQUIRED:
Doctorate (Ph.D. or Ed.D.) in Early Childhood Education,
Developmental Psychology, Educational Psychology, Special
Education, Curriculum and Instruction, or a closely related
field.
An established, externally recognized research record in early
childhood development, learning science, or evidence-based
instructional practice, with a sustained publication history in
peer-reviewed venues.
A record of successful university-level teaching and curriculum
development, typically including prior experience at the rank of
Assistant Professor or equivalent. We are willing to consider
candidates currently at the advanced Asistant Professor level who
would be eligible for hire at the Associate Professor level.
A demonstrated record of securing external funding to support
research and program development.
Ability to translate research findings for practitioner and
community audiences.
PREFERRED:
Experience designing or validating assessment instruments
related to learning readiness or developmental outcomes.
A sustained track record of partnership work with schools,
districts, or community organizations, particularly in urban or
underserved settings.
A demonstrated record of mentoring graduate or doctoral
students to successful completion, including dissertation
chairing.
Interdisciplinary leadership experience, particularly with
researchers in language development, human development, or public
health.
Evidence of service and leadership within professional
organizations or editorial boards.
The expected base pay salary range for this position is $123,002 -
$179,905.
Application Instructions
Review of applications will begin December 3, 2026.
Applicants are required to provide:
Curriculum Vitae
A Research and Teaching Statement (in a single document)
describing your interest and qualifications for the position,
including information that describes relevant experiences (include
evidence of effective teaching as available) and understanding of
the School's mission, vision, and values.
Three names of references who can attest to your qualifications
for the position. We will only contact references for
finalists.
Equal Employment Opportunity Statement
Salary Range
The referenced salary range represents the minimum and maximum
salaries for this position and is based on Johns Hopkins
University's good faith belief at the time of posting. Not all
candidates will be eligible for the upper end of the salary range.
The actual compensation offered to the selected candidate may vary
and will ultimately depend on multiple factors, which may include
the successful candidate's geographic location, skills, work
experience, internal equity, market conditions, education/training
and other factors, as reasonably determined by the
University.
Total Rewards
Johns Hopkins offers a total rewards package that supports our
employees' health, life, career and retirement. More information
can be found here: https://hr.jhu.edu/benefits-worklife/
.
Equal Opportunity Employer
The Johns Hopkins University is committed to equal opportunity for
its faculty, staff, and students. To that end, the university does
not discriminate on the basis of sex, gender, marital status,
pregnancy, race, color, ethnicity, national origin, age,
disability, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity or
expression, veteran status or other legally protected
characteristics. The University is committed to providing qualified
individuals access to all academic and employment programs,
benefits and activities on the basis of demonstrated ability,
performance and merit without regard to personal factors or
demographic characteristics that are irrelevant to the program
involved.
Pre-Employment Information
If you are interested in applying for employment with Johns Hopkins
University and require special assistance or accommodation during
any part of the pre-employment process, please contact the HR
Business Services Office at jhurecruitment@jhu.edu . For
TTY users, call via Maryland Relay or dial 711. For more
information about workplace accommodations at Johns Hopkins
University for disabilities, medical conditions (including medical
conditions related to pregnancy or childbirth), accessibility, or
religious reasons, please visit accessibility.jhu.edu .
Background Checks
After receiving a conditional offer, the successful candidate(s)
for this position will be subject to a pre-employment background
check including education verification. When deciding whether a
candidate’s conviction history is job-disqualifying, the University
considers the nature and gravity of the offense, the time that has
passed since the conviction, and the nature of the job being
sought.
EEO is the Law
https://www.eeoc.gov/employees-job-applicants
Vaccine Requirements
Johns Hopkins University strongly encourages, but no longer
requires, at least one dose of the COVID-19 vaccine. This change
does not apply to the School of Medicine (SOM). SOM hires must be
fully vaccinated with an FDA COVID-19 vaccination and provide proof
of vaccination status. We still require all faculty, staff, and
students to receive the seasonal
flu vaccine .
Exceptions to the seasonal flu vaccine or COVID-19 vaccine (for
SOM) requirement(s) may be provided to individuals with sincerely
held religious beliefs or medical conditions that preclude them
from receiving the vaccine. Requests for an exception must be
submitted to the JHU vaccination registry. For additional
information, applicants for SOM positions should visit https://www.hopkinsmedicine.org/coronavirus/covid-19-vaccine/
and all other JHU applicants should visit
https://covidinfo.jhu.edu/health-safety/covid-vaccination-information/
.
The following additional vaccine requirements may apply,
depending upon your campus. Please contact the hiring department
for more information.
The pre-employment physical for positions in clinical areas,
laboratories, working with research subjects, or involving
community contact requires documentation of immune status against
Rubella (German measles), Rubeola (Measles), Mumps, Varicella
(chickenpox), Hepatitis B and documentation of having received the
Tdap (Tetanus, diphtheria, pertussis) vaccination. This may include
documentation of having two (2) MMR vaccines; two (2) Varicella
vaccines; or antibody status to these diseases from laboratory
testing. Blood tests for immunities to these diseases are
ordinarily included in the pre-employment physical exam except for
those candidates who provide results of blood tests or immunization
documentation from their own health care providers. Any
vaccinations required for these diseases will be given at no cost
in our Occupational Health office.

jobs.title: Research Assistant Professor, Research Associate Professor and Research Professor in Cyber Security
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Description
Based on the foundation of the Ted and Karyn Hume Center for
National Security and Technology, Virginia Tech launched the
Virginia Tech National Security Institute (VTNSI) in September
2021. With a presence in Blacksburg and the Washington, D.C., metro
area, the institute aspires to be the nation's preeminent academic
organization at the nexus of interdisciplinary research,
technology, policy, and talent development, the national security
institute will advance national security in pursuit of a secure
America.
Motivated applicants are sought to join VTNSI as Research Assistant
Professor, Research Associate Professor, or Research Professor in
Cyber Security to support rapid growth in our body of programs in
cyber security, cyber analytics, and cyber operations. Rank will be
determined based upon experience and credentials. This position
serves as a research staff member of the Hume Center and in the
Intelligent Systems Division (ISD). ISD hosts a range of dynamic
research projects, and the successful applicant will have the
ability to contribute to these programs, lead the development of
new programs, and mentor students engaged in these programs. ISD is
a leader in research and development in three core capabilities: 1)
AI Applications, 2) AI Assurance, and 3) AI and Digitial
Engineering.
Specific responsibilities include the following: (1) support the
execution of university sponsored programs by conducting research
and development; (2) author technical documents and publish
peer-reviewed academic papers; (3) support the development of new
funded research programs by participating on proposal teams and
supporting the business development activities of VTNSI; (4)
support the development and growth of the future national security
workforce through student mentoring and advisement, and workforce
training and education.
We are seeking individuals with expertise in cyber security, cyber
operations, artificial intelligence, machine learning, data
science. Successful applicants will have experience applying these
methods to complex organization and/or system technologies.
Required Qualifications
- Given the nature of the research conducted and requirement from
the federal sponsor, candidates must be a U.S. Citizen.
- Active security clearance with the ability to maintain the
clearance.
- An earned Doctorate degree in Computer Science, Computer
Engineering, Systems Engineering, Mathematics, Statistics,
Psychology, or a related field.
- Experience with cyber security and cyber operations (including
software, AI/ML, or autonomy).
- Evidence of high potential for excellence in research and
development as demonstrated through academic study or
experience.
- Scholarship and funding credentials that support the rank of
either research assistant professor, research associate professor,
or research professor.
- Demonstrated mastery of ones’ field of study through publication
of relevant research in peer-reviewed academic venues appropriate
to the discipline.
- Proficiency with the tools germane to field of research.
- Demonstrated ability to work as a member of a team in executing
upon research projects.
Preferred Qualifications
- Active TS/SCI security clearance.
- Proficiency in cyber security and cyber test (including software,
AI/ML, or autonomy), network and penetration testing, malware
analysis, or red teaming.
- Experience with cryptography or software reverse
engineering.
- Proficiency in testing AI-enabled systems (including
benchmarking, prompting, narratives, AI use in human workflows) and
agentic AI (including assessing behavior and security, autonomous
use of AI).
- Experience in policy, risk assessment, or risk management
frameworks (RMF) for systems testing.
- Experience writing grant and contract proposals.
- Experience serving as principal investigator on research grants
and contracts.
- Interest and/or experience in working effectively with a diverse
faculty, staff and student population.
- Experience conducting research programs supporting defense and
intelligence sponsors.
Overtime Status
Exempt: Not eligible for overtime
Appointment Type
Restricted
Salary Information
$150,000 - $260,000, commensurate with experience and rank at
hire
Research Assistant Professor $150-$180k
Research Associate Professor $180-$220k
Research Professor $220-$260k
Hours per week
40
Review Date
November 30, 2026
Additional Information
Positions will be located in the Virginia Tech Research Center in
Arlington, VA. Due to the nature of our work, the successful
candidates must be US citizens with an active security
clearance.
The successful candidate will be required to have a criminal
conviction check.
About Virginia Tech
Dedicated to its motto, Ut Prosim (That I May Serve),
Virginia Tech pushes the boundaries of knowledge by taking a
hands-on, transdisciplinary approach to preparing scholars to be
leaders and problem-solvers. A comprehensive land-grant institution
that enhances the quality of life in Virginia and throughout the
world, Virginia Tech is an
inclusive community dedicated to knowledge, discovery, and
creativity. The university offers more than 280 majors to a diverse
enrollment of more than 36,000 undergraduate, graduate, and
professional students in eight
undergraduate colleges , a
school of medicine , a
veterinary medicine college,
Graduate School , and
Honors College . The university has a significant presence
across Virginia, including Blacksburg, the greater Washington, D.C.
area, the Health Sciences and Technology Campus in Roanoke, sites
in Newport News and Richmond, and numerous
Extension offices and
research institutes . A leading global research institution,
Virginia Tech conducts more than $650 million in research
annually.
Virginia Tech endorses and encourages participation in professional
development opportunities and university shared governance . These valuable
contributions to university shared governance provide important
representation and perspective, along with opportunities for unique
and impactful professional development.
Virginia Tech does not discriminate against employees, students, or
applicants on the basis of age, color, disability, sex (including
pregnancy), gender, gender identity, gender expression, genetic
information, ethnicity or national origin, political affiliation,
race, religion, sexual orientation, or military status, or
otherwise discriminate against employees or applicants who inquire
about, discuss, or disclose their compensation or the compensation
of other employees or applicants, or on any other basis protected
by law.
If you are an individual with a disability and desire an
accommodation, please contact Alex Tuuri at
alext3@vt.edu during regular business hours at least 10
business days prior to the event.

jobs.title: Assistant/Associate Professor in Poultry Nutrition and Health
jobs.description:
Job Details
Job Description
This is a tenure-track position at the Assistant/Associate
Professor rank with an initial appointment of 60% research and 40%
extension in the School of Animal Sciences. We are seeking a
dynamic individual with a commitment to establish, fund, and
maintain a vigorous research and extension program that creates
knowledge for our poultry producers in Virginia and nationwide.
Areas of interest include, but are not restricted to, growth
biology, metabolic basis of nutrient absorption and utilization,

jobs.description:
The School of Public Policy at the University of Maryland, College Park seeks to appoint a tenure-track Assistant Professor in Science and Technology Policy, starting in Fall 2027. The successful candidate will strengthen the School’s research and teaching capacity at the intersection of science, technology, and public policy and contribute to the continued development of science and technology policy as a strategic area of focus for the School.
We seek candidates with an ambitious research agenda focused on how public policy shapes the development, deployment, and governance of science and technology and how scientific and technological change affects international relations, governments, markets, institutions, risk management and society. Areas of interest may include, but are not limited to, science and innovation policy; research and development policy; semiconductor and industrial policy; standards and regulation; emerging technology governance; cybersecurity; biotechnology; space policy; quantum technologies; international, national, and homeland security; energy and climate technologies; international competition and cooperation in science and technology; and the institutions and processes through which scientific and technical expertise informs policymaking.
Candidates should demonstrate the potential to develop a strong record of high-quality scholarly research, effective teaching, policy and public engagement, and institutional service. The successful candidate will have the potential to develop a nationally recognized, externally funded research program; teach in the School’s undergraduate and graduate programs, including the development of foundational courses in science and technology policy as well as advanced courses in their areas of expertise; and contribute to collaborations across the School and the University, such as the School’s Center for Governance of Technology and Systems, the Global Policy Institute, the Center for Global Sustainability, Center for International and Security Studies at Maryland, the Do Good Institute, and other units across UMD, including the Artificial Intelligence Interdisciplinary Institute at Maryland (AIM).

jobs.title: Open Rank Faculty Position Future of Work and Emerging Technologies
jobs.description:
The University of South Florida (USF), a member of the Association of American Universities (AAU), invites applications for an open-rank (Assistant, Associate, or Full Professor) faculty position to lead and expand a strategic research area focused on the Future of Work and Emerging Technologies.
USF seeks a nationally and internationally recognized or rising scholar whose work is reshaping how individuals, organizations, educational institutions, and communities prepare for and thrive in a workforce transformed by artificial intelligence and technological innovation.
This position represents a significant institutional investment intended to establish a nationally and internationally visible, externally funded research enterprise focused on the future of learning, work, emerging technologies, economic opportunity, and workforce development. Particular interest will be given to candidates with a demonstrated record of securing competitive external funding and leading impactful research programs. Candidates with experience serving as Principal Investigator on federal grants are especially encouraged to apply. The successful candidate will build a productive research program while creating opportunities for colleagues and students to develop their scholarship and compete for external funding.
Position Overview
Artificial intelligence, automation, digital transformation, and emerging technologies are rapidly changing the nature of work and learning. The successful candidate will play a leadership role in building an innovative and forward-looking research agenda that examines how educational systems, workforce development organizations, employers, and policymakers can prepare individuals for evolving careers while promoting economic mobility and expanding access to opportunity.
Relevant areas of scholarship may include, but are not limited to:
Future of work
Artificial intelligence and workforce transformation
Human-AI collaboration
Workforce development and workforce policy
Career pathways and talent development
Credentials, microcredentials, and alternative pathways
Skills acquisition, reskilling, and upskilling
Adult learning and lifelong learning
Experiential and work-based learning
Community college and workforce partnerships
Industry-education collaborations
Labor market analytics and workforce alignment
Technology-enabled learning and training systems
Economic mobility and workforce success
Emerging technologies and human capital development
Candidates may come from a wide range of disciplines, including education, workforce development, labor economics, information science, learning sciences, human resource development, human-computer interaction, computer science, engineering, or related fields.
Expectations
The successful candidate will:
Develop and sustain a nationally and internationally prominent research program.
Secure substantial competitive external funding from federal agencies, foundations, industry, and other sponsors.
Serve as Principal Investigator and provide leadership for externally funded research initiatives.
Pursue large-scale interdisciplinary and collaborative research initiatives within USF and with external partners.
Publish influential scholarship in leading peer-reviewed journals and other high-impact scholarly outlets.
Teach graduate level courses.
Mentor graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, and/or early-career scholars and contribute to the development of the next generation of researchers and scholars.
Build productive partnerships with workforce organizations, employers, educational institutions, policymakers, and other external partners.
Collaborate broadly across the University and with external partners.
Help establish USF as a national and international leader in workforce innovation, technology, and economic mobility research.
Particular emphasis will be placed on a candidate's ability and potential to attract major investments through programs supported by agencies and organizations such as:
National Science Foundation (NSF)
Institute of Education Sciences (IES)
U.S. Department of Labor
Department of Commerce
Department of Defense
National Institutes of Health
Major national and regional foundations
Industry-sponsored research partnerships
Required Qualifications
Earned doctoral degree in appropriate discipline.
Demonstrated record of strong publication in high-quality scholarly venues related to work and learning, workforce development, emerging technologies, economic opportunity, or area relevant to the future of work and emerging technologies that is consistent with appointment at a research-intensive university.
Documented record of successfully securing competitive external funding or strong potential, appropriate to career stage.
Demonstrated capacity to work effectively in interdisciplinary environments.
Candidates seeking appointment at the Associate Professor or Professor level must demonstrate sustained scholarly productivity, substantive leadership on externally funded research, and national or international recognition commensurate with the proposed rank. Appointment rank and tenure status will be determined in accordance with University policies and the approved position authorization.
Preferred Qualifications
Preference will be given to candidates who demonstrate:
Sustained success obtaining significant competitive external funding as Principal Investigator or equivalent research leader.
National or international recognition for research excellence.
Experience leading interdisciplinary research centers, laboratories, institutes, or large collaborative projects.
Success building partnerships with industry, government agencies, educational systems, workforce organizations, or community partners.
Experience translating research into policy, practice, products, or measurable societal impact.
Evidence of, or commitment to effective teaching and mentoring of graduate students, postdoctoral fellows, and/or early career scholars.
A compelling vision for building a high-impact Future of Work and Emerging Technologies research enterprise at USF.
Strategic Opportunity
USF is seeking more than a faculty member. We seek an entrepreneurial research leader who can shape a signature area of excellence at a major AAU institution. The successful candidate will have the opportunity to build collaborative initiatives across education, business, engineering, computer science, public policy, health, and other disciplines while developing a nationally recognized center of scholarship focused on the future of learning, work, emerging technologies, and economic mobility.
Application Instructions
Review of applications will begin on November 12, 2026 and continue until the position is filled. To ensure full consideration, candidates are encouraged to apply by November 12, 2026. Applications should be submitted through https://jobs.usf.edu/hcmUI/CandidateExperience/en/sites/USF/. Please specify Position # 330147242 on all submitted documents and include the following materials:
1. Cover letter that describes candidate’s interest in the position and specifically addresses how the candidate’s background, accomplishments, and future plans align with the required qualifications and preferred qualifications.
2. Full curriculum vitae.

We are dedicated to cultivating a talented, engaged and driven workforce that strives to be bold. Employees excel in USF‘s rich academic environment, which fosters their development and advancement. In 2025, Forbes recognized USF as one of Florida’s best large employers, ranked No. 1 among the state’s 12 public universities. Our first-class benefits package includes medical, dental and life insurance plans, retirement plan options, employee and dependent tuition programs, generous leave, and hundreds of employee perks and discounts.

The University of South Florida is a top-ranked research university serving approximately 50,000 students from across the globe at campuses in Tampa, St. Petersburg, Sarasota-Manatee and USF Health. USF is recognized by U.S. News & World Report as a top 50 public university and the best value in Florida. jobs.title: ASSISTANT/ ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR IN KINESIOLOGY- HEALTH AND EXERCISE SCIENCE
jobs.description:
ASSISTANT/ ASSOCIATE PROFESSOR IN KINESIOLOGY- HEALTH AND EXERCISE SCIENCE
The Ohio State University
Columbus, OH
The Department of Human Sciences in the College of Education and Human Ecology at The Ohio State University invites applications for a full-time (9-month) assistant/associate professor tenure-track position in the Health and Exercise Science program. The Health and Exercise Science program within Kinesiology is consistently ranked among the top programs in the country based on its innovative research activity and vibrant curriculum making it a preeminent place for the professional development of students and faculty.
The goal of this search is to add a promising scholar to an internationally renowned team of faculty whose research interests focus on areas relevant to optimizing the human condition, including the application of behavioral science to exercise interventions impacting cardiovascular disease, cancer, aging, obesity, diabetes and other chronic diseases. We seek a candidate with distinct and recognized expertise in social and behavioral aspects of physical activity that includes an ongoing research agenda that aligns with major extramural funding opportunities from federal sources (e.g., NIH, CDC, and HHS). We seek candidates with an excellent record of scholarship, teaching and service relative to the assistant/associate professor rank and commensurate with a research-intensive university. For candidates at the associate professor rank, they must have achievements qualifying them for tenure at a major R1 institution with strong preference for those with a track record of securing competitive extramural funding and recognized leadership in a focal area of scholarship. Preference will be granted to candidates who are able to integrate basic and/or applied science discoveries into behavioral interventions that improve health, teaching, and service agendas, and who offer evidence of sustained impact. Our current faculty have access to state-of-the-art laboratory facilities and strong ongoing research collaborations with physicians and scientists within the Wexner Medical Center and the James Cancer Center as well as Psychology, Nursing, Engineering, and Sports Medicine. Our program also has numerous collaborations with external academic and research institutions and industry.
Performance Objectives
- Develop independent / extramurally funded research focused on behavioral aspects of exercise science.
- Contribute to a collaborative research team within exercise science, the department, college and university.
- Effectively teach undergraduate and graduate courses and engage in curriculum development to advance undergraduate and graduate education.
- Mentor graduate and undergraduate students to advance scholarship and career-readiness.
- Engage in academic service to advance the missions of the Health and Exercise Science Program, the Department and College. undefined
- Experience/ willingness to pursue American College of Sports Medicine accreditation preferred.
Education and Experience Requirements
Candidates must have a PhD in Kinesiology, Exercise Science, Psychology, Public Health or closely related field; demonstrated research productivity and evidence of an independently funded research program; demonstrated teaching competency. Post-doctoral training is valued but is not necessary. Ohio State strives to become a global leader in AI-driven discovery (https://go.osu.edu/ai-initiative) and promote AI fluency for human thriving. Thus, a desired qualification is experience with the use of AI to forward research and teaching agendas in the field of Health and Exercise Science.
How to Apply
For application instructions and a list of required materials, visit:
https://osu.wd1.myworkdayjobs.com/en-US/OSUCareers/job/ASSISTANT--ASSOCIATE-PROFESSOR-IN-KINESIOLOGY--HEALTH-AND-EXERCISE-SCIENCE_R160934-2
The university is an equal opportunity employer, including veterans and disability.

jobs.title: Open Rank Tenure Track Faculty (Assistant/Associate/Full Professor)
jobs.description:
The University of Illinois Chicago is a vibrant and leading public R1 institution in the heart of Chicago. The Division of Environmental and Occupational Health seeks applications for a faculty position to begin Fall 2027:
Open Rank Tenure Track Faculty (Assistant/Associate/Full Professor) - Two positions
Description:
The University of Illinois Chicago (UIC) School of Public Health (SPH) Division of Environmental and Occupational Health Sciences (EOHS) announces a search for two tenure-track faculty members at a rank commensurate with experience. The Division of Environmental and Occupational Health Sciences is one of four Divisions within the UIC SPH, the only accredited school of public health in the state of Illinois. It is a leading research department within the school.
Applicants at all levels should demonstrate research achievements in environmental and / or occupational health and the ability to advance the Division’s teaching mission. The ideal candidates will have experience obtaining research grant funding as a PI/Co-PI, success in teaching and mentoring graduate students, and a record of successful collaborations. A strong scientific background in environmental and occupational health sciences or a related discipline is required. We are particularly interested in research and teaching experience in the areas of exposure science, industrial hygiene, occupational safety, farmworker health, the impacts of extreme weather on health, as well as air and water quality. Other desirable assets include strong communications, team building; experience teaching graduate students online, and evidence of successful mentorship.
This position is a 9-month salaried appointment with opportunities for summer research support. The budgeted salary range for the position is $95,000 - $200,000. The pay offered to the selected candidate will be determined based on factors including (but not limited to) the experience and qualifications of the selected candidate including equivalent years in rank, training, and field or discipline; internal equity; and external market pay for comparable jobs.
This position is intended to be eligible for benefits. This includes Health, Dental, Vision, Life Insurance, a Retirement Plan, Paid time Off, and Tuition waivers for employees and dependents.
Candidates must have:
A doctoral degree (or equivalent) in engineering, environmental science, epidemiology, industrial hygiene, occupational health, public health or a closely related field.
Peer-reviewed research publications and evidence of capacity to secure funding in the fields of occupational and /or environmental health sciences, appropriate for years of experience and job expectations.
Experience teaching and mentoring graduate students.
Interest in collaborative and multidisciplinary research.
The EOHS division has a dynamic, multi-disciplinary and impactful portfolio of research and service that reflect our values of community engagement and the promotion of environmental and occupational health. Many opportunities exist at UIC for research collaboration with faculty in the fields of occupational safety, epidemiology, occupational medicine, community health, environmental health, and health policy. The EOHS division serves about 80 students in MPH, MS and PhD programs, with eight tenure-system faculty, and twice that number of research and clinical faculty. Within the EOHS division, the NIOSH-funded Illinois Education and Research Center (ERC) supports training, research, outreach and continuing education in a variety of occupational health disciplines; the NIOSH-funded Center for Healthy Work, which is using innovative engaged research methods to examine precarious work and its impacts on health; and the Great Lakes Center for Farmworker Health and Wellbeing which conducts research to improve working conditions, fair and equitable wages, social protections, and access to healthcare for farmworkers. The NIH-funded Center for Extreme Conditions and Health Excellence supports interdisciplinary research and community engagement addressing extreme weather and health including flooding and nature-based solutions. Other active areas of research include water quality and ambient air quality.
UIC is one of the most diverse research-intensive universities in the United States, and is designated as a Minority Serving Institution, an Asian American and Native American Pacific Islander-Serving Institute, and a Hispanic Serving Institution. The EOHS division is committed to ensuring access to graduate education for students who are diverse across multiple dimensions, including: race, ethnicity, gender, age, disability, disadvantages socioeconomic status, ideas and perspectives. We seek applicants that will enrich and contribute to the diversity of the EOHS division and help us expand the perspectives and experiences we bring to our work.
Application Process:
Applicants must submit an on-line application using the link provided below. Please upload a cover letter describing relevant experience and goals, teaching statement, curriculum vitae, and contact information for three references. For fullest consideration, all requested information must be submitted by January 1, 2027.
Questions: Email Samuel Dorevitch, MD, MPH, Search Committee Chair at sdorevit@uic.edu
Only online applications will be considered. Apply at uic.csod.com/ux/ats/careersite/1/home/requisition/21152?c=uic by January 1, 2027.
